w: Runs each user turn as a loop: call the model, run the tool calls it returns, feed results back, and repeat until the model stops, streaming every step.
Runs each turn as an explicit, re-entrant state machine or operation pipeline over persisted state so a rebuilt run reaches the same decisions.

f: Event-sourced agent loop with typed immutable events
w: All conversation activity is a frozen typed event (message, action, observation, condensation); each step reads a view of the event log and appends new events.

f: Agent loop built as workflow steps
w: The model/tool iteration loop is itself a workflow of steps, so it inherits workflow suspend, resume and tracing.

f: Processor and middleware pipeline around the loop
w: Input, step and output processors (or an ordered middleware stack) hook every model call and stream so guardrails and features plug in without touching the loop.
A workflow can be registered as a processor for multi-step guardrail pipelines.
A processor can abort a request and optionally ask the agent to retry with a reason.
A global cap on processor-requested retries backstops processors that always ask to retry.
The agent loop runs as a durable workflow with persisted checkpoints so paused, approval-waiting or crashed runs resume without replaying finished work.
Drives the durable loop through pub/sub events so steps run on separate workers.
The agent loop is published as a standalone library or factory that other hosts embed with their own model, tools and features.
Compiles the agent loop for wasm so it can run in a browser host.
Runs for the same session are serialized in arrival order while other sessions run concurrently, with global and per-lane caps.
Only one process at a time may load, run and flush a shared session.
Force-aborts turns that wedge silently mid-flight.
Each agent or turn resolves which runtime owns the model loop (built-in or an external harness) through a driver registry.
Chooses an in-process, hub-backed or remote runtime host behind one interface.
Routes chats to external agent platforms (Dify, Coze, n8n, DashScope, DeerFlow) instead of the built-in loop, discovered as plugins.
Runs agents on the Claude Agent SDK (Claude Code) with a process manager, warm query pool and AGENTS.md loading.
Runs agents on the Pi SDK with model injection, MCP tool adapter and approvals.
Runs agents on the DSH runtime via a bridge server.
Delegates turns to the official Codex app-server so Codex owns thread resume and native tools, with the host's tools bridged over MCP.
Runs agent turns through the GitHub Copilot SDK, bridging tools, permissions and hooks.
Replaces the built-in harness with the cloud-hosted Agents API.
Registers an AI SDK ToolLoopAgent as a native agent.
Runs models from different AI SDK majors in the same loop.

f: Native LLM runtime with AI SDK fallback
w: Routes through an in-house LLM runtime when supported, else the AI SDK.
One transport per API mode (Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic Messages, Bedrock) behind a common interface.

f: Responses WebSocket transport with HTTP fallback
w: Prefers a cached, prewarmed Responses WebSocket per turn and falls back to HTTP.
zstd-compresses request bodies.
Agent activity is exposed as an async stream of typed events for any client.
Runs an agent turn non-interactively from the command line or an API trigger, without sessions or a UI.
Emits every headless event as a timestamped JSON line through one writer.
Messages sent while the agent works are injected into the live run at the next model or tool boundary instead of waiting for the turn to end.
Messages typed during a run are queued durably, shown as editable items, and sent in order when the run finishes; nothing queued is lost.
A setting chooses what a new message does during a run: steer into it, queue as follow-up, collect, or interrupt.
Carries current agent state (tasks, goals) as a superseding cache-aware snapshot.
When a background shell, sub-agent or monitor finishes, a notification is queued into the conversation and the agent resumes.
Eligible tool calls run detached: the model gets a handle immediately and the real result arrives later.
Polls a script on an interval until it matches, then reports to the agent.
Stop or Esc cancels the running model call and in-flight tools through a turn-scoped abort signal, keeping partial output and recording the interruption.
Pause stops the loop after the current step and resume continues from there.
One switch pauses cron, dispatch and new runs until resumed.
Propagates per-turn stream callbacks and cancellation through model and action code without threading arguments.
Caps model iterations per run (shared between parent and sub-agents) and asks the user to continue when used up; the limit is visible and changeable.
Annotates results at 80/90/95% of the step budget and injects a force-finish summary instruction so the run wraps up cleanly.
Sums token usage across calls and enforces soft-warning and hard limits per run or session, including shared budgets across sub-agents.
Reads a '+500k' style directive from the user's message and tracks the turn's spend against it.
Per-step, per-model-call, per-action and whole-run timeouts with model-specific defaults abort hung work.

f: Session goals: keep working until a condition is met
w: /goal attaches a completion condition to the session; after each turn a judge model decides whether it is met and, if not, the agent keeps going.
Before accepting 'done', a verifier judges declared acceptance checks against the actual evidence and reports failures instead of trusting the agent's own claim.
If the agent tries to finish right after editing code without fresh verification, it is sent back to verify.
A critic scores the result and, below a threshold, sends the agent back with feedback.
When a claimed file edit did not land, the model and user get a verification footer; turns that end oddly get an explanation.
The model ends a task by calling a finish/submit/status tool (completed or needs help), which drives task completion.
After a reply without tool calls, a fast model decides whether the agent should continue or hand back to the user.
When the model says it will do something but stops without a tool call, or a tool call is dropped, it is re-prompted.
Re-runs a task when shell success checks fail, running failure hooks and respecting the attempt bound.
Tracks identical tool calls (name and arguments) over a sliding window, warns and then hard-stops when the agent repeats itself; ships on.
When a loop is detected the user is asked whether to keep or disable loop detection for the session.
Detects repeated action/observation pairs, repeated errors, monologues and tool stagnation from structured signals.
Cheap checks stop a reply dominated by a repeated fragment.
Aborts the run if the model repeats identical calls right after an auto-compaction.
Counts consecutive mistakes or errors, appends recovery notices, makes one final recovery call and stops the run at the cap.
Retries rate limits, 5xx and network errors with jittered exponential backoff that honours Retry-After and quota-reset hints.
Retries streams that produced no output or broke mid-stream on transient socket errors.

f: LLM circuit breaker and process-wide limiter
w: Caps in-flight model calls across the process and trips a circuit breaker on repeated failures.

f: Provider error classification with recovery hints
w: Maps any provider exception or HTTP status to a typed error (auth, billing, rate limit, context length, overload) with a recovery hint.
Failed turns carry a typed reason and are shown with a plain-language explanation; provider error payloads are summarised and redacted.
After a context or output-length error, reports approximate token counts versus the model's limits.
On errors before streaming or empty output, switches to the next configured model or account instead of failing.
After retries and fallbacks are exhausted, keeps waiting and retrying within a bound.
When a model call fails, one-shot handlers repair the request (strip unsupported params, fix a trailing assistant prefill) and retry.
Shrinks and retries images rejected as too large; drops undecodable ones.
When the model returns no visible text, tries partial-stream recovery and a nudge, then surfaces a visible error instead of an empty answer.
Detects safety terminations across providers, does not blindly retry, injects bounded recovery guidance and tells the user to rephrase when needed.
When a reply hits the output-token limit, asks the model to continue (or uses assistant prefill) and stitches the parts.
When output was cut at the token cap, truncated tool calls are not executed and the model is told why.

f: Output token clamp to remaining context
w: Clamps max output tokens to the remaining context window, with a stream chunk timeout.
Detects streams that go silent or drip forever, kills and retries them, with longer floors for reasoning models.
Generation runs as a server-side job; a client that drops reattaches and replays the in-flight stream.
Records which edge served a dead stream and how much arrived.
After a silent stretch, a neutral status line says which phase is waiting.
Reads failed responses' error bodies with size and time bounds.
Skips client-side request re-walks for huge payloads.
Repairs malformed tool calls (bad JSON, control characters, mis-cased or legacy names) or feeds a corrective retry.
Validates model output with checker functions or a schema and rerolls with feedback when it fails.
Detects tool calls a model wrote as plain text (XML, Harmony markers, bare JSON) and either converts them or refuses to accept them as an answer.
Calls to missing tools or with invalid arguments become explicit errors the model can recover from, with hints such as a matching skill.

f: Tool exceptions returned as error results
w: Exceptions inside tools are caught and returned to the model as structured error results.
Ends the turn when an unrecoverable error remains instead of looping.
Before each model call, inserts placeholders for unanswered tool calls and drops orphaned tool results so providers never reject the history; ships on.
Enforces tool-call/result pairing and batch atomicity and computes safe cut points for summarising or trimming.
Sends deliberately broken histories to providers to pin down what each one rejects.
Rewrites stored history a provider would reject (tool-call id formats, role order, multiple system messages, bad characters).
Keeps each function call's thought signature and sends it back (synthetic only if lost), with call ids on function responses.
Rewrites a past tool call's arguments consistently across provider surfaces.
Switching model mid-thread injects instructions so the new model understands inherited context.
When the conversation nears the model's window, older turns are summarised by the model into a checkpoint while the head, the current request and recent turns are kept; ships on.
The summary is a structured, most-important-first state snapshot (decisions, constraints, open work) rather than free prose.
/compact (or /compress, /smol, /newtask) summarises on demand, with optional focus text, keep-last-N, preview and cancel, and reports the savings.
Old tool outputs beyond the newest tokens are cleared or masked to placeholders first, with no model call; summarising runs only if that is not enough.
Recognises provider context-overflow errors from a pattern table, compacts once and retries instead of failing.
If summarising itself overflows, retry with progressively less context (dropping the oldest items) before a hard reset.
A cooldown stops compress-retry loops after repeated failures, a stalled summary retries on a fallback model, and a deterministic summary is the last resort.
Uses the provider's server-side compaction where available and persists its replacement history.
Compacts sessions in the background after an idle gap so the next turn does not pay for it.
Folds older exchanges one at a time into a rolling summary.

f: Compaction thresholds per model and profile
w: The auto-compaction trigger is set as a percentage of the window, globally or per model/profile, with a floor for small models.
Choose agentic (model summary), basic (no model) or off, per run or globally.
Replace the summarisation prompt with your own text or file.
Condensing summarises earlier messages into a fresh start but keeps the originals so they can be restored.
If summarising is off or fails, the oldest messages are dropped or hidden behind a marker to fit the window.
On condensing, files the agent had read are re-added as signature-only outlines.
Tracks each read file at full, partial, summary or excluded level with cached summaries.
Summarises an explored branch, recording files read and modified.

f: In-place compaction with stable session id
w: Compaction rewrites the transcript in place and archives the folded rows, keeping the session id.
Keeps the just-delivered reply live across a compaction.
Goal, plan/todos, delegations and loaded skills are captured in durable state and re-injected after summarization so the plan survives compaction.
After an auto-compaction with nothing pending, the agent continues its reply.
Before each call, the fully assembled request is measured against the model's own window and output reserve, projecting what to drop or compact.
Tools let the model ask how much context remains and schedule its own compaction.
The model (or a token budget) installs a fresh context window without touching environment state.
A plugin slot lets a context engine own context assembly, compaction and sub-agent context.
Messages are built by a pipeline of processors (truncate, trim stale tool results, inject context) over a history graph.
Keeps only the latest N images or screenshots in history and degrades older ones to placeholders.
Very large tool outputs or pages are summarised by a model before entering context.

f: Oversized tool output spill to file
w: Tool results above a size budget are written to a file and replaced by a typed synopsis and pointer the agent can read.
Caps how much of each tool result enters context with head/tail truncation, budgeted against the remaining window.
Token-based caps per prompt field before templating.
File paths, URLs and task ids from tool results become short durable handles.

f: Token estimation calibrated to real usage
w: Local token estimates are anchored to the provider's reported usage, with per-model tokenizer profiles for text and images.

f: Token counting off the main thread
w: Runs token counting in a worker pool.
Shows how full the window is now, with a per-category breakdown (system prompt, tools, skills, history) and a context audit.
Pin or reset a per-agent context window that compaction and estimates respect, warning when it disagrees with provider metadata.
/recap summarises the conversation on demand or automatically.

f: Task continuity notes and history recall
w: Working notes per task plus history search/read tools over the thread.
Links model turns to persisted platform history for rebuilds.

f: Canonical transcript separate from wire request
w: One canonical transcript projects to each provider request, so storage, compaction and replay never depend on wire quirks.
Computer-use transcripts stored as blocks and trimmed with deterministic summaries.
The system prompt is built from typed, keyed sections (identity, tools, skills, workspace files, mode) chosen by context.
Keeps the request prefix byte-identical across turns (volatile data at the tail or in reminders) so provider prompt caches keep hitting.
Places provider cache breakpoints (static prefix, end of system, recent messages) and a stable cache key across compactions.
Selects a base prompt or guidance per model family, including a reduced prompt for small local models.
Tool schemas resolved per model family so each model sees what it handles best.
Users replace or extend the system prompt with their own text or file, presets, or a developer-role message.
Prompts declare typed {{variables}} (user, date, custom) resolved per chat, with an admin page for custom ones.

f: Personas with few-shot openers and tool scoping
w: Personas define a system prompt, opening dialogue, allowed tools and skills, and can be forced per session.
Built-in and user personalities layered over the prompt.
SOUL, IDENTITY, USER, TOOLS and similar workspace files are seeded and injected so users shape the agent's voice and knowledge.
AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules are loaded with per-file and total budgets and truncation warnings.
Instruction files found in subdirectories are added as tools touch them.
Per-surface hints tell the model how its output will be shown.
In a code workspace the agent adopts a coding mode with matching guidance.
The model is told its cwd, shell, OS, date, workspace layout, git status and sandbox profile, with configurable detail.
Open files, active file and visible ranges from the IDE are injected as context.
Callers inject text or multimodal content as an environment message.
A once-per-turn agent-only block composed from registered providers (time, todo state, token usage, channel).
Catalogued hidden reminders (session info, permissions, todo nudges) injected into the conversation.
User-provided text injected into every turn's context.
The model periodically gets the current date/time and location so its sense of time stays accurate.
Adds the signed-in user's account info as non-persisted context.
Bridges context events from connected modules (games, bots, plugins).
Adds Discord channel context for bot runs.
Turns user reactions on messages into feedback context.
Environment, permissions, instructions, tools and mode are rendered as typed snapshots and only diffs are sent.
@file, @folder, @diff, @git and @url references in a message expand into attached context.
External or model-authored text is normalised and fenced before entering prompts.
Long URLs are swapped for placeholders in model input and restored in output.
Deterministic transforms shrink page element trees before prompting.
Scales screenshots to model-friendly sizes and estimates image tokens.
Caches extraction results per page content.
Example conversations are sent as prior messages or folded into the system prompt.
The worker prompt is generated by introspecting action signatures and docstrings.
Prompt documents the screen size, apps and valid key names.

f: Prompt-based tool calling for models without native tools
w: Pluggable tool-call engines: native function calling, tools rendered into the prompt with text/XML parsing, or structured outputs, chosen per model.
A capability table decides per provider/model whether native tool calling is used.
Partial tool-call argument JSON is parsed as it streams so UIs can show file writes or commands before the call finishes.
Only a one-line tool index is sent; the model searches and activates full tool schemas on demand, keeping the hot path small.
Ranks a large tool or action catalog for the current prompt (keyword, BM25, embeddings, rank fusion or a reranker) before the planner sees it.

f: Code mode: tools called from code
w: Tools are exposed as typed functions and the model writes a script that calls them, with inner calls traced in the UI.

f: Parallel tool execution with resource locks
w: Independent tool calls from one response run concurrently up to a limit, while calls touching the same file or resource are serialized.
All tool calls from one response are prepared as one immutable batch for confirmation and execution.
Tool calls start as soon as the model emits them, before the step finishes.
Several actions are predicted in one call and each is validated against live state, aborting the rest when the page or UI changes.
Validates, confirms (policy and approvals), executes and records each tool call, with role and account gates.
Rewrites tool schemas so strict providers accept them.
Include or exclude tools by name pattern per agent.
Removes calls to disabled tools, or selected tool calls and results, from the prompt for a model call.
Merges built-in, MCP, plugin and custom tools with precedence and injects tool roles, user-selected tools and skills for the turn.
An injected parameter makes the model state, per call, what the tool call is for.
A fast model writes a short label for each batch of tool calls for the UI.
Reminder text (stale file warnings, follow-ups) rides along with tool results.
Per-tool time and model time-to-first-token in events.
Re-runs a tool call from an earlier message and continues from there.
A message starting with ! runs directly as a shell command.
A no-side-effect tool where the model logs a reasoning note.

f: Structured output via a final tool or schema
w: With a JSON schema (or Pydantic/Zod model), the agent must finish by returning validated structured output, natively or via a structuring step.
Each agent step returns a typed object (thinking, evaluation, memory, next goal, actions) parsed from the model.
Per model decides whether to send a JSON schema, JSON mode or nothing.
JSON/structured responses are rendered as formatted structures.
Executes structured prompts and streams user-visible schema fields as tokens arrive, filtering reasoning tags.
Emits an engine-neutral response grammar from registered actions for constrained local decoding.
Pools independent structured prompt sections into shared model calls.
Runs all post-turn evaluators in one schema-constrained small-model call.
A cheap first-stage call decides whether and how to respond before the planner runs.
Each pipeline's stored config becomes an ordered chain of stages (access control, preprocessing, runner, postprocessing).

f: Data source and output mode router
w: A model call picks which sources and output modes a message needs.
Messages starting with /notes, /online, /image, /research and similar pick the mode.

f: Search query extraction with date awareness
w: Rewrites the message and history into standalone search queries with date ranges.
Parent actions with sub-actions get a gated nested planner.
Fills parameters the planner left out from the conversation.
A small model writes the user-facing reply for an action from its result.
Rewrites canned templates and raw errors into the agent's voice before sending.
Keeps the user on a defined form path with required fields and progress.
Chooses between a one-shot call and an iterative peek/grep strategy over long inputs.
Detects the user's language from settings, locale or recent text so replies and examples match.
Per-model reminders to write complete code or not overreach.
The model keeps a visible checklist of subtasks (pending, in progress, done) that is re-injected as a reminder and shown with progress.
Persistent task tools to create, update, list and link tasks with dependencies.
Injects the current plan into context.
A read-only plan mode where the agent researches and writes a plan (mutating tools blocked), then switches to act mode to carry it out.
/deep-planning expands into silent research and an implementation plan before coding.
A composer selector switches between fast, standard, planning and sub-agent modes.
Drops evaluation fields and thinking to cut tokens and latency per step.
Pins or opens bounded windows of priority/faster inference tiers.
Persona modes (Architect, Code, Ask, Debug, Orchestrator) each with role text, when-to-use and tool groups.
User-defined modes from project and global files.
The model asks to change mode mid-task, subject to approval.
A task reopens in the mode it ran in.
Exports a mode with its rules files as one document and imports it.
Resolves which model and reasoning variant a slash workflow uses.
The agent asks structured questions (options or free text, optional form fields) mid-task; the turn pauses until answered, with timeouts falling back to a recommended option.
Tool calls pause for approve, deny or edit per policy and the run resumes from a checkpoint.
Scheduled, webhook and autonomous runs auto-deny approvals and questions instead of hanging.
Maps server approval conflicts to a recovery action shared by TUI and headless.
Agents report progress and decisions as brief cards with actions and can pause for input.
Predicts the user's next prompt or follow-up questions and shows them as chips or Tab-accept ghost text.
Starts running an accepted suggestion early on a forked, copy-on-write chat.
Starter prompts on the landing screen.
After the first exchange a cheap model writes a short title (instant placeholder first), plus tags and emoji.
The model sets a topic title and intent the UI uses to group turns.
One effort ladder (off to max/adaptive) set inline or per mode and clamped to what each provider supports.
Model reasoning streams separately into a collapsible thinking block with a live subject line; a setting chooses whether it shows.
Holds partial <think> tags across stream deltas so reasoning from tag-based models never leaks into the answer.
Parses special in-stream markers that trigger actions, delays or calls.
Restores paragraph boundaries in streamed reasoning summary parts.
Long reasoning is stored as head and tail with an omission marker.
Incremental parsers for think, chat, code and tool calls from Seed models.
One owner of stream lifecycles fans events out to listeners under a single-writer fence, with token callbacks.
Text, reasoning and tool parts are persisted as they stream with a stable id per step, so every part survives a crash.
Each finished step is saved at turn end so a crash keeps completed steps.
On restart, classifies how a session ended and recovers or finalizes in-flight turns, resuming from saved partial state.
While tools run, short status lines (searching, generating, done) stream to the client from the agent's own events and end with the real status.
Tallies what a turn did (tools run, files changed) for display.
Elapsed time of a running or finished generation is shown.
Shows when a run is parked on the user or budget, and when it completes or fails.

f: Turn state tracking for the UI
w: Per-turn streaming and approval state drives loading and button states.
Merges consecutive snapshot and delta events before flushing to a slow UI.
Batches many small stream parts into fewer chunks.
Re-chunks text into word or line pieces for smooth typing.
Streams replies with stable lines printed permanently and the tail live.
Buffers or disables streaming where a platform cannot stream.
A runner can send explicit replies mid-run.

f: Chat API over WebSocket and HTTP
w: Chat events stream over a WebSocket with origin checks and connection caps, or over HTTP streaming.
Modules send urgent notify events the character queues and reacts to.
Shared queue and stream utilities.
Hooks on agent begin/end, each step, model request/response and tool start/end let hosts and plugins observe and modify the run.
Command or HTTP hook handlers on pre/post tool use and other events, in Claude Code's format.
Pre/post request and error hook payloads are safe and redacted, and stream observers run on their own queues.
Plugins get immutable sub-agent lifecycle contracts.
Goals, memories, search and more plug into core through one extension API.
/btw asks a quick question about the conversation from a detached fork, leaving the main history unchanged.
Runs a forked child that shares the parent's prompt cache.
Forks a session from a checkpoint, copying workspace files.
Several reference models answer and an aggregator model merges them into one reply.
Records each mixture-of-agents fan-out per session.
A task tool spawns a named sub-agent (own prompt, model and tools, defined in files) in its own thread and returns its result.
The UI tracks dispatched sub-agents and their tool activity.
Merges GUI, code and MCP agent plugins into one prompt and toolset.
Caches full model responses keyed by the request.
A typed, validated per-request context (user, tenant, flags, counters) flows through agents and tools.
Typed reducers merge sandbox, artifacts, todos and goal channels in shared thread state.
Messages convert between internal events and every SDK/provider format, merging parallel actions.
Batches consecutive saves per thread.
Pulls the agent's final answer from the event history.
Skills and system/user message suffixes carried on the agent context.
Stateless single model calls outside any conversation.
A tool schedules a future wake-up stored in the database.
Tracks the net file diff produced during a turn.
Hashes each request's body, tools and images for comparison.
Logs per-call usage and annotates each step with model and usage.
Records which author each turn came from.
An async run releases the state lock while awaiting model calls.
A status machine (idle, running, paused, waiting, finished, error, stuck).
Agent runs execute on the server through a queue, isolated per run.
An in-app assistant that manages the workspace through an allowlist of tools.
Starts a new conversation after a session idles too long.
Creates agents with default memory, tools and model.
Recompiles the system prompt and memory into the conversation on demand.
A prefix is required before a woken message reaches the model.

f: Follow-up task on the same session
w: Appends a new task to a finished agent, keeping history and state.

f: Initial actions before the first step
w: Runs caller-given actions before the first model step.
Builds the user turn from text, images and files, expanding @mentions.
A minimum gap between model requests across all tasks.
Malformed edits, lint/test failures or each step's trajectory are reflected back so the agent corrects itself.
Decides which written files are user-facing outputs and shows them as artifacts.
A research mode runs bounded plan-act rounds where a model picks the next tool each step.

f: Browser task step loop (vision and element tree)
w: Each step scrapes the page into an element tree and screenshot and asks for a list of actions.
Iteratively plans the next mini-goal, runs it as a sub-task and checks completion.
One persistent conversation drives raw browser tools via native tool calls.
Builds each block's goal from navigation goal, directives and prior outputs.
Multi-turn callers for UI-TARS and Yutori computer-use models.
Parses model action JSON into typed browser actions.
Prompts for custom dropdowns and autocomplete inputs.
Tasks declare error codes and failures are mapped to them.
When a run hits its step or retry cap, a model summarises why it failed.
A single worker plans and acts each step without a manager agent.
Creates, updates, finalizes and reviews multi-phase project plans from parameters.
Turns goals into simple or model-decomposed plans, validates actions up front, and executes steps sequentially, in parallel or as a DAG.

f: Markdown-safe block chunking for chat channels
w: Splits streamed replies into channel-sized messages at paragraph boundaries without breaking markdown.
Sorts each model reply into exactly one type (tool calls, content, reasoning-only, empty) and dispatches it.

f: Condensation triggers by token budget or event count
w: Fires summarising condensation when a token budget or event-count limit is exceeded, computing the shortest prefix to fold.
A condenser base class with rolling, pipeline (chained) and no-op strategies selected in settings.

A helpers frame above the message box (up to 3, expands to a roster); steer or stop one helper; open its record view-only with Back; helpers stay out of Recent and search; the chip never says done while helpers work or failed; plain-word approvals tied to the opened conversation; helper faces are never the mascot.
Lanes per member in Team > Teams of specialists.
A live overview of every Trunk, helper, computer, board and task, with steer, stop and pause.
Looking up a setting costs one call with trimmed results.
A short question does not run a tool search or load lots of context.
What the agent adopts is decided by evals, not extra model reasoning; learning runs overnight on local or subscription models only.

f: JEV decision models and compaction evaluation
w: Typed yes/pick/score judgments with calibrated confidence, and an evaluation of JEV for compaction with a five-second target preserving recall, decisions and tool calls.
Explain why a given tool call would be allowed or refused, with examples checked when the contract loads.
A write with unknown outcome requires checking external state before any automatic repeat.
After an interruption the window explains that a task is continuing and from where, and shows when live updates reconnect.

f: Branch setting defaults for loop features
w: fly-core ships ON when needed; troubleshoot mode ships when-needed with the real shell ranked first.
LlamaIndex-style chat engines over data.
Completions that draw on repository context.

f: JSONL session persistence and working-session tracking
w: Sessions persisted as JSONL, and tracking of the working session.
Vision input for user-provided image files in tasks.
Jobs (one-shot, recurring, event-driven) persist with their runtime state and fire from an in-process scheduler that survives restarts, with atomic claiming of due occurrences.

f: Schedule kinds with timezones and DST
w: Fire at an ISO or relative time, on a fixed interval, or on a 5/6-field cron in an IANA timezone, with weekday/monthly recurrence and DST-safe repeats.
The schedule form rejects invalid cron (fields, aliases, steps, impossible dates) before saving.
Recurring jobs that all land on the hour are spread over a deterministic window (or random minute plus jitter) to avoid load spikes, with an exact opt-out.
Before saving, the user sees the next times the schedule will fire.
"every weekday at 9am", "in 45m", "once in two minutes" or a sentence asking for a recurring task is turned into a normalized schedule.
Schedules are shown back in plain words in the user's timezone ("every day at 8:00"), never as cron or ISO strings.
After downtime, overdue jobs run once (coalesced) and say so, interrupted runs reconcile to their exact occurrence ids instead of staying stuck.
Failures notify the owner once (grouped by error signature), repeated failures pause the job with a plain-language reason the UI shows.
When an automation keeps failing, the scheduler posts a repair request into the owner conversation (job text and errors treated as data) so the agent can fix it.

f: Retry classification, re-runs and quota holds
w: Failures are classified (rate limit, overload, network, timeout); unreachable-model fires retry on a bounded ladder and quota-closed providers hold fires until the window reopens.
Every attempt is recorded with status, delivery outcome and errors, queryable per job (successful, failed, active).
Before a run, credentials, delivery targets and skills are checked; failed or stalled runs get normalized, phase-specific reasons.
A health scan of all jobs (overdue fires, stuck dispatch, broken delivery) with actionable findings, including warning when schedules exist but the gateway is not running.
Each run is bounded by a per-job or default timeout and an inactivity watchdog, and the edit form enforces the server ceiling.
Jobs run in a worker process outside the gateway so a gateway restart does not kill in-flight runs.
One gateway serving many profiles decides which profile's cron it ticks, with profile-scoped state.
The in-process trigger can be swapped for a plugin or cloud-managed scheduler.
Due scheduled tasks are queued and the highest-priority pending task runs next.
The model can create, list, edit, pause, resume, run and remove jobs from conversation.
The agent schedules a future point when the same session resumes with a prompt (after N seconds, at a time, or on cron), and can list or cancel its wakeups.
/loop [interval] <prompt> re-wakes the current conversation on a fixed or self-paced cadence until done, a count, or a judge says stop.
A recurring job proposes its own next check time, clamped to min/max bounds.
A periodic check-in (default 30 min) reads a HEARTBEAT checklist and runs only when there is something to do, with an interval setting.

f: Active hours, quiet windows and fire gates
w: Proactive work respects active hours, quiet hours, weekends, days off and travel through pluggable shouldFire gates.
The owner pauses all scheduled and proactive work for a period with one switch.
After a check runs, a small model (or a [SILENT] reply) decides whether the result is worth messaging the user about.
A cheap probe (script or URL) runs each tick and the model only wakes when its output changes, so watches stay silent when nothing changed.
A script runs before (or instead of) the model and decides whether to fire, passing state and a message; a script that wants approval asks first.
Each job keeps a small key-value scratch (cursors, watermarks, checklist) between runs.
A job can run a shell command or a headless script with the agent's tools on schedule, with no model call.
Trigger and payload scripts can call configured MCP servers as functions, scoped by the job's allowed servers.
A job runs in the main session, the conversation that created it, a fresh isolated session or a named one, and its turns stay in a conversation of their own.
A conversation header links to the scheduled tasks bound to it.
Expired per-run sessions are pruned on a retention schedule while live descendants are kept.
Each job pins its own provider, model and reasoning effort, falling back to the default.

f: Per-job tool allowlist and creator authority
w: A job stores its own tool policy and the creator's authority at creation, so unattended runs never widen what they can do.
Cron prompts and trigger payloads are scanned for injection and exfiltration patterns and framed as outside data.
Jobs whose prompt or script would restart or stop the gateway from inside it are refused.
Finished runs are delivered to the origin chat, a home channel, any platform:chat, a webhook or nowhere, with a dry-run preview of where each job will deliver.
Run results are queued in a restart-safe outbox that a delivery worker sends with retries, parking undeliverable sends for later.
A delivered cron result is seeded into the chat's session so the user can reply and continue with the job's context.
A job injects the latest output of upstream jobs into its prompt (collect, triage, ship).
A job attaches skills whose bodies load into its prompt at fire time.
A job runs its agent and scripts inside a chosen project folder.
Jobs can be created paused for review or a manual run before they start firing.

f: Declarative automations from files and git
w: Automations defined in files (markdown with frontmatter, declared keys) or a git repo are reconciled into the store, upserting only declared fields.
Automations export to a portable file and import back, including merging a foreign store.
Authenticated endpoints let outside services wake an agent or submit a turn; the door stays closed until the owner opens it, and routes can be managed at runtime.
Named webhook routes render message templates from the payload ({{field.path}}) and route or fan out to agents and sessions.
Normalized outside events (PR opened, Slack event, signed MCP event, webhook) start matching automations through a durable ingress with leases, backoff and dead-lettering.
A named trigger bound to a session can be fired from a local command or stdin and is delivered at least once.
Agent lifecycle and run-completion events are POSTed to URLs, HMAC-signed (Standard Webhooks style), with retries and a bounded queue.
Outbound automation webhook URLs are validated and private or loopback targets refused unless allowed.
A watched mailbox starts an isolated restricted session per new allowed email, gating senders by DKIM/SPF/DMARC; Gmail uses Pub/Sub push.
Agents subscribe to PR reviews, comments, CI and mentions and get them as signals or replies.
A watcher on a command's output, a stream or a WebSocket, or a command exiting, wakes the agent with the buffered events.
Long MCP submit/status/cancel tools become durable background tasks the agent can list or cancel, with notifications.
Submit a task to the background hub and exit; it runs there and notifies on completion (/bg).

User shell hooks run on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, PreCompact and more with JSON on stdin; they can block or rewrite tool calls and inject context (Claude Code compatible).
Outputs from several matching hooks merge with defined precedence for decisions and context.
Hooks before and after model calls see a stable, versioned request/response format.
A hook asks a model (or a sub-agent) for an allow or block decision against written criteria.
A hook calls an MCP tool with arguments filled from the event fields.
Oversized hook context is saved to a temp file and replaced by a preview and path.
Converts Claude Code hook settings into this app's hook events.
Lists hooks with status and lets the user enable or disable each, from a panel, CLI or API.
Ready-made hooks (block rm -rf, desktop notify, typecheck on change, memory logger).
A user program runs with a JSON payload when a turn completes, for custom alerts.
Folder-based hook packages (HOOK.md/HOOK.yaml + handler) run on gateway, command and message lifecycle events and install from npm, archives or URLs.
On /new or /reset the ending session's context is saved to a dated memory file.
Runs the workspace BOOT.md instructions when the gateway starts.
Logs command events to a central audit file.
Posts a visible chat notice when compaction starts and finishes.
Injects extra workspace files into agent context on bootstrap.
Curated starter jobs are offered as one-tap accept or dismiss cards, and recommended automations show on home.
A gallery of pre-written automation templates (blueprints) that fill a form, a slash command or a chat seed.
Prebuilt automations ship setup manifests with a capability check, prerequisites review, required inputs and metrics.
Seeded routines like a morning brief, reminder digest and evening check-in, plus a daily brief of agent results, so the assistant messages you first when switched on.
Reminder fires escalate by priority (retry, cross-channel), snooze resets the ladder.
A fired task completes itself when the user acknowledges, replies or the subject changes.
Triggers relative to wake time, bedtime or a calendar event start.
The model picks reminder content and timing but delivery is pinned to the verified private chat.

f: Owner life surfaces (reminders, alarms, todos, routines)
w: Owner-facing actions for reminders, alarms, todos and routines over one shared engine.
A drafted message scheduled to send later is persisted whole so it survives restarts.
On iOS, background tasks wake the agent so scheduled work runs while the app is backgrounded.
UI events are watched and at most one scoped helpful offer is surfaced under governance rules.
With autonomy on, a background tick lets the agent think and act on its own.
Long-horizon goals (quarter, year, life) are first-class objects whose check-ins run on the scheduler and record responses.
A goal stays active across turns; a judge model decides after each turn whether it is met, with budgets and pause, resume and stop.
Goals carry explicit completion criteria and quality gates; /subgoal adds criteria mid-run.
Agent-managed todos, follow-ups, handoffs and reminders with status and priority, reviewable by the user.
Scheduled CI workflows run the agent to triage issues, find duplicates, implement TODOs, sweep issues or track upstream releases.
Backups run on a schedule to local, git, WebDAV, S3 or offsite targets.
One shared timer runs periodic maintenance (cleanup, re-indexing connected sources, skill review) in worker processes.
Run one prompt non-interactively from the CLI, a file or stdin with text, JSON or stream-JSON output and exit codes for scripts and CI.

f: Command stream into a running agent
w: An outside process sends NDJSON commands (start, message, cancel) over stdin or an input file to a long-lived agent.
A running session mirrors structured events to a side channel so other tools can follow along.
Other programs start, resume, cancel and message tasks and subscribe to task events through an SDK, extension API or IPC socket.
A recipe file packages instructions, prompt, extensions, settings, typed parameters and response schema, renders templates, validates and auto-submits its first prompt.
A recipe runs other recipes as subagent tasks.
Recipes encode into links that open in the desktop app.
Recipes are found in local folders and a GitHub repo and can be browsed and loaded.
ACP clients list, load, save and start sessions from recipes.
Desktop editor for recipes with sub-recipes, model and extension selectors and a schema editor.
Code-built workflows with typed steps and .then, .branch, .parallel, .foreach and loops, nested workflows and validated inputs, saved with steps that survive a restart.
A step suspends with a payload (for approval or input) and the run resumes later from where it stopped.
Re-run a past run from any step with changed input, replaying earlier step results.
Active runs recover after a crash, with state checkpointed after each step, or run on Inngest or Temporal.
Workflows execute through pubsub events so steps run on distributed workers with fencing and retries.

f: Workflow cancel, sleep and wait steps
w: Runs can be cancelled; steps wait for a duration, until a time, print or navigate.
Steps read and write a typed workflow-level state object.
Runs stream step events and custom chunks; watchers subscribe to state changes.
Workflows defined as JSON graphs are validated and rehydrated at runtime without code deploys.
An agent writes, saves, searches and runs workflows from chat or from an uploaded SOP document.
Workflows declare cron schedules, so a saved procedure starts itself on a clock.
Typed classifiers, predicates or LLM prompts choose which branch of a workflow runs.
Agents and tools are used directly as workflow steps, and workflows become tools for agents.
For-each and while blocks repeat nested steps over a list or until a condition holds.
A step starts another workflow, waiting for it or fire-and-forget, with a depth check.
A step runs user or generated code against the live page with run-scoped files.
A step calls a model with a templated prompt and optional JSON schema output.
Step fields use templates over parameters, trigger payload and earlier outputs.
A step signs in with a stored credential and TOTP, so scheduled jobs can re-sign-in unattended.
A run retries with the next stored credential when one fails.
A step makes templated HTTP calls with authorization checks on each redirect.
Steps for free-form browser tasks, navigation goals, single actions and schema extraction.
Download and upload files, parse CSV/Excel/ZIP/PDF, fill and split PDFs, export records as Parquet.
A step sends templated email with attachments over SMTP.
A step reads messages from a connected Gmail or Outlook inbox.
Steps read and write Google Sheets, never retrying non-idempotent writes.
A step runs a web search and passes results on.
A step checks the result against criteria and fails or stops the run when unmet.
A multi-step tool pipeline runs as one deterministic call with approval and input checkpoints and resume tokens.
A predefined step plan (JSON or workflow) executes step by step through the policy-checked executor, including batches of plans.
Persisted workflows run in an isolated child process with a fail-closed protocol, stored per tenant with revisions and run events.
Workflow-aware turns see the owner's saved workflows, listed or ranked by the message.
A coding task runs as a durable workflow with provision, turn, approval and submit steps.
Rules bound to sources start agent sessions on work-item transitions and reconcile external issues on a schedule.
Notifications are stored with delivery policies and dispatched to agents as signals, with an inbox tool.
A user demonstration in the live browser is recorded and turned into workflow steps or code, so the agent learns a job by watching once.
One view of scheduled and triggered automations with search, on/off switch, owner name, health badge and Run now.
A detail page with prompt, configuration and an activity log of runs with stdout/stderr, and recent runs in the sidebar.
Edit name, prompt, schedule, timeout, profile and plugins with validation before saving.
Success rate, durations, cost totals and per-run sparklines computed from run history.
From a failed run, start a conversation seeded with the instructions and the error tail so the agent can fix it.
A guided entry starts a chat seeded to set up an automation, and the agent shows a confirm card in chat once scheduled.
Client-visible status folds live turns and the next pending wakeup so UIs can show "scheduled".
RPC methods for listing, history, run logs and wake, scoped to the caller, plus schedule lifecycle events to clients.
A command set to add, edit, list, show, run now and remove schedules and view their runs.
/tasks in a chat app renders the chat's scheduled tasks as a card with enable, disable and delete buttons.
One inbox aggregates briefs, approvals, finished work and history across agents.
Each Trunk owns its own schedules and routines; the assistant can own schedules too.
Rejected schedule text stays in the box, the trigger placeholder suggests only what works, and check-in interval buttons.
"What it needs" card with fix options and costs; Later tab actions (Stop waiting, I've signed it, Finish now); questions sit under the last message.
Scoped flow questions, stale answers revoked, old asks expire, a late yes is never silently lost and Allow continues the same task.
A saved procedure shows its proposed steps and runs only after the owner has seen everything; replays are held for safety review; Trunks propose changes as a "Change suggested" pill.
The flow editor as a picture with add, move, remove, run and save, plus a branching layout.
Tries four versions of an automation flow and keeps the best (automatic workflow optimization).
Kanban boards, a waiting line of tasks and widgets for automations.
Dashboards and live pages the agent writes and refreshes on a schedule.
"From now on" standing instructions the assistant keeps applying.
Undoing a goal forgets its facts and deletes its drafts.
Saved prompts switch on, validate, save, persist, and Use fills the message box.

f: Project board for flows and schedules
w: Each project keeps its flows and schedules together.
Start an automation when a USB device is plugged in; ships off.
Capture a site's network traffic and turn it into an API skill to skip the browser next time.
Onboarding asks which boring task to take off your plate and turns the answer into a first routine.
Prepare and schedule a social post that stays in the approval queue until authorized.
After the computer wakes, probe each chat adapter once and reconnect failures, merging duplicate resume events.
SendInput absolute coordinates, per-monitor DPI and Unicode typing, plus scroll, drag, double-click, right-click and hover tools.

f: Misplaced: Home Assistant script lock guard
w: Home Assistant scripts and scenes go through the same always-ask lock guard.
OAuth sign-in flows for connected services.
Notifications for new Branch versions with an Apply button, and gateway restart or mode-change triggers.

f: Misplaced: Chat app connect wizard save
w: Saving the chat wizard marks the app connected and confirms messages there reach Branch.

f: Misplaced: Ship-on defaults for other areas
w: Default on/off decisions for features listed under automation settings that belong elsewhere: answer engine, answer pages and article writer (research), intent pipeline and runtimes (multi-agent), hindsight (memory), analytics and nodes (ops), app-server and snapshots (coding), forecasts (research), leads and readiness (tools).

f: Agent browser toolset (navigate, click, type, scroll, tabs, upload, keys, JS)
w: The agent drives a real browser with one family of tools: open pages, go back/forward, click, type, pick dropdowns, send keys, scroll, wait, manage tabs, upload files and run page JavaScript.
The page is read as a compact accessibility tree where every element gets a short ref (e.g. e12) that later clicks and typing target.

f: Indexed DOM snapshot of interactive elements
w: Merges DOM, accessibility tree and layout into one numbered list of the things a user could click, optionally with a screenshot.
Finds interactive elements from tags, ARIA roles, cursor style and attached JavaScript event listeners, so custom widgets are clickable.
Hides elements that are fully covered by others so the model only sees what a person could actually click.
Walks iframes from other origins and routes clicks and reads into the right frame.

f: Numbered marks on the page (annotate, then act by number)
w: Draws numbered boxes on clickable elements, in-page or on the screenshot, so the model (and owner) can say 'click 7'.
For vision models: screenshot the page, let the model output pixel actions (click x,y, drag, type) and execute them.
Picks how the agent drives the browser: DOM tools, pure vision, or both together.
Falls back from visual modes to DOM tools when the chosen model cannot do visual grounding.

f: LLM extraction to markdown or structured JSON
w: Turns the page into clean markdown (chunked for long pages) and asks a model to pull out structured data against a schema.

f: Web fetch: rendered page to markdown
w: web.fetch-style reading of a URL through a headless/rendering browser or scrape service, slimmed and converted to markdown.
Reads the current page's main content (Readability) as markdown with offset pagination so long pages don't flood context.

f: Cheap page search (find text, CSS query)
w: Non-LLM actions that grep visible page text or query elements by CSS selector without a full extraction.
URLs typed in a message trigger an offer to read them in, with per-URL 'don't ask again'.
The first browser use checks for Playwright/Chromium and installs it (one command), choosing mirrors when needed.

f: Find and launch a local browser
w: Locates installed Chrome/Edge/Chromium/Firefox per OS, launches it (local, CDP or cloud engines) and cleans up its processes afterwards.

f: Event-driven CDP browser session with watchdogs
w: One browser session object on an event bus, with independent watchdogs for navigation, tabs, downloads and crashes.

f: CDP target and session pool tracking
w: Keeps the pool of CDP sessions in sync with attached/detached targets so tabs and popups are never lost.

f: Hang and crash protection for the browser
w: Every CDP call has a timeout, crashed targets and stalled requests raise events, and unhealthy browsers are retired instead of hanging the task.
The browser starts only when first needed, is reused by every tool in that conversation/thread and recovers if it was closed.

f: Browser session cleanup (idle janitor, orphan reaper, tab cleanup)
w: Closes idle sessions and tabs the agent opened, and kills leaked browser processes on exit.
Long-lived browser sessions that later tasks reuse, renew and reap on timeout, keeping the page and login state between steps.
Named browser profiles (cookies, storage, user-data dir) that are isolated from each other and can be saved, listed, renamed, reset and reused.

f: Use the owner's real signed-in profile
w: Snapshot the owner's active Chromium profile into an agent-owned copy so the agent browses with the owner's logins without touching the original.

f: Attach to a running Chrome over CDP
w: Discover or launch a debug-port Chrome/Edge/Brave and attach the agent to it (local or remote CDP URL, with headers).
Loads and saves cookies and localStorage to a storage-state file on connect and shutdown.

f: Read and write cookies / storage as tools
w: Tools that read and set cookies, localStorage and sessionStorage for logged-in work.

f: Import cookies and logins from the owner's browser
w: Copies (decrypting) Chrome-family cookies and profiles into the agent's isolated profile, optionally keeping them in sync.
Merges fresh cookies from each run back into the saved profile, freshest wins, so logins stay alive.
Proxy server, bypass list and proxy auth applied at launch.
Grants configured permissions (clipboard, notifications, geolocation) on connect.
Optionally loads uBlock Origin, a cookie-banner dismisser and ClearURLs into the agent browser.
alert/confirm/prompt dialogs never block the agent: they are captured into a queue the agent answers (or auto-accepted).
Tracks what the browser downloaded (local and remote CDP), sanitises names, auto-saves PDFs and exposes the files.

f: Wait for page readiness or a condition
w: Waits for network idle after navigation, or polls until the URL matches a pattern, streaming progress.
A Page/Element/Mouse API for deterministic scripted steps that mixes with AI steps.
Escape-hatch tool that sends any Chrome DevTools Protocol command to the session.
The model gets one tool that runs code against a persistent browser with helpers (tabs, click_at_xy, js, cdp).
A dedicated sub-agent (or planner/navigator/validator trio) handles a browsing task and reports back to the main agent.
An SDK where a page gets AI commands: act('...'), extract, validate, plus AI-assisted click/fill and high-level run_task/login/download helpers.

f: AI element locator (describe an element in words)
w: Find an element by describing it; the AI resolves it once, then it behaves like a normal locator.
When an action fails because the page changed, it is rerouted between DOM, accessibility and vision surfaces instead of failing.
The SDK runs its API server in-process so no separate deployment is needed.
Hosted browsers (Browser Use, Browserbase, Firecrawl) on one provider registry, selected by config.

f: Localhost URLs when the browser is remote
w: Detects localhost/LAN URLs on a cloud browser and either spawns a local sidecar browser or returns a tunnel hint.

f: Serve a local browser to the cloud via tunnel
w: Starts Chrome plus a CDP proxy and optional tunnel so a hosted service can drive a local browser.
Self-hosted fingerprint-spoofing Firefox fork mapped onto the same browser tools.
Opt-in low-memory headless engine for text/DOM tasks with automatic fallback to Chrome.
Opens a visible browser window and keeps headed sessions alive between tasks.
Detects captcha / 'are you human' checks and pauses the step loop until it is solved.

f: Live browser view with input forwarding
w: Streams the agent's browser as a live screencast the owner watches and can click, type and scroll in, with tabs, takeover and annotations sent back to the agent.

f: In-app agent browser (built into the desktop app)
w: A browser inside the app window that agents drive through tools while the owner watches, with a visible agent cursor and 'agent controlling' chip.
Visual feedback while the agent works: animated cursor, click ripples, highlighted targets and a border marking the page as under agent control.
An overlay blocks the owner's input and shows a banner while the agent acts, lifting only during its own actions.
Records a browser task (rrweb events, MJPEG video with action overlays, or whole-display MP4) for replay and sharing.

f: Save page as PDF or screenshot
w: Actions that print the current page to PDF and capture screenshots into the agent's files.

f: Page snapshot diffs (watch a page for change)
w: Takes successive snapshots of a tab and diffs them under a deadline, plus screenshots and PDFs of the page.

f: Ask a vision model about the page
w: Takes an (optionally annotated) screenshot and answers a question about it with a vision model.
Lists the images on the current page (src, alt) for follow-up analysis, SSRF-guarded.
Returns page console output and evaluates JavaScript in the page.
Every navigation, redirect, snapshot, console and eval path is checked against private/loopback addresses, with a denylist of sensitive JS primitives.
Config sets a default plus per-origin allow/deny policy (and history access) for the agent's browser.

f: Managed requirements for the in-app browser
w: Admin-managed requirements for the interactive in-app browser, such as whether external sites are allowed.
Oversized trees are truncated (full copy saved to a file), secrets are redacted before reaching the model and typed text is redacted in logs.
The owner acknowledges a privacy notice before the browser agent is first used.
Fills saved usernames, passwords and OTP codes into page fields by handle from a local vault, so the model never sees the secret; only on allowed origins.
Shows 1Password/pass entries as metadata only and delivers a secret by a confirmed, expiring clipboard copy.
Detects OTP inputs split across several boxes and types the code digit by digit.

f: Drive the owner's own Chrome tabs via an extension
w: A Chrome extension (chrome.debugger) plus an authenticated local relay lets the agent drive tabs the owner shares in his signed-in browser, with per-tab pause/allow.
One browser action routes each call to whichever target is available: the extension, the embedded browser, a headless fallback or a remote server.

f: Extension screenshot and file upload channel
w: A one-shot, time-limited upload channel for screenshots and files from the extension, with size and type caps.
The desktop controller holds identity keys in the OS credential store and exchanges encrypted, signed browser commands with remote devices.
When no real browser is available, browser commands run against JSDOM.
Injects the live tab list and dispatch mode into the agent's context when browsing.
Older page snapshots in history are replaced with short placeholders so only the latest stays in context.
Seeded minimum-jerk pointer paths that land inside the target, instead of teleporting.

f: Interactive task lifecycle with revalidated actuation
w: Each step of an interactive task is persisted before dispatch and re-checked (page, frame, input revision, policy) at the moment of the click, so stale approvals are refused.
Runs the browser inside a sandbox container network and lets the owner watch/take over through an authenticated noVNC link.
One shared definition of browser action limits and timeouts used by both the tool schema and the runtime.
Settings/CLI flags for the browser: CDP endpoint, executable, headless, proxy, user agent, user-data dir, viewport, provider.

f: Discord account scraper over the browser
w: Per-account Discord scraper over a browser CDP session, exposed as a service.
A browser extension streams page, video progress, subtitles and frames from video sites to the agent.

f: Owner browser controls (address bar, search, back/forward/reload, Stop/Pause, truthful states, Chrome extras)
w: The owner-facing browser chrome: type an address or search words, back/forward/reload, Stop and Pause, honest loading/refused/failed states, IME/clipboard/selection, find-in-page, zoom, history and bookmarks, and an owner window not bound by per-task limits.

f: Branch browser view layout (full-size view, docked chat, PiP, Trunk naming)
w: Branch's own look for the browser: full-size view with the conversation docked, picture-in-picture, a globe button in the header, no separate Browser tab, named for its Trunk with its face.
keepoak.com opens in Branch's browser view as a locked session of its own; the agent can't act there unless allowed.

End-to-end proof in the owner's app: start, open, read, close, then a signed-in flow; works on modern sites with measured speed; side-by-side comparison against Chrome, Codex and GrokBot; multistep form fixture that pauses before approval.
Screenshots black out password boxes before any picture reaches a model or the owner's log.
A named multi-page journey with one picture per step, saved and run again in one step.
Remember a site's quirks (cookie notice to press, what to wait for) with a Settings list and Forget.
Always pick the most private choice (decline non-essential) on any site, e.g. via DuckDuckGo autoconsent in opt-out mode.
A per-site opt-in lets scheduled tasks use a saved sign-in, with an owner recovery step when it fails.
Hand to the owner for password changes, captchas and security warnings; confirm camera/mic/location prompts and downloads; optional confirm-every-type and block-uploads switches.
Read the owner's browser history only with approval and within a date range.

f: Learn a site's API from network traffic
w: Capture a site's network traffic and turn it into an API skill so later tasks skip the browser.

f: Misplaced: computer-use items in the browser list
w: Requirements filed under browser that are about desktop computer use.
Open a preview server the agent started in the owner's browser or phone through a token-guarded proxy.

f: Misplaced: safety items in the browser list
w: CSV formula injection in exports; configurable autonomy modes.
Web Push (VAPID) to the browser and installed web app for 'needs you' and 'finished'.
The Settings page section for system access, browser extension and computer assignment.

f: Misplaced: document and PDF text extraction
w: Extract text from PDFs and documents.

f: All apps: gateway runs every chat app in one background process
w: One long-running gateway starts each enabled chat app, relays messages to agent sessions and sends replies back, and keeps answering while the window is closed. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: channel plugin SDK and adapter contract
w: A public contract for writing one chat-app adapter: inbound context, ingress authorization, outbound adapters with receipts, durable sends and live previews, so every app gets the same behaviours. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: ordered message pipeline stages
w: Every inbound message passes ordered stages (wake, allowlist, session status, rate limit, safety, preprocess, process, decorate, respond) that can wrap later stages.

f: All apps: supervised gateway process with auto-restart
w: Chat adapters run in a supervised child process with a ready signal and restart with exponential backoff, so one crash does not take chat apps down.

f: All apps: reconnect with a needs-attention status
w: Disconnected adapters reconnect in the background (also after sleep/wake) and, past a failure threshold, are flagged as needing attention with the reason shown, instead of retrying silently forever. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: enable, disable, pause or reload one chat app live
w: Turning a chat app on, off or reconfiguring it (or pausing a failing one with /platform from chat) starts or stops only that adapter inside the running gateway.

f: All apps: single gateway per user (attach instead of a second copy)
w: A host lock plus rendezvous record lets later launches attach to, rescan or replace the live gateway instead of binding a second port.

f: All apps: restart-complete notice to the requesting chat
w: After a restart the gateway tells the chat (and thread) that asked for it that it is back, including how long it took.

f: All apps: auto-resume turns cut off by a restart
w: Turns interrupted by a gateway restart are marked and continued automatically after boot if still fresh, never twice.

f: All apps: relay adapter for platforms fronted by a remote connector
w: One generic adapter takes a capability descriptor at handshake and lets a remote connector own the platform wire, so a relay machine can hold the chat accounts.

f: All apps: relay egress target authorization
w: Messages sent through the relay are refused unless the gateway has a record of that destination, so the model cannot address arbitrary chats.

f: All apps: hosted multi-tenant webhook gateway
w: A hosted gateway verifies connector webhooks, routes each event to the owning agent and delivers replies for many tenants.

f: All apps: one public webhook URL for every webhook-based app
w: Webhook-based adapters (Slack HTTP, LINE, WeCom, QQ, Lark, Teams, SMS) share one listener under per-bot or per-profile paths instead of opening their own ports.

f: All apps: DM pairing codes for unknown senders
w: A stranger who DMs the bot gets a short one-time code (unambiguous alphabet, expiry, rate-limited, lockout on failed approvals); the owner approves it and the sender is added for that app. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: unauthorized senders get a code or silence, owner gets one notice
w: Strangers either receive a pairing code or total silence when an allowlist exists (so the bot is not revealed), and the owner gets one sanitized notice per sender explaining the fix.

f: All apps: DM access policy (open, allowlist, pairing, disabled)
w: Each app has a DM policy and a group policy chosen from open, allowlist, pairing or disabled, with per-scope allow lists. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: sender and group allowlists (one global list plus per-app lists)
w: Allowlists of users and groups (exact ids, wildcards, group names/keywords) gate who may talk to the bot, read per profile and fail closed; a nickname blocklist drops named users. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: bind a chat account as the owner
w: A pairing command (e.g. /pair with a 6-digit code) binds a chat user as the owner, and the backend can DM the owner by id; sender authority is resolved per message.

f: All apps: command permission tiers (owner/admin vs everyone)
w: A second access axis decides who may run which slash commands, separately for DMs and groups, with a /help and /whoami floor for others.

f: All apps: confirm destructive slash commands
w: Destructive commands such as session reset ask for an explicit confirm (buttons where supported, text otherwise) before running.

f: All apps: cap on concurrently active chat sessions
w: An optional limit on simultaneously active chat sessions; new conversations beyond it get a polite rejection.

f: All apps: hide raw user and chat ids from the model
w: User and chat identifiers can be hashed in the model-visible session context where raw ids are not needed.

f: All apps: bot-to-bot reply loop guard
w: A budget on bot-authored messages per conversation plus a 'this is a bot' hint stops two agents from replying to each other forever. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: ignore the bot's own echoes
w: Messages the bot just sent (or its own account's messages) are not processed as new input.
A fixed-window limit per chat either waits for the next window or drops the extra messages.
The bot answers only between configured start and stop times.

f: All apps: ignore messages by prefix or pattern
w: Messages starting with configured prefixes or matching patterns are dropped silently.

f: All apps: mute or switch off the agent in one chat
w: Mute a room or a whole server (optionally for a time that auto-expires), set a reply gate (mention-only, muted until a lift phrase), or disable a session entirely.
A group can switch individual plugins off for itself.

f: All apps: human takeover of a room
w: The agent stops replying while a human has taken over a room and resumes when handed back.

f: All apps: group trigger rules (mention, reply, prefix, keyword, pattern)
w: In groups the agent answers only when mentioned, replied to, or triggered by a configured prefix, keyword or pattern (stripped before processing), with a per-group 'every message / only when mentioned' activation the owner can set from chat. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: bare mention asks what the person wants
w: A message that only mentions the bot gets a short 'what can I do?' and the next message is treated as addressed.

f: All apps: work out who a group message is addressed to
w: Classifies, without a model call, whether a message addresses the agent, someone else or nobody, and records addressing edges.

f: All apps: talk less when dominating a group
w: Live signals (the agent's share of recent turns, who talks to whom, pace) make the agent hold back in busy groups; includes a When2Speak evaluation.

f: All apps: occasional unprompted replies in groups
w: In chosen groups the bot may reply to unaddressed messages with a set probability or a decaying attention score.

f: All apps: listen to unmentioned group messages as quiet context
w: Unmentioned group chatter is recorded as context (with sender names and media) so the next mention knows what was said, without the bot replying.

f: All apps: follow-ups in threads the bot already joined
w: Threads the bot has replied in are remembered, so follow-ups there are answered without a fresh mention.

f: All apps: say who is speaking in shared group sessions
w: In shared group sessions each message is prefixed with the sender's name so the agent knows who is talking.

f: All apps: introduction when added to a group
w: When the bot joins a group (or a user subscribes) it posts one configurable introduction grounded in the room's title and description.

f: All apps: session keys per chat, thread, topic and user
w: One deterministic builder gives each DM, group member, thread or topic its own conversation (or a shared one by choice), persisted across restarts with readable aliases. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: route each chat, group, topic or thread to a chosen agent
w: Bindings by peer, parent, guild, team, roles, account or channel pick which agent answers each conversation (most specific wins), with a trace of why; the owner's DMs on every app can share one main conversation with the window. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: several bot accounts per app, each bound to its own agent
w: One gateway runs several bot accounts of the same app (e.g. two Telegram bots), each with its own credentials and owning agent.

f: All apps: per-channel model and system prompt overrides
w: A channel or thread can pin its own model, system prompt additions and auto-loaded skills, between a session override and the global default.
Per-channel hooks adjust run parameters after they are resolved (e.g. Feishu, GitHub).

f: All apps: continuity hint after a session reset
w: After a reset in a long-lived channel, the agent gets a note pointing at the previous session so it can recall it.

f: All apps: messages that arrive while busy: queue, interrupt or steer
w: Messages sent while the agent is working are queued, interrupt the run, or are steered into it, per setting; control commands (/stop, /approve) always get through. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: read receipts for queued follow-ups
w: Follow-up messages drained mid-turn still get their read-receipt reactions.

f: All apps: /cancel that bypasses the queue
w: /cancel is handled before queueing and stops the chat's running turn at once.

f: All apps: skip messages a newer turn already superseded
w: Out-of-order inbound messages are tagged, skipped or ignored so the agent does not answer something a newer turn replaced.

f: All apps: in-chat slash commands from one command catalog
w: Commands such as /new, /reset, /status, /model, /stop, /help work inside every chat app from one shared catalog. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: session idle reset and max age
w: The owner chooses when a chat's conversation resets: after an idle period or a maximum age, per thread.

f: All apps: wait for messages split in two (inbound debounce)
w: Bursts of short messages from the same chat (and long pastes the app split) are merged into one turn after a quiet window, keeping order. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: drop redelivered and duplicate inbound messages
w: A bounded cache (in-process or shared SQL across pods) of seen message ids drops platform retries and duplicate events, including Slack unfurl duplicates.

f: All apps: suppress a duplicate reply to the same message
w: An identical second reply to the same inbound message is dropped.

f: All apps: photos, files and voice notes in, with size limits
w: Inbound attachments are downloaded with byte and time caps, cached safely, inlined as model input (images, documents) and can wait to join the follow-up question. Applies to every connected chat app.
Allowed URLs in messages (including hidden link targets) are fetched with limits and summarized into context.

f: All apps: quoted message added to context
w: When someone replies to an earlier message, the quoted message is fetched and added so the agent sees what is referenced.

f: All apps: message timestamps in model context
w: Inbound messages carry a readable timestamp in the model context without changing what is stored.

f: All apps: platform chat and sender context
w: Room metadata and sender identity (handles, aliases, account labels) are injected separately from the transcript.
Shared pins, venues and live locations become text the agent can use; outbound locations are sent where supported (Telegram, others).

f: All apps: reactions, edits, joins and pokes reach the agent
w: Non-message events (reactions on the bot's messages, edits, membership changes, QQ pokes, friend requests) are normalized, authorized and delivered to the agent and plugins.

f: All apps: edited messages are answered in their newest version
w: When the person edits a message before or during the reply, the newest version supersedes the old one (Telegram edits, Discord MESSAGE_UPDATE, Slack message_changed, Matrix edits).
The agent can send native polls (Telegram, Matrix, Teams Adaptive Cards) and read the results.

f: All apps: native formatting per app from one Markdown model
w: Replies are parsed once into text plus style/link spans and rendered natively per app (Telegram HTML, Slack mrkdwn, Signal ranges, Matrix HTML, WhatsApp), with a plain-text fallback, chosen live per app. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: long replies split at paragraph breaks, code fences never broken
w: Long replies go out as several messages at paragraph or sentence boundaries within each app's limit, merging tiny blocks and never leaving a code block open. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: very long replies as an image or merged-forward message
w: Replies over a threshold are rendered to an image or folded into a merged-forward message (QQ) to avoid flooding.

f: All apps: human-like pauses between message parts
w: Multi-part replies can be split and sent with natural or random delays so they read like typing.

f: All apps: portable message cards (buttons, selects, forms, charts, tables)
w: One semantic presentation (cards, buttons, selects, forms, follow-ups, charts, tables) is rendered natively by each app or degraded to text within limits. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: clarify questions as buttons with a text fallback
w: When the agent asks the person to choose, options appear as native buttons (Telegram, Discord, Slack); any failure falls back to a numbered text list, and expiry is handled. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: answer a question by reacting with a number
w: On apps without buttons (WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage) people answer a 1-4 option question by reacting with a number emoji.

f: All apps: tool approvals in chat, with /approve and /deny fallback
w: Risky actions ask in the chat with shared wording (what, why, silence means no) as native buttons bound to the request, or /approve and /deny where there are no buttons; only authorized people can answer. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: approvals by emoji reaction
w: On WhatsApp, Signal and Matrix an approval is answered by reacting, limited to the requester.

f: All apps: model picker in chat
