w: /model opens a picker (provider, then model) as Telegram inline keyboards, Discord select menus or Slack Block Kit menus, and the choice is saved per chat.

f: All apps: send files and images back as native attachments
w: Files the agent makes (charts, PDFs, audio, images) are sent as native attachments after a path safety check, from MEDIA tags or bare paths in the reply, including files on a remote sandbox. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: expiring file links for platforms that fetch by URL
w: Local files are served under expiring tokens so platforms and TTS can fetch media by URL.

f: All apps: usage footer on replies
w: An optional footer (model, context use, latency) on final replies, per app, toggled with /footer.
When the agent's whole answer is a silence marker, nothing is sent while history still records the turn.

f: All apps: quote-reply and @-mention the sender
w: Replies quote the message they answer (with a first/all/off mode for multi-part answers) and can @-mention the sender in groups; optional reply prefix/suffix. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: choose what reaches the chat (progress, tool hints, reasoning)
w: Global and per-app switches decide whether progress, tool hints, model reasoning and compaction notices are shown in chat apps.

f: All apps: diagnostics kept apart from answers
w: Engine warnings and service notices are classified separately so chats can mute or route them without hiding real replies.

f: All apps: what the person sees when a turn fails
w: On errors the chat gets a configurable hint, the error, or nothing.

f: All apps: notices that delete themselves
w: Short system notices are deleted after a time on apps that allow deleting messages.

f: All apps: replies stream into one message, edited in place
w: The answer streams into a single message that is edited at a throttled rate (or a native draft/stream where the app has one), with fences closed in previews, think blocks hidden, overflow split and no duplicate final. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: one progress message with step lines, edited in place
w: While working, one quiet message shows the status line and tool steps (with per-app level: off/new/all/verbose), rolls to a new message when too long, and the answer is its own message; SMS gets none and phone-first apps get a summary line. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: remove progress messages once the answer lands
w: Opt-in deletion of tool-progress messages after the final reply so the chat keeps only the answer.

f: All apps: friendly status phrases for long turns
w: Long turns show short human status lines from a catalog the owner can extend, never quoting tool arguments.
If a running turn shows no activity for a while, the chat gets a stall notice that clears when work resumes.
One pinned message, edited in place, shows the agent's tasks and plan as a sidebar substitute (Telegram /tasks, Slack summaries).

f: All apps: typing indicator while working
w: The app's typing indicator is shown and refreshed during a turn, with modes and a timeout so a stuck turn does not type forever. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: status reactions on the person's message
w: An acknowledgement emoji on receipt, then reactions that cycle queued, thinking, tool, done or error (tapbacks on iMessage). Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: bot presence shows health
w: The bot's online status shows healthy, degraded or rate-limited so people can see when the agent is unavailable.

Inbound events are journaled before they are acknowledged, drained in order with retries and ownership claims, and dead letters can be inspected and resubmitted, so nothing is lost or handled twice. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: durable delivery ledger for replies
w: Each reply is recorded pending, attempting, delivered or failed; a crash before the app confirms redelivers it in order, ambiguous resends are marked, dead letters can be retried, and a turn ends when delivery is confirmed. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: retry sends with backoff
w: Failed sends retry on a backoff ladder (honouring Retry-After) but stop on errors marked permanent.

f: All apps: catch up on messages missed while offline
w: After downtime the gateway finds messages sent meanwhile (history scan or persisted cursor), deduplicates them and answers once, while an age fence suppresses stale backlog.
Chats proven unreachable (bot removed, group deleted) are skipped by scheduled delivery until a later send succeeds.

f: All apps: send, edit, react and delete across apps (message tool)
w: One agent tool lists targets and sends text or files to any connected chat, edits or deletes its own earlier messages, reacts, pins and reads channels; scripts can post too. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: directory of reachable chats
w: The gateway keeps a refreshed map of reachable channels and contacts with friendly names, used to resolve targets.

f: All apps: home channel and delivery targets for scheduled output
w: Scheduled and background output goes to an explicit chat, the app's home channel (/sethome), the origin chat or a file, landing in the right thread; friendly aliases and email delivery included.

f: All apps: record what was sent into the target chat's history
w: When the agent sends into another chat, that chat's transcript records it so the agent there knows.

f: All apps: wake the chat when background work finishes
w: Background processes and delegations resume the owning chat session when they complete.

f: All apps: escalate to the owner across apps until acknowledged
w: An unacknowledged message escalates to the owner across ordered channels with retries until seen.

f: All apps: draft a reply and hand it to the owner for approval
w: The agent drafts a reply to a chosen message and sends it at once or holds it for owner approval.

f: All apps: install a messenger into a workspace and push into chats
w: Install the bot into Slack, Discord, Telegram or WeChat workspaces via OAuth or link tokens and push resources into chats.

f: All apps: pair a device from chat
w: /pair in chat creates a setup code for the phone app and lets the owner approve pending devices; the desktop hosts a hub phones connect to by QR.

f: All apps: guided setup with credential checks
w: Each app has an in-window setup: credential fields, live validation with clear progress and errors, and enable switches. Applies to every connected chat app.

f: All apps: chat apps from the command line
w: Commands to list, configure, start, stop and log in to chat apps (including QR logins) with schema-checked config and secret redaction.

f: All apps: bot list with per-bot logs and status
w: Create, enable and disable bots and read each bot's own log; the owner can ask for connector status from chat.

f: All apps: one-click app creation by QR (Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, WeCom)
w: Instead of copying app ids and secrets, the owner scans a QR code and the platform app is created and its credentials filled in.

f: All apps: QR login for phone-linked accounts (WhatsApp, WeChat)
w: Interactive QR login sessions shown in the window (with steps, connected and error states) that save credentials when the scan completes.

f: All apps: third-party chat frontends authenticate as a client app
w: Registered client apps act for a user identified by a phone number verified by OTP.

f: All apps: synthetic QA channel for testing
w: A deterministic fake channel lets automated tests drive the real channel plugin boundary with inspectable state.

f: All apps: several agents answer in one group
w: One group message can fan out to several configured agents, each in its own session, selected by mention, with a bounded number of follow-up rounds and names shown on replies.

f: All apps: channel doctor, probe and security audit
w: Per-app health checks probe credentials and connectivity, list status issues with fixes, and audit the app's security settings (open DMs, wildcard allowlists).

f: All apps: remember sent messages so replies to them keep context
w: A local index of what the bot sent (and WhatsApp received) by message id lets a reply to an earlier rich message recover its text and attachments, which Telegram and WhatsApp do not echo back.

f: All apps: hand a window conversation off to a chat app
w: /handoff moves the current conversation to a chat app (Telegram, Discord) so it continues there.
Telegram bot over polling or webhook with photos, video, voice, documents, locations, reply context, proxy support and per-chat state.

f: Telegram: durable polling, single poller and liveness watchdog
w: Long polling runs in a worker that spools every update durably before acknowledging it, keeps the read position per bot (surviving update renumbering), holds a single-poller lease per token, handles 409 conflicts and rebuilds on stalls; the after-restart backlog is marked as catch-up.
Updates arrive through a gateway-hosted webhook instead of polling, refusing updates without a secret token.

f: Telegram: flood control and send pacing
w: A per-chat one-per-second budget paces sends and edits (interim edits skipped, finals never), waits out retry_after, backs off on 5xx, and edits more slowly in groups.

f: Telegram: network fallback when the API host is unreachable
w: When api.telegram.org cannot be reached, requests retry known IPv4 addresses with the hostname kept, using DNS-over-HTTPS discovery.

f: Telegram: live draft streaming and progress drafts
w: Replies stream into a preview message (or Telegram's native sendMessageDraft in DMs) in off/partial/block/progress modes, so only the final message notifies.

f: Telegram: forum topics and DM topics as separate chats
w: Each forum topic (and bot DM topic via /topic) is its own session, with topic create/rename, model-generated topic names, persisted bindings and pruning.
In groups the bot answers when @mentioned, replied to, addressed by /cmd@bot (ignoring /cmd@otherbot) or in free-response topics; reply chains in normal groups stay one conversation.
The '/' menu is filled from the command list per scope (default, private, groups, owner DM) within Telegram's limits, refreshed only when changed; /start gets a proper welcome.
Typing @bot <query> in any chat searches every command and skill with paging; tapping one sends it.

f: Telegram: rich formatting (HTML, tables, task lists, math)
w: Markdown becomes Telegram HTML, with tables, task lists, details and math sent as rich blocks where available and plain-text fallback.
Approvals show as inline buttons (once, session, always, deny) bound to the request; clicks are authorization-checked and fail closed.

f: Telegram: photo albums read as one message
w: Photos sent as an album, with their captions, become one message to the agent.

f: Telegram: photos, files and documents in and out
w: Inbound documents and images are cached with size limits (large images compressed); outbound photos go as photos and documents up to 50 MB as files.
Incoming stickers (including animated) are described once by a vision model and cached; sticker packs can be added.

f: Telegram: voice bubbles versus audio files
w: Spoken replies go out as native voice-note bubbles with duration; other audio as files; inbound voice notes are cached for transcription.
/dashboard in a DM opens the full control UI inside Telegram as a Mini App, owner-checked from Telegram's signed init data.

f: Telegram: follow a group upgraded to a supergroup
w: When a group migrates to a supergroup (migrate_to_chat_id), bindings, allowlists and sessions move to the new chat id.

f: Telegram: read-only history from a personal account
w: Identity-verified personal Telegram clients serve read-only chat history with owner policy checked per page.
Discord bot for servers and DMs with channel gating, bot-to-bot policy, forwarded messages, attachments, reply-to and typing.

Commands and skills register as Discord application commands with argument menus, synced by fingerprint with rate-limit pacing and role checks, including a model picker that remembers per-user choices.
A channel message can start a thread named by the model; each thread is its own conversation and bindings persist.

f: Discord: mention gating and free-response channels
w: In servers the bot needs a mention (also inside threads) except in free-response channels; ignored and no-thread channels are configurable.

f: Discord: Components v2 buttons, selects and modals
w: Agent messages use Discord components (buttons, selects, modals, embeds) and interactions route back to the agent.
An 'Open widget' button launches an agent-made HTML widget inside a Discord Activity, gated by Discord OAuth.
A reply streams into one Discord message edited as chunks arrive, never splitting surrogate pairs.
Approvals render as Discord button views (once, session, always, deny), can mention the owner, and accept clicks only from authorized users.
Access can be granted by Discord role or username, resolved to ids and reloaded live.
Outbound messages block @everyone, @here and role pings by default.

f: Discord: long messages, escaping and forum posts
w: Long replies split losslessly under Discord's cap (code fences, surrogates), markdown is escaped, and replies to forum channels create forum posts.
Inbound images, audio and documents are downloaded with size caps; files go out as attachments.

f: Discord: gateway liveness and close-code handling
w: Health comes from the gateway socket's heartbeat state; fatal close codes stop with a plain card (e.g. turn on Message Content intent), zombies RESUME, and REST rate limits are kept per bucket.

f: Discord: server management and moderation actions
w: Gated actions create/edit channels, categories and roles, set permissions, assign roles, create invites and moderate (timeouts, kicks, bans).
Proxied PluralKit messages resolve to the real member so allowlists and identity work for plural systems.
Agent audio is sent as a native Discord voice message with waveform and duration.

f: Discord: voice channel join, listen and talk
w: The bot joins a voice channel, transcribes each speaker separately and plays spoken replies, with idle timeouts.

f: Discord: use the desktop app without a bot token
w: Connects to the local Discord desktop app over RPC to read messages and reply through UI automation.
Slack app for channels, DMs and threads with ingress and bot policies, thread replies, user-mention resolution and reaction acknowledgement.

f: Slack: Socket Mode, HTTP and relay transports with a watchdog
w: Connects by Socket Mode, HTTP request URLs, or a relay that owns the single socket and forwards typed events; a watchdog restarts stale sockets.
Replies stream through Slack's native streaming API as one message that becomes the final reply.

f: Slack: Block Kit and mrkdwn rendering
w: Replies render as Block Kit (headers, lists, buttons, selects) or mrkdwn with code kept exact; text fallback when blocks are rejected; <!channel>/<!here> made inert.
Chart and table blocks map to Slack's native data-visualization and table blocks.

f: Slack: assistant status, task cards and Agent View
w: In Slack's AI pane the bot shows live 'is thinking' status, per-tool progress or task cards, thread titles and suggested prompts; each composer message starts its own thread session.

f: Slack: thread context and proactive posts
w: When pulled into a thread the bot reads earlier thread messages; it can also post proactively to configured targets or feeds.

f: Slack: channel mention rules and DM policy
w: Channels answer on mention, mention-or-reply or everything, with group allowlists, and a separate DM policy that issues pairing codes.

f: Slack: approval buttons and model picker
w: Approvals and model choice post as Block Kit buttons/menus that only authorized users can use, updated in place.
Slack file attachments are downloaded (restricted to Slack hosts) and agent files uploaded back to the thread.

f: Slack: start a turn by reacting
w: Users can start a turn by reacting with chosen emoji.
Raw <@U...> mentions become readable names and the bot knows which one is itself.
Slack modals collect structured input and global/message shortcuts start agent actions; submitted values are summarized for the agent.
Org-wide installs resolve the right workspace and user for each event.

f: Slack: slash command and App Home
w: A Slack slash command (with argument menus) starts or steers sessions; !cmd works in threads; a safe App Home tab.

f: Slack: post as a real user
w: Optionally read and post as the human who authorized the app, or override display name and icon.
When a recent participant comes online the agent may send one short, memory-informed greeting with a long cooldown.

f: WhatsApp: personal number by QR (linked device)
w: Links a personal WhatsApp account as a linked device by QR, then sends and receives text, voice and media, quote-replies and handles LID identities.

f: WhatsApp: connection controller (reconnect, relink on logout)
w: Owns the socket lifecycle with reconnect backoff and credential persistence; 'logged out' or 'replaced by another session' asks to relink instead of looping.
Official WhatsApp Business webhooks with signature checks and Graph API sends.

f: WhatsApp: one identity for LID and phone ids
w: A person seen as a LID or a phone JID maps to one identifier so allowlists and sessions stay consistent.

f: WhatsApp: group activation and mention gating
w: Groups answer on mention or reply to the bot (or always, per group) with group allowlists and a one-time introduction.
Signal through a signal-cli daemon (JSON-RPC and SSE) with attachments, reactions, typing, quotes, groups and account-conflict detection.

f: Signal: signal-cli install, daemon and transports
w: Installs signal-cli if missing and supervises its daemon (QR-linked or registered number), or uses a REST container or UNIX socket, auto-detected.
Markdown becomes Signal text-style ranges (bold, italic, monospace) with long replies chunked without breaking styles and wide tables shown as key-value lines.
A token bucket mirrors Signal's per-account attachment limit and recalibrates from Retry-After.
Group messages are processed only when the bot is mentioned (configurable), with a separate lane for commands.

f: iMessage: on the Messages Mac (chat.db / imsg)
w: Reads Messages on the Mac (Full Disk Access) and sends replies, with contacts resolved and group/DM policies; blocked on Windows and Linux with the Mac prerequisites stated.

f: iMessage: from a non-Mac through BlueBubbles
w: iMessage through a BlueBubbles server on a Mac: REST sends, webhook inbound with media, typing and read receipts.
iMessage through hosted services: signed webhooks or a supervised sidecar stream, with device-code setup.

f: iMessage: tapbacks, effects, threaded replies and groups
w: With the private API the agent sends threaded replies, tapbacks, effects, polls and attachment replies and manages groups.

f: iMessage: approvals by poll or tapback
w: Approval requests show as iMessage polls or tapback prompts and resolve from the vote or reaction.
Any homeserver with E2EE, cross-signing bootstrap, recovery keys, device verification and key-backup health; supervises bridge bots.
Matrix threads are their own sessions with thread relations on replies; rooms answer on mention, open or allowlist.
Replies and steps stream by editing one m.notice (m.replace) and only the final edit notifies.
Markdown renders to Matrix HTML including tables, code and spoilers.
Room invites are accepted by policy so the bot can be added without manual joins.

f: Matrix: voice messages wait for the mention
w: Unmentioned voice messages in mention-gated rooms wait until the sender's follow-up mention claims them.
Teams DMs, group chats and channels through a Bot Framework webhook with token verification, in-thread replies, history, media and reactions.
Approvals render as Adaptive Cards and resolve from card submits.

f: Teams: file uploads by consent card
w: Files go to users via Teams' file-consent card in DMs and via Graph/SharePoint elsewhere; inbound attachments come through Graph.
Stored conversation references let the agent message Teams users and channels proactively.
Replies use Teams' streaming message protocol with full-redelivery fallback.

f: Teams: meeting summaries posted to Teams
w: The meeting pipeline posts meeting summaries through the same Teams app.
Google Chat app for DMs and spaces via signed HTTP webhooks or Pub/Sub, with Cards v2 replies, threads, attachments and reactions.

f: Google Chat: native attachments via per-user OAuth
w: Each user grants OAuth once so the bot can upload native attachments as that user.
Approvals show as Google Chat cards with buttons, updated when resolved.
Feishu/Lark bots for DMs and groups over WebSocket or encrypted webhook, with mention-gated groups, allowlists, per-chat serial processing, media and custom domains.
Replies stream into a CardKit card (typewriter effect, collapsible reasoning, tables split to card limits), falling back to a normal message.

f: Feishu/Lark: processing reactions and card approvals
