w: Edits to the agent's own config, rules and instruction files (and .git) always ask or stay read-only, even under broad allow.
Reads and writes of .env files, ~/.ssh, cloud credentials, the agent's credential files and other profiles' homes are refused or ask, except .env.example.
A gitignore-style file keeps chosen files out of tools and @-mentions.

f: Workspace boundary for file and shell tools
w: File and shell access outside the project folder asks or is refused; paths are canonicalised so symlinks cannot sneak out.
When the agent needs a path or network access it lacks, it asks; the user grants it for the session or permanently.

f: Safe upload, download and served-file paths
w: Uploaded, downloaded and served files cannot escape their folder through crafted names or traversal.
Writes refuse to follow planted symlinks and use create-exclusive files, so edits cannot land outside their root.
Opening an untrusted folder runs in a safe mode (no project settings, hooks, MCP servers or custom commands) until the user trusts it, after a scan of what it contains.

f: Re-approve project hooks and policy files when they change
w: Project hooks and policy files are hashed; new or changed ones need the user's approval before they take effect.

f: OS sandbox for commands (Seatbelt, bubblewrap, Landlock)
w: Each shell command runs in a kernel sandbox that limits writes to allowed folders and blocks network unless allowed.
On Windows, commands run under an AppContainer or restricted token with ACLs so the agent cannot reach beyond its folders.

f: Sandbox modes and named permission profiles
w: Pick read-only, workspace-write or full access, or named profiles describing folders, globs and network rules that can extend each other.

f: Run the whole app in a container or sandbox
w: The whole agent can be relaunched inside Docker, Podman, gVisor or a Seatbelt profile, optionally with an egress firewall.

f: Sandbox backends (Docker per agent, SSH, remote machines)
w: Tools run inside a container scoped per agent or session (no network, read-only root, capabilities dropped) or on a remote machine, with a file bridge.
Sessions, processes, disk and run time inside the sandbox are capped, failing closed.

f: Explain where tools run and why something is blocked
w: A command explains which sandbox a session's tools use and why an action was blocked.
Scripts that call several tools at once run inside a WebAssembly or V8 isolate.

f: Static checks on user code blocks
w: User code blocks are scanned for subprocess/exec-style calls and refused.

f: Scripts go through the same approval gate
w: Code sent to an execute-code tool passes the same approval checks as terminal commands.

f: Network allowlist proxy for sandboxed commands
w: Sandboxed commands reach the network only through a proxy that allows listed domains and can ask the user about new ones.
Network destinations in shell commands (curl, scp, git push, publish) are extracted and logged.
Agent fetches cannot reach private, loopback, link-local or metadata addresses; DNS is resolved once and pinned, and redirects are re-checked.
Browser navigation and new tabs are limited to allowed domains and blocked from listed ones, with wildcard and scheme matching.
Each browser action is classified (read, mutating, navigation, egress) and allowed or denied by policy before it runs.

f: Electron window, navigation and IPC hardening
w: Links open only to safe schemes, privileged windows cannot navigate away, IPC checks the sender frame and media permissions are granted only to trusted frames.
Agent-made HTML, MCP apps and previews render in opaque-origin sandboxes with a CSP.
Rendered model output passes an allow-list sanitiser with safe URL schemes.
External images in model output load only when the user clicks, since URLs can leak data.
Web surfaces send CSP and security headers built per deployment.
Web pages, tool results, MCP output and imported text are wrapped as untrusted data; commands whose flags came from untrusted text get extra review.

f: Neutralise fake system tags and role headers
w: Fake <system> tags, [SYSTEM]: headers and confirmation-bypass phrases in user or outside text are escaped so they read as text.
Invisible tag characters, control and direction-override characters are stripped and text normalised to block hidden injections.
Inputs, context files, memory and cron prompts are scanned for injection, jailbreak and social-engineering patterns, then blocked, warned, filtered or rewritten.
Attacker-controlled MCP JSON schemas are bounded in bytes, depth and nodes before compiling or rewriting.
Inputs or outputs are checked against harm categories with thresholds (model or provider API).
Configured words or regexes block or mask content on the way in or out.
User-supplied regexes run with size and CPU-time caps to prevent ReDoS.
Messages, files, memories and tool arguments are scanned for personal data and blocked, redacted or pseudonymised, with an audit trail.

f: Secret redaction in logs, prompts and tool output
w: Secrets and codes are masked in logs, model prompts, tool results, traces and artifacts.

f: Secret masking in API and config responses
w: Settings and config sent to the UI mask keys and URL secrets, and masked placeholders are swapped back on save.
Secrets split across streamed chunks are still masked before deltas leave the process.

f: Named secrets injected by reference and masked by value
w: Secrets are referenced by name ($NAME), injected only into the command that needs them, and every value is masked wherever it appears afterwards.

f: Secret placeholders at the model boundary
w: The model only sees placeholders for secrets; real values are substituted at action time.
A stored credential is released only to the site it belongs to, with warnings when domains do not match.

f: Inject credentials at the network edge
w: Sandboxes, coding agents and WASM add-ons hold only dummy values; the real credential is swapped in at egress for matching destinations.
Spawned commands and servers get a filtered environment without credentials or code-injection variables, with explicit passthrough.
The binary disables core dumps and ptrace and strips preload variables at start.
Secrets are bound only to the skills that declare them and stripped from child processes afterwards.
Remote workers get rotating short-lived credentials instead of long-lived secrets.
Config names secrets by reference (env, file, command, Bitwarden, 1Password, store) and resolves them in memory instead of storing values.
A command finds plaintext credentials in config and env and migrates them into secret references.

f: OS keychain storage with encrypted fallback
w: Tokens live in the OS keychain; if unavailable, an encrypted file is used, never reversible encoding.
Secrets are encrypted at rest (AES-GCM, key in the OS keychain) with access scoping and audit.
Credential files are written atomically with owner-only permissions.
The local database can be encrypted with SQLCipher.
A settings page creates, edits and deletes named secrets with descriptions, injected into the agent without revealing values.
Per-provider forms collect API keys or subscription files and warn about conflicts.
The agent asks for a credential through a trusted prompt that stores it directly; the model never sees it.
Sign-ins fill from a vault or password manager (Bitwarden, 1Password) at fill time; the model sees only which login exists.

f: Password-manager broker with reason and audit
w: Agents get a curated list of secrets and must give a reason; each fetch follows an approval policy and is audited.

f: Mask typed secrets and password fields
w: Values typed into password fields are detected and masked in recordings, previews and the UI.
Chat media are stored as file-id references instead of URLs that embed the bot token.
Auth headers survive redirects only on the same origin.
All HTTP clients use the operating system's certificate verifier.

f: Loopback-only by default; key required when exposed
w: Local servers bind to 127.0.0.1; exposing them beyond loopback requires a key or token, and loopback trust cannot be faked with forwarded headers.

f: WebSocket auth without keys in URLs
w: Socket connections authenticate with tickets or a first message, keeping keys out of URLs and logs.
Server sign-in works with JWT, OAuth/OIDC (PKCE) and providers like Auth0, Clerk or Supabase, chained as one composite check.

f: Gateway auth modes (token, password, trusted proxy)
w: The gateway uses a token, password or an identity-aware reverse proxy, and refuses ambiguous configs.

f: Host and Origin checks against DNS rebinding
w: Requests with an unexpected Host or Origin header are refused.
State-changing requests need a CSRF token.
A workspace-scoped HttpOnly cookie lets previews load files without headers, with path-based CORS.
Each device has its own key and must be approved; devices can be listed, rotated and revoked.

f: Auth failure rate limiting and bans
w: Failed sign-in attempts are rate-limited per IP and identity, and repeat offenders are banned.
Messages, uploads, tool calls and control writes are rate-limited per user, session or key.
API keys carry scopes, are shown once, stored as digests and can be revoked.
Channels and schedulers call the gateway with signed internal headers.
Auth can be disabled only by explicit opt-in for local use, refused in production.
The server checks which options a client may set per session.
The server can reject new queries while one is running.

f: One client gateway for engine calls
w: All UI-to-engine calls go through typed adapters, enforced by a test.
A first-run owner account with strong password hashing, sessions and admin password reset.
Authenticator-app codes with recovery codes protect sign-in or chosen actions.
Register, name, delete and sign in with passkeys.
The account password can be reset with an instance recovery key.
Turnstile protects login and registration.
New sign-ups stay pending until an admin approves them.
Every query and thread is filtered by owner, so one user never sees another's data.
Roles and groups (owner, admin, member, viewer) map to fine-grained permissions enforced on every route.
Admins per bot or group may run privileged commands and tools; others get a denial.
Every API method is classified into scopes and callers are checked against them, failing closed.

f: Authorization gate for tools, skills and models
w: A pluggable authorization layer filters denied tools, skills and models before the model sees them and re-checks at execution.
Agents, prompts, files and documents are shared with users or groups as viewer, editor or owner.
A sender's effective role (owner, admin, user, guest) is resolved from one rank table.
The owner links a chat account with a one-time code; only that account counts as the owner.
Edit locks stop conflicting concurrent edits.

f: Audit log of admin and permission events
w: Admin actions and permission decisions are recorded.
Each rule records its source so the UI can say why a call was auto-approved or denied.

f: Pairing codes for unknown chat senders
w: Unknown senders get an expiring code and are ignored until the owner approves them.

f: Sender allowlists and DM / group policies
w: Per message, one admission check decides whether a sender or group may reach the agent (pairing, allowlist, open, disabled).
Named sender lists are defined once and referenced from any channel allowlist.
Replies stop when two bots ping-pong or the bot hears its own reflected output.
Repeated no-progress tool calls and argument churn are detected and the run is stopped.
Agents owned by different people talk over an encrypted channel screened by a pinned model.

f: Spoken confirmation for risky voice actions
w: High-impact actions requested by voice need a spoken confirmation bound to the run.
If a voice session fails a safety check, queued voice hand-offs are retired.
Webhooks are signature-verified with replay protection before processing.

f: Safety-check pipeline before every tool call
w: Every tool call from every entry point runs through ordered checks (security, egress, permission, repetition, custom checkers) that allow, ask or deny; a failing check denies.
Skills and plugins are scanned before install (secrets, exfiltration, shell, obfuscation, invisible Unicode) and blocked or held for review.

f: Scan agent writes for secrets and risky code
w: Content the agent writes to files or memory is scanned for credentials and dangerous code.
npm and PyPI packages launched as extensions or MCP servers are checked against OSV malware advisories.
On demand, installed packages are checked against OSV and known-compromised versions.
A command checks config, channels, file permissions, plugins and exec rules, and fixes what it can.

f: Add-on install consent and declared permissions
w: Installing or updating an add-on shows what it adds and may do and asks for consent; undeclared permissions are never granted.
Plugin code can pause a tool call until the user approves it.
Add-on archives are verified against trusted publisher keys and install records are tamper-checked.
The updater verifies signatures before installing.
Shell snippets in skill files run only for trusted skills, behind one approval and a kill switch.

f: Tool profiles per agent, mode and chat surface
w: Each agent, mode, skill or sandbox gets a defined tool set; high-risk tools are denied by default on remote surfaces.
Sub-agents inherit the parent's deny rules and boundaries and can never gain more.
An administrator layer (file, MDM or cloud) constrains modes, sandboxing, models and MCP servers and cannot be changed by users or the agent.
Hide models that may train on prompts and show what each provider receives.
All model traffic and spawned coding agents go through one configured gateway.
The user takes control; the agent stops, records what the user did, and resumes when handed back.

f: Agent asks for help when blocked
w: A task enters a needs-help state so the user can reply or take over.
Accessibility, Screen Recording and other OS permissions are checked and requested before desktop control.
Desktop actions are checked against a policy; sensitive ones wait for explicit approval.
Distracting sites and apps are blocked via the hosts file, a local VPN or Safari content blockers.
Trades and payments follow a policy (venue, amount, rate) and need a separate yes.
Startup checks TEE attestation before releasing secrets.
Certain actions need a device-bound biometric proof.

f: Retry responses held by safety buffering
w: Responses held by server-side safety show a status and offer a retry.
Signed-in users may see server-driven security reminders.
Git calls override core.fsmonitor so a repo cannot run a helper program.
An attacker model is trained to social-engineer target models.
A threat model organised by MITRE ATLAS tactics with risks and recommendations.
Advisory-derived static rules run in CI to block security regressions.

f: Replies must be grounded in real effects
w: Replies claiming a completed action without recorded evidence are blocked or corrected.

f: Audience check before disclosing private data
w: Private details are only sent when the room's attested audience may see them.
When the agent needs a secret or payment, it picks a safe delivery channel.
Trust profiles are computed from evidence per entity.
A user can temporarily elevate permissions, which expire.

f: Exact-preview one-time approval for outbound effects
w: Sends, writes and payments are approved against an exact preview; the approval is one-time, bound to actor and content, and rejected if anything changes.

f: Outbound sanitiser for leaked reasoning and tool syntax
w: Thinking tags and tool-call markup are stripped before replies reach a chat app.
Model-generated SQL is checked so mutations cannot hide in comments or literals.
Only the scopes a capability needs are requested.
Writes to a file the agent has not read at its current version are blocked.
Each message carries an immutable scope enforced at model and tool level.
Each agent has its own folder and memory; access to another agent's memory is hard-denied by a kernel sandbox.
Each profile resolves its own credentials; unscoped reads fail.
Each message carries the human who sent it so credits and memory go to the sender.
Agent writes to memory or skills can be prompted or staged for review.

f: Waiting on a human is accounted separately
w: Time blocked on an approval is excluded from tool deadlines.
Grouped prompts support all, skip all and don't-ask-again.

f: Inspect the effective policy and dry-run a command
w: Commands show the effective policy and what would happen to a command without running it.
One-click presets set permission levels (hands-off vs careful).
Each agent has a permission form.

f: Delete a user's data across services
w: Deleting an account removes data across all services.

f: Connection role binding and session isolation
w: Each connection is bound to its role; spoofed roles and session reuse are refused.
Text sent to the system speech command is stripped of shell metacharacters.
IDs are generated with a cryptographically secure source.

f: Language detection and translation of input
w: Input language is detected and optionally translated.
The number of bots, pipelines and knowledge bases is capped per edition.
An integration has a none/read/write toggle.
Terminal routes need a step-up token.
Credential bindings carry versions so stale ones are detected.

f: Owner opt-in before using the real browser
w: Controlling the user's real browser needs an owner-only grant file.

f: Safe launch of local tool servers
w: Local MCP servers launch only allow-listed commands, inside the sandbox, with risky flags refused.

Every yes is bound to a fingerprint of the exact request (tool plus canonical JSON arguments, keyed per launch), names the question it answers, is used once, and re-runs through the same gate; a refused or stale yes is spent, and an approved program launch or remote command cannot turn into a different one (serialised arguments, unwrapped wrappers).

f: Shared safety layer: re-check authority after every await
w: Owner, profile, App lock, Lockdown and config are re-checked after every await and right before each side effect, using monotonic revisions and run generations, so stale work never acts.

f: Shared safety layer: caller identity and local-only actions
w: Each request's caller is resolved once; keys are bound to one conversation and device, risky control changes (Lockdown off, webhooks, people) only come from the local window, the window proves it is talking to the real engine, and viewing sessions and phone-capability lending use one-use, expiring grants bound to owner, profile, device and action.

f: Shared safety layer: household profile scoping
w: Household profiles read only allow-listed routes, see and steer only their own tasks, cannot write to owner stores, and get scoped usage and exports.

f: Shared safety layer: content never grants authority
w: Forwarded, quoted, copied, exported or persona-written text never changes who is speaking or what is allowed; engine nudges are never treated as the owner's words.

f: Shared safety layer: secret scrubbing everywhere
w: Secrets are redacted before truncation, never appear in audit records, URLs, outside-agent messages or unmaskable media, credentials needed in URLs are built and stripped in one place, and problem reports are opt-in, previewed and redacted.

f: Shared safety layer: no duplicate or replayed side effects
w: Triggers claim jobs atomically, inbound events are deduplicated before any effect, interrupted work is settled rather than replayed, uncertain sends are reconciled, and only the agent's own delivered messages can be edited.

f: Shared safety layer: outside-started work is capped
w: Work started from chat apps, triggers, schedules, voice or paired senders starts no looser than Ask first with a restricted tool list; only the owner's verified direct chat is an exception.

f: Shared safety layer: chat-app identity and owner authority
w: A chat account is the owner only when the owner named it; owner commands need a live direct chat, edits count only from the original sender, and an email sender is an identity only with aligned DMARC/SPF/DKIM.

f: Shared safety layer: automation only narrows permissions
w: Unattended steps, nested flows, replayed procedures and resumed work get their own capped yes and inherit only the intersection of permissions; per-rule options may tighten but never loosen.

f: Shared safety layer: settings fail closed and loosening asks
w: Unreadable settings count as off, damaged key files re-ask, loosening changes (including numeric ones) need explicit confirmation and are refused under Lockdown, model tools cannot reach gateway and update settings, stale proposals are refused, and only one app instance may open a data folder.

f: Shared safety layer: bounded inputs and honest truncation
w: Every external read, archive and import is size-, count- and time-bounded and checked before inflating; anything cut off is reported as incomplete; only an explicit 400/413 counts as a context overflow and learned limits only go down.

f: Shared safety layer: spend caps fail conservative
w: Incomplete spend totals refuse against the cap, unknown prices stop the next round, and helper model calls use the task's own budget and cancellation.

f: Shared safety layer: complete deletion and data lifecycle
w: Deleting removes every derived record through one path, 'delete everything' is all-or-nothing with secure delete, deleted items stay deleted after a backup restore, temporary chats never persist, and backups exclude credentials.

f: Shared safety layer: screen and browser control
w: Capture is pinned to the chosen display and excludes the agent's windows, input is bound to the frame the agent saw, ambiguous clicks press nothing, raw CDP is never exposed, and control hand-overs are serialised.

f: Shared safety layer: update and release identity
w: Updates are accepted only with proven identity (strict tags, matching versions, exact commit), never downgrade on channel switch, publish only after verification, keep signing keys out of PR code, and only the owner's local window can adopt one.

f: Shared safety layer: delegated coding agents stay boxed
w: Delegated coding agents get no shell of their own (a single-job local door instead), no tools for non-owner tasks, and stop if their isolated worktree cannot be proven.
One switch (Settings, mode menu, palette, Ctrl+Shift+L) that makes everything ask, turns off everything that reaches outside, holds on every surface, and shows a banner.
A PIN lock that refuses almost every request while locked, cancels in-flight owner work, rate-limits unlock attempts and needs the current PIN to change.
One control stops or pauses every Trunk at once and resumes them.

Branch edits itself only for the owner (never household, keys or chat apps), tests each change in isolation with rollback, pushes only to recorded repos, merges only on the exact checked head, and stops under Lockdown.
Switch person, PINs, roles, invites and per-person live views; household people see, steer and stop only their own Trunks.
New Trunks and rooms start on Ask first with consistent mode words, and restored Trunks come back paused and look-only until the owner restores their access.
What runs without asking (reading Documents, browsing, recording) and what always asks (sending, deleting many files, spending, installing, screen control, sign-ins); Full access is never shipped on.

f: Approval outcomes: hand off to me, only if I asked
w: Two extra rule outcomes: the Trunk prepares a step and hands it to the owner, or it runs only when the owner's own message asked for exactly this.
One page with Without asking, Pinned settings, Rules, Checks, Isolation and Locks sections.

f: Egress guard for secrets in outbound URLs
w: Outbound addresses carrying a secret (whole, fragment or encoded) or bursts of unique URLs are flagged and held for an owner yes in every mode.
Mail clients establish TLS or required STARTTLS before sending credentials; plain is loopback-only.
Remote computers are refused if their host key changed.

f: Scoped exposure as an MCP / A2A server
w: With sharing off, nothing is listed or callable; with sharing on, only the shared tools and their resources are reachable, server-initiated requests need a live owner dialog, and pairing links never carry the app key.

f: Local-only mode never falls back to the cloud
w: A conversation marked 'stays on this computer' never routes to a cloud model.

f: Disabled add-ons are inert; add-on UI is plain data
w: Inspecting a disabled plugin never runs its code, hooks of disabled skills never fire, and plugin UI contributions are namespaced data with no executable HTML.

f: Tamper-evident activity chain and tool receipts
w: A hash chain over the activity record plus signed receipts for successful tool calls that detect modified results.
A public SECURITY.md with GitHub private vulnerability reporting switched on.
Tests taken from upstream advisories covering path policy, sandbox walls, Windows 8.3 short names and rate-limit isolation.

f: Share a conversation as a page
w: Share one conversation as a page with keys blanked and a receipt of what went out, served on this computer only.
Connecting to a KeepOak team workspace needs an approval code; members, seats and shared Trunks.

One checklist of the seven Mac permissions with real status pills and the one button that changes each; asked the moment a feature needs it, re-checked on return, Restart to finish for Screen Recording, and Open System Settings after a refusal.
Old Branch CI, test, doctor and CLI issues.
A lasting, scrubbed startup log.

f: Misplaced: run limits and history repair
w: Run time limits, queued follow-ups, tool output caps and history repair.
Gemini tool-result names and Vertex AI sign-in.
A finished reply behind the composer; Recents stays empty.

f: Misplaced: chat delivery and router split
w: Replied-while-queued status and splitting the chat router.
Evaluation page honesty, isolated evaluation workspace and stale-file grading.
Atomic profile replacement and reusable signed-in browser state.
Validate JSON after write operations.
GardenBook.seeds() reads only the newest 300 seeds.
Collaborative project comments and labels.

f: Misplaced: several humans and bots in one room
w: Presence, invite into a session, hand-off.

f: Misplaced: Codex app-server approval reply shape
w: Codex permission approval replies must send {permissions, scope}.
Runs terminal-bench style tasks (via Harbor) against the agent and other harnesses, and classifies failures from the results.
Runs the agent on coding exercises in many languages inside Docker throwaway folders with chosen model and edit format, then summarises pass rates.
Tabulates benchmark runs per model and task, finds the hardest tasks and charts results over time.
Adapters connect the agent to many public benchmarks, and a resumable campaign runner executes suites across harnesses and providers for head-to-head scores.
Runs tasks in one or more parallel OSWorld VMs (VMware, Docker, AWS, Azure, GCP or VirtualBox) with configurable steps, screen size and result directories.
Scripts and datasets to run and score WebVoyager tasks with task v2.
An eval script indexes the FRAMES Wikipedia knowledge base, runs questions through Khoj chat modes and grades answers with an LLM judge, tracking accuracy and cost; runnable from a CI workflow.
Real-model evals check the agent picks the right actions (tools, delegation, safety) with pass policies, run nightly and on PRs, with early stop on clear failure.

f: Scenario runner against a live runtime
w: Scripted scenarios (seeds, clock, messages, actions) run against the real running app and check assertions end to end.
Scripts inventory evals, compute coverage per tool category and policy, validate eval files, and produce regression reports.
Build evaluators from preprocess, analyze, score and reason steps (code or LLM judge), attach them to agents and workflows, and scaffold prebuilt ones.
Prebuilt LLM judges score faithfulness, relevancy, hallucination, rubrics and whole conversations, optionally with majority vote.
Deterministic scorers for completeness, content similarity, keyword coverage, textual difference, tone and checks.
Score whether the agent called the right tools in the right order, via code or LLM judging.
After a run, a judge decides from the trajectory (and screenshots) whether the task was really completed.
Captions each before/after screenshot pair with the executed mouse action marked to produce factual behaviour narratives of a run.
Prompts a model to judge a goal's review state and suggestions, rejecting unknown enum values and bounding goal/evidence graphs.

f: Eval pass thresholds and CI gates
w: Scorers declare pass thresholds so CI gates can fail builds on regressions.
expect-style matchers and a Vitest reporter run evals as unit tests in CI.
Versioned datasets of inputs and expected outputs run against agents as experiments with scorers and traces, from code, UI or CLI.
Captures tool calls from traces and replays them as mocks during experiments, aborting on mismatches.

f: Score stored traces after the fact
w: Runs scorers over stored traces after the fact via a scoring workflow.
Scorers grade coding sessions on outcome and efficiency, classifying executed commands.

f: Learning signals from runs and feedback
w: Feedback, reactions and corrections from runs become structured signals that drive learning.
Turns thumbs-down feedback on a bot reply (e.g. Teams feedback buttons) into a rate-limited reflection turn where the agent records a learning and optionally follows up.
Real model requests and responses are recorded and replayed deterministically to regression-test the agent across providers.
HTTP proxy that injects provider-specific errors, including in streams, to test retry and error handling.

Generates recall questions from the region compaction will drop, runs ContextCompressor under several policies, asks a fresh LLM using only post-compaction context and scores recall vs tokens retained.
Runs the same seeded tasks against two git refs or builds and recomputes cost, cache and tool friction to compare them.
Benchmark runner comparing raw, markdown, Readability and optimised page extraction strategies on time, length and token count.
Benchmarks browser MCP server tool latency.
Static and runtime benchmark of how easily an agent can resolve symbols across the repo's facade/sibling module layout.
Past runs are flattened into per-call records and exported as JSONL, CSV, ShareGPT or RL-ready formats.
Post-processes trajectories into a token budget by protecting head and tail turns and summarizing only as many middle turns as needed without splitting tool call/response pairs.
Runs the agent over a prompt dataset in parallel with checkpoint and resume to generate training trajectories.
Python GRPO trainer pulling scored trajectory batches from an Atropos server, with KL control, checkpointing and vLLM serving, plus JSON trajectory import.
Supervised fine-tuning that computes delight = loss x surprisal per example and only backpropagates the hard cases.

f: Learn from other agents' history (Claude Code, Codex)
w: Normalizes past coding-agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex and others) into trajectory-v1 JSON so memory workers can review, list, view and search them.
Runs GEPA prompt optimization against planner cases with caller-owned scoring and reflection, recording wire traffic and proving source provenance, without auto-activating results.

Serves authenticated, versioned prompt artifacts (vN.json plus MAC sidecars, five retained versions) to runtime consumers; setPrompt validates and activates, rollback swaps to predecessors, and absent artifacts fall back to the caller's baseline.
Experimentation providers gate prompt variants, LLM configs and engine arms per org/run.
The agent creates and patches its own SKILL.md skills (and supporting files) through a tool with path safety and validation.
skill_manage accepts up to 20 create/patch/write_file/remove_file ops validated up front and applied atomically via staging.

f: Skill write guards and origin provenance
w: Guards refuse unsafe skill_manage actions: background-review edits without a prior read or to pinned/non-agent skills, curator-consolidation deletes, writes to org-mirror skills (auto-proposing an org edit) and delete targets that escape or redirect out of the skills root.

f: Redirect where new skills are written
w: skills.create_dir sends agent-created skills to a chosen directory (e.g. a synced repo) instead of ~/.hermes/skills.
A bundled skill (or mode) guides the agent to author, validate and package new skills, with eval runs to measure them.
/learn turns a file, URL, pasted notes or the conversation into a reusable skill.
A review pass reads recorded trajectories and drafts a skill only when a reusable multi-step procedure was performed; candidates wait for approval.
After a turn (or when a session goes idle), a forked restricted agent reviews the conversation and saves memory or skill improvements.

f: Review cost controls and model routing
w: auxiliary.background_review lets the review run on a cheaper model, cap input tokens, disable itself, add narrowly scoped extra tools and set reasoning effort.

f: Idle-deferred review queue on local GPU
w: On the managed local llama-server, reviews are queued (one slot per session, newest wins) and dispatched when the GPU is idle or the item ages out, so learning doesn't fight live turns.
Optional display.memory_notifications surfaces a short summary of what the review saved (memory/skill changes) to CLI, TUI and gateway.
Governed path where agents or operators create skill proposals (content, target binding, scanner state, hashes, rollback metadata) that become live only when applied.

When the agent finds a used skill wrong or incomplete, it drafts a targeted fix in the same turn; prepare_patch authorizes one exact unique span with bounded context so the following patch can edit skills too large to read whole.
Agent-created skills move active, stale and archived by usage; nothing is deleted, pins are honoured, and a periodic review runs on its own.
A forked auxiliary agent reviews the skill library and may pin, archive, merge or patch skills via skill_manage, rewriting cron skill references and producing per-run reports with rename maps.
`hermes curator` status, run, pause/resume, pin/unpin, list/adopt unmanaged, archive/restore, prune and purge archives, backup, ledger, rollback and usage.
Before any automated change the skills (and memory) are snapshotted, and a rollback restores them.
Every skill mutation appends a JSONL entry with content-addressed before/after manifests; any single edit can be rolled back, failing closed if the safety capture fails.
Atomic, cross-process-locked .usage.json records views/uses/last-used and agent-created markers per skill without touching SKILL.md.
Only a one-line index of skills sits in the prompt; full skill text loads on demand.
When compaction reduces an old skill_view result to metadata, a canonical [SKILL_PRUNED] marker and re-derived ghosted-skill list tell the model the instructions are gone and how to reload them.
Plugins can ship skills served through skill_view under a plugin: namespace with the same injection checks as local skills.
Skills declare required env vars; on load Hermes reports readiness, captures missing secrets via a secure prompt and passes them to remote backends.
Frontmatter platforms/environments (docker, kanban...)/required apps and toolset fallbacks decide whether a skill is shown for the current session.
`hermes skills` config toggles skills globally or per messaging platform; disabled skills are hidden from the index and invocation.
Skills declare config keys in frontmatter that are discovered and resolved from config.yaml (dotpaths, path expansion) when the skill loads.

f: Skill template tokens and inline shell
w: ${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}/${HERMES_SESSION_ID} tokens and single-line !`cmd` snippets are expanded when a skill loads.
skills.external_dirs adds read-only skill roots (e.g. shared team repos) to discovery alongside ~/.hermes/skills.
Skills under an org mirror path are namespaced (org:skill) and resolved by the active org id.
Skills inside a project's .hermes/skills load only after the project is trusted; untrusted ones are counted and quarantined at scan time, with non-interactive surfaces fail-closed.
Turns a skill name (one or several stacked) into a user message carrying the SKILL.md content and user instruction, with a multi-slot cache and platform gating shared by CLI and gateway.
YAML files in skill-bundles/ alias several skills (plus optional instruction) under one name that loads them together.
Versioned skill sources store skill revisions and publish them so agents can pin or roll forward skill versions.
createSkill defines skills in code (inline sources) and resolves them for agents alongside filesystem skills.
Push/pull of skills to a sync plane with CAS refs and three-way merge on conflict, driven by skill_manage and the curator; currently inert unless the user is a Nous admin.
58 bundled SKILL.md skills across apple, autonomous-ai-agents, creative, email, media, productivity, research and more, seeded into every profile.
Serves repo-shipped optional skills and a centralized Hermes skills index as trusted official sources.

f: Bundled skill updates that keep user edits
w: Manifest-based seeding of repo skills into ~/.hermes/skills with origin hashes: new skills copied, unchanged ones updated, user-edited or user-deleted ones left alone.
Regex scan of external skills for dangerous patterns (exfil, agent-config modification, shell abuse) with builtin/trusted/community trust levels deciding install, overridable with --force.

review_skill_package inspects installed skills, local packages, archives or pasted SKILL.md without activating them, producing readiness facts, resource graph and eval-manifest checks; also a CI CLI with expiring waivers.

f: Skills hub (search, install, lock file, audit)
w: Search all skill catalogs at once and install skills through a quarantine and scan pipeline with a lock file and audit log.
Adapter for the clawhub.ai HTTP API: search, metadata and zip-streamed bundle download with retry-after handling.
Fetches skills from GitHub repos/taps via Contents/Trees API with token auth (env, gh CLI) and rate-limit handling.
Discovers skills via the skills.sh catalog and fetches content from GitHub.

f: Install a skill from a well-known endpoint or URL
w: Installs skills from /.well-known skill endpoints or a direct SKILL.md URL, validating names and bundle paths.
Adapters for the LobeHub agent index and browse.sh catalog, with a shipped index cache for offline browse.
Dashboard routes to create/edit custom SKILL.md files, search/install/scan hub skills and attach skills to cron jobs without SSH.

f: Find and install a missing skill
w: Guides the agent to find and install new skills when it lacks a capability.
Lets the agent inspect and change its own settings and permissions through bundled scripts.
The agent rewrites parts of its own persona or identity file through a safety-filtered edit, with each change recorded.

Single action to set/clear verbosity, tone and formality, arm or lift the reply gate, add free-text directives and save/load named profiles; every mutation goes through PersonalityStore and writes an audit memory.
A timeline and graph of learned skills and memories that the owner can inspect, edit or remove.
Analyses past sessions into a dated insight-YYYY-MM-DD.html report (quantitative charts plus qualitative sections and a share card).
Unified store of proposed cron jobs from a curated catalog, skill blueprints, self-improvement review and integrations that users accept or dismiss (dismissals latched), never auto-created.
Vendored dashboard plugin (Python API + prebuilt JS bundle) that scans local session history and unlocks tiered badges (tool chains, debugging, skills/memory use) with shareable PNG cards.
blame.py counts lines per release attributed to aider commits (via '(aider)' authors or Co-authored-by trailers) and records the percentage for the site.
update-history.py feeds git log and diffs since the last release plus the blame percentage to aider itself to update HISTORY.md.
Records what was tried, the outcome and the lesson, and recalls relevant experience for similar tasks, decaying confidence over time.
Parses Windows Steps Recorder (.mht) recordings, summarises them into demonstration plans and saves them for retrieval.
Ingests user corrections/rejections into expertise rules per domain, consolidates them and injects expertise into context.
Agents declare self-feedback intents (memory/skill/prompt improvements with confidence and evidence) that downstream reviewers validate, dedupe and apply.
Topics are summarised automatically in the background for later recall.
Runs learning targets that evaluate mods against headless scenarios with assertions and forbidden trace markers, so agents can iterate on harness changes.
A reflection subagent reviews recent conversations and rewrites memory in an isolated worktree, triggered on demand or after N turns.
Runs reflection with two models (a default and one sampled by weight from a pool) and asks the user for a blind preference, with optional transcript upload.
An agent that creates and edits other agents, workflows and templates, with task planning and template-builder workflows.
A successful run is turned into a deterministic script; later runs execute it and fall back to the AI only for failing steps.
An LLM reviewer audits generated scripts mid-run and post-run (hardcoded values, extraction, conditionals) with skills to investigate, validate and persist fixes.
A shared kanban.db is the cross-profile coordination primitive: tasks, runs, comments, events and assignees with idempotent create, driven by `hermes kanban` and /kanban.

f: PR card accepted only on green exact-head checks
w: Tasks that declare a GitHub PR are only accepted when the exact head commit passes acceptance checks, with receipts persisted after rechecking under lock.

Branch edits its own source in an isolated worktree pinned to the Beta line, under a write-once contract (paths, tools, tests, rollback) checked before every tool call; starting or widening needs the owner's yes; tests run and are recorded (persisted by commit); downloads stay inside; Windows sandbox first, WSL fallback; ships off.

Commits go only to branch/… lines, PRs only to the origin repo, as a draft with "Why merge" and evidence; Branch waits for checks on the exact commit, confirms rulesets, fixes review comments, then merges itself.

An Inbox card "Branch wants to improve itself" shows a bounded diff and stages; tasks link to their PR and record "merged repo#n"; honest receipts and metrics (time to PR, rounds, cost); status separates changed, tested, pending, merged, installed.

Self-edits reach the app only as a merged change plus a candidate build that passes a self-test on a copy of the data; automatic rollback if it does not stay up; rollback refuses half-undo; versioned app folders; GitHub checkpoint before update; "Fix update" hand-off; "Try a bad change" journal; updates never kill a waiting task.

Prove the whole loop from inside Branch: /improve from Telegram to draft PR, the first real self-fix, "add a missing knob" end to end, one real night of this project's work, and 30 days of Branch running on itself.

f: Build a missing knob on request
w: "There is no setting for X" becomes a source change that adds the knob.

Branch knows what each switch does, has a switch to change ordinary settings without asking, a restart tool, a card suggesting settings for the task, a Settings › Branch itself page with editable self-change rules, durable receipts with undo, and "Why is this on?".

A skill is adopted only when replaying held-out tasks shows a measured gain over baseline (blind, best of 3, at least 2 proof tasks); evidence, baseline, eval case and history travel with the skill; nightly evals score the owner's skills; failing environments are excluded.

f: Seasons safety: fresh permissions and model gates
w: Every Gardener step re-checks permissions; anything adding network, credentials, spending or installs asks; paid models stay off overnight; the night continues past seeds waiting for approval; work holds when its project or authority cannot be restored.

Budding records a capability gap, climbs the cheapest rung first (combine tools and record a skill; install an MCP server or plugin with OK and hot-reload; write its own tool with tests in the walled sandbox; a Branch code PR), then finishes the original task.

A Seasons page shows Rings, Gardener and Budding history with measured gains, Veto/Keep/Pin controls, in four languages; Seasons switches (Rings, night window, paid models, min gain) change by asking or in Settings.
Specialist agents are evaluated, promoted and rolled back on evidence.
Ideas drawn from history, a personal feed with an editable prompt, and learning to write like the owner.

A dogfood agent uses the installed app like a person (no deleting, sending, spending or safety changes); a continuous QA agent runs on an isolated build; findings become fixes at once; Branch compares itself step by step with Hermes, GrokBot and Muse.
Run an eval suite from Settings › Usage, with honest wording about judge-model calls.
Recall quality and latency measured on real questions (LongMemEval / LoCoMo style).
Ship-state of memory-side learning switches: editable memory blocks, meaning search over past conversations, expiring memories, reading back note edits, outside memory services.
The gateway starts detached and owns the engine so relaunches never stop tasks; a keep-awake knob; background builds stay low priority.

f: Hot reload of tools, skills, plugins and MCP
w: Tools, skills, plugins and MCP load when needed and reload without a restart; one "Tool loading" switch.
Window changes go live keeping draft, scroll and streams, with no flash.
Round limit visible and changeable, long runs like Claude Code, context room equals the model window, cheap settings lookups.

f: Live thinking summary and background reviewer
w: A short live summary of what it is thinking, and a reviewer that checks the work while it happens.
Scripts call tools over RPC to save context.

f: Subscription use through a Claude Code transport
w: Use subscriptions through a Claude Code plugin or transport.

f: Codex hand-off process cleanup on Windows
w: Stopping or timing out a Codex hand-off kills the whole process tree.
Background programs settle on stream close with a grace period, keep head and tail output and cool down repeated watch matches.
An execution-and-debugging loop with a dedicated troubleshooting role.
Every session, message, usage counter and metadata is persisted in a local SQLite database that survives restarts.
Each session is recorded as an append-only JSONL file of canonical items that can be replayed, resumed or inspected.
save_conversation_path writes every prompt/response pair per step to files for debugging.
Sessions are stored as durable events projected into message state, so clients can replay from a sequence number and sync between hosts.
A durable SQLite signal log records session state changes for watchers and emits coalesced stale-state notices.
Session persistence sits behind one store interface with local file, SQLite, in-memory and remote implementations.

f: Session schema migrations and legacy import
w: Creates the schema and reconciles columns with ALTER TABLE ADD on upgrade, rebuilding tables atomically when needed.
Cold rollout files are compressed in the background and legacy rollouts can be migrated (codex migrate-rollouts) with safe rename-based publication and rollback.
A damaged session database is copied aside, canonical rows are salvaged into a fresh store and indexes rebuilt, never overwriting the live file.
One process-wide health latch per state.db plus a cause-keyed copy table so every surface reports the same 'session storage unavailable' message and doctor code.
PRAGMA policy applies WAL with fallback and never live-downgrades; `sessions set-journal-mode` converts offline once no process holds the store.

f: Test isolation from the live session DB
w: Every SessionDB path resolution refuses to open a production state.db from a pytest context (env or process ancestry).
`hermes sessions stats` reports session/message counts, page and freelist counts, logical and WAL size, journal mode and FTS table/rebuild status; `sessions optimize` merges FTS segments and VACUUMs.
Lock files or leases ensure only one process writes a session at a time, reclaiming stale locks from crashed processes.

f: Several clients attach to one live session
w: CLI, desktop and IDE clients attach to and detach from the same hosted session without stopping it.
A cheap model call names each conversation after the first exchange; a manual rename always wins.
Titles are sanitized and lineage-aware (name, name #2...) so resume-by-title picks the latest variant; continue-last and by-id resume resolve through the store.
Read-only index of user prompts with jump-to-message windows that never hydrate the whole transcript.
Pin threads to the top of the sidebar list; pin state survives archive/restore.
Archive a chat to hide it without deleting (with Undo), browse archived chats and restore them.
Deleting a chat requires a confirmation showing its title and removes the conversation and files.
Deleted conversations and files go to a trash for restore or permanent deletion.
Lifecycle flags on session rows (pinned, archived, hidden, read/unread, ended/reopened) shared by CLI, TUI and dashboard.
One search box finds words across all conversations and messages, with previews and a jump to the matching message.

f: Agent tool to search and read past sessions
w: The agent searches past conversations and reads a session or a window around a message, returned as untrusted data.
sessions_list, sessions_history and sessions_send let an agent inspect other sessions, read anchored history windows and message or steer another session.

f: Bring a past conversation in as context
w: Attach earlier conversations to a message; the agent pages through them with run-scoped permission and the access is recorded.
Reads back stored message history of the room the request came from so a group member can ask for a recap or 'last N messages' of their own channel.
When a message replies to an earlier one, pulls the replied-to message and surrounding turns into the prompt so the reply is read in its original exchange.

f: Quote text into the next message
w: Select response text to quote it into the next message as chips.
Continue the last session or any earlier one by id or name, restoring full history and settings.

f: Session picker with search and preview
w: /threads picker, /thread, /new, /clone, /name and /resource manage per-project conversation threads and switch resource scopes.
On launch, resumes the last agent and conversation for the current directory, or creates a new agent, honouring flags.
Summarizes the current/resumed session from in-memory history with no LLM call or cache invalidation.
Branch a conversation from any message into a new one, leaving the original untouched.
Copy a topic with its messages into a new topic.
Edits and regenerations create sibling branches of a message that you can switch between.
Topic message flow canvas showing the message tree with live updates.

f: Edit an earlier message and rerun
w: Pick an earlier message, edit it and rerun the conversation from there (optionally restoring files).
Delete a message from history.
Select multiple messages to copy, export or delete.
The workspace is snapshotted each turn in a shadow git repo without touching the user's own history.

f: Restore a checkpoint (files, conversation, or both)

Diffs checkpoints in four modes (this checkpoint vs previous, from task start, to current workspace, full) and adds jump-to-previous-checkpoint navigation in chat, on top of the files / files-and-task restore Cline also offers.
Pick an earlier message to jump back to, optionally reverting file changes made since, with a confirmation showing changed-line stats.
/chat save, resume, list, delete tag-named conversation checkpoints, plus /chat share to export to Markdown or JSON.
Save a conversation as Markdown, JSON, text or other formats, with options for tool calls and reasoning.
Render selected messages as a shareable image with preview.
Builds a self-contained HTML replay of a session (events embedded) and optionally uploads it to a share provider for a link.
Export every conversation (and user data) in one go, in stable batches.
Export sessions with secrets replaced by a redaction marker, for sharing or as agent traces.
Exports character, memories, entities, relationships, rooms, worlds, tasks and optionally logs into a password-encrypted .eliza-agent file for migrating agents between machines.
Back up/restore to local files.
Back up/restore to S3-compatible storage.
Import conversation exports from ChatGPT, Claude and other chat apps into history.

f: Import Claude Code and Codex sessions
w: Import Claude Code, Codex and other coding-agent transcripts as sessions that can be continued.
Discovers existing Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi sessions on paired computers, shows their transcripts and adopts or continues them inside Branch while watching for upstream human activity.

f: Capture delegated Claude Code / Codex runs
w: Captures sessions produced by delegated Claude Code or Codex runs and links them back to the agent conversation.

`hermes claw migrate` detects an older install’s folder (and legacy dirs), warns if it is running, previews then migrates config, workspace, skills and optionally secrets via the migration skill script, with backup and cleanup.
Share a read-only snapshot of a conversation through a link that can be revoked, optionally with expiry; viewers can fork it.
Share a folder with other users/groups; shared folders appear in the sidebar.
In-app links carry backend and org query params so new tabs resolve against the right backend, and switching backends jumps to that backend's most recent conversation.
Group conversations into (nested) folders or projects and move them between groups.
A sidebar or page lists past conversations grouped by date with infinite scroll, a pinned section and running indicators.
Keeps multiple chat sessions per character in IndexedDB with create, switch, rename and delete.
Each agent has topics (conversations) with list caching, rename, favourite, search and topic manager.
Left rail merging dashboard conversations, connector inbox chats (Discord, Telegram…) and terminal PTY sessions into one time-bucketed list with source/world scope filter, rename and keyword search.

f: Session groups, sections and colour tags
w: The conversation list supports layout presets, workspace or repo folder grouping with drag-to-reorder, compact rows and a hide-older toggle with interval, all persisted.
Add or edit tags on conversations with optimistic updates and filter the sidebar list by active tags with icon chips.
Pin favourite agents/models for quick access in the sidebar.
Topics can be marked/unmarked completed to separate finished work.
Builds bounded single-line previews of the last user-visible message for session lists.
Messages show timestamps honouring clock format.
Minimap of the conversation with indicators and previews for quick jumping.
Zoom into a message for focused reading.
Conversation view loads older events on demand when scrolling up, tracking whether the server may have more.
Home page opens topics in tabs, with cross-window navigation coordinated by main.
Keeps several chat sessions running concurrently in the desktop, each with its own agent in the execution manager.
Add a second model/agent to the same prompt and compare responses in parallel.
A chat that is never saved to history (kept in memory only or deleted after a retention period).
Old sessions are deleted (or archived) automatically by age or count, skipping active ones.

f: Bulk prune or archive by filter
w: Prune or archive by age, duration windows, absolute timestamps, platform and title filters with dry-run preview and whole-lineage handling.
Composer drafts are debounced into localStorage per conversation (sessionStorage on home), restored on mount and cleared on confirmed delivery.
The prompt and attachments typed on home are held in a store and delivered as the first message once the conversation exists, including attachments queued during cloud start-task provisioning.

f: Message queue while the agent works
w: Queue messages while the model is generating.

f: Message an existing session from the CLI
w: codex queue (and the queue extension) enqueues a user message for an existing local or remote session, durably dispatched when the session goes idle.
Up/down arrows recall previous prompts (seeded from the project's logged user messages) and Ctrl+R reverse-searches them.
Ctrl+R in the composer searches persistent and local prompt history, previewing matches in place and restoring the draft on cancel.
/clear, /reset or /new drops the current history and starts fresh, optionally archiving it into memory first.
Writes /drop, /add and /read-only commands to a file so the current chat file set can be recreated later.
All direct messages from every channel and device collapse into one rolling personal conversation.
Sessions persist until /new or /reset, or opt into daily resets at a configured hour or idle resets after N minutes, per direct, group and thread session.

f: Recover turns interrupted by a restart
w: If the gateway dies mid-turn, WebUI turns are recovered on restart in a side-effect-safe way and a recovery notice is shown.
Clients reconnect to an in-flight run (after a refresh or drop) and replay missed output in order.
run.enqueue acknowledges immediately and executes runs FIFO per session, surviving socket drops.
Gateway implements LangGraph Platform threads/runs endpoints (create, stream, wait, cancel, history) over an in-memory run registry with optional persistent store.
Persistent run ownership lets multiple Gateway workers coordinate runs, cancel requests and recover runs after restarts.

f: Real-time sync across tabs and devices
w: Chat updates are pushed live to other tabs and devices, with an outbox for offline sends.
RemoteConversation drives a conversation hosted by an agent server over REST and keeps a read-only RemoteEventsList and RemoteState in sync via WebSocket.

w: Hands a local session to the cloud after git preflight (repo/branch/head checks), fingerprinting and transcript verification.
Streams session messages, parts and diffs to Kilo cloud with a per-session debounced ingest queue, in-flight cache, drain-on-shutdown and title sync.

With nodeHost.workerRuns enabled, a Mac app or headless host runs full Branch worker sessions with slot capacity, durable launch/turn journals, prepared git workspaces and optional container isolation.

Gives each Branch session its own dedicated ClickClack channel, creating, naming, syncing and retiring the channel as the session changes.
Gateway session-key to session-id routing, peers and heartbeats persisted in state.db (sessions.json legacy mirror) so conversations survive restarts.
Builds, parses and normalizes agent:{agentId}:{rest} session identifiers.
Exposes the active session context to agents during message processing.
Start, append operations, check status and complete long-running assistant work threads persisted in a store and resumable via scheduled triggers, with a semaphore serializing concurrent mutations.
Owns bounded idempotency reservations and replayable outcomes for chat turns so retried client requests return the settled result instead of running twice.
Stores per-session extension state (e.g. todo.v0) and which extensions are enabled for a session.
Each topic remembers its own model and reasoning config.
Applies project, title and other fields from session/new _meta to the new session row.
Bundles session data, logs and config into a diagnostics report users can attach to bug reports.
The conversation title menu offers rename, stop, delete with confirmation, download, show cost, show agent tools, skills, plugins and hooks, a public toggle and copy share link.
Finds text within the current conversation with case sensitivity, highlighting and next/previous navigation.
Task history shows subtasks nested under their parent as collapsible rows with links between parent and child, alongside fuzzy search and multi-select batch delete.
Context compression splits a conversation into child sessions linked by parent_session_id with locks, turn leases and cooldown counters.
AgentHistoryList saves to JSON and rerun_history replays actions deterministically, re-locating elements and using an AI step when needed, then summarising.
Detects values typed during a run (emails, names, dates) as variables so a recorded history can be replayed with substitutions.

f: Run one tool outside the model loop
w: execute_tool(name, action) runs one of the agent's tools outside the LLM loop, for scripted setup or client actions.
Open conversations are closed through an atexit hook so tools, terminals and MCP sessions shut down cleanly.
get_user_persistence_dir and conversation persistence paths resolve consistently (env override, warning on relative paths) across all stores.
MemoryLRUCache bounds both entry count and byte size when caching event file reads.
Files and images attached to threads are stored and referenced by id so they survive resume and can be listed per thread.
Stores checkpoint channels as deltas with periodic snapshots, with mode frozen per process and a fail-closed gate.
Keeps one session per (workspace, bot, launcher type, launcher id) with an O(1) index, expiry heap and retention caps on sessions, conversations per session and messages per conversation.
Web UI replays a recorded event stream with play/pause/seek and speed controls.
Thumbs up/down with tags on responses, forwarded to Langfuse when configured.
Session graph model and display-message projection used by UIs.
New chats show suggested starter questions from per-user or global reflective questions and built-in suggestion cards.

f: Side question in a background fork
w: Forks the conversation in the background to answer a side question in a separate pane without disturbing the main thread.
Browses pinned, Letta Code and all agents with keyboard shortcuts, pins agents per project, and lets you rename or describe them.

f: Inspect messages and steps from the CLI
w: Inspects an agent's messages, message status and execution steps from the command line.
Global command palette to search agents/topics/settings, ask AI, run context commands and switch theme.
Comment on topics for collaboration.
A new chat starts as an unsaved draft; the new-topic shortcut either opens a fresh draft or saves the current draft as a topic.
cleanupStaleRunningTopics resets topics left stuck in a running state.
Forward messages to other agents/topics via a forward modal.
Workflow runs persist snapshots after each step so they can be inspected, resumed or time-travelled.
Captures first messages, first exec, filesystem changes and run audits per factory session, mirroring titles.
SessionFactory creates interactive, plan-following, batch-from-folder, OpenAI-operator or service sessions.
Parses session logs and screenshots into a structured trajectory object for analysis.
Schema v31 columns store message and tool-call uids so transcript writers, restore and repair agree on message identity.
Emoji reactions set on transcript rows are stored in message metadata and survive compaction.
Coalescing background writer records per-model token usage and billing-route columns per session.

`hermes sessions` list, export, delete, prune, archive, rename/retitle, pin/unpin/pinned, browse, stats, optimize, clean-markers, optimize-storage plus pre-DB handlers (repair, recover, import) that work when the schema is broken.
Finds sessions whose stored system prompt is degraded, verifies candidates and clears them after confirmation (JSON report option).
Shapes stored history into wire messages for TUI/Desktop: image refs, content coercion, in-flight turn tracking and failure detail.
Dashboard routes for listing, searching, viewing and managing sessions per profile with schema heal and an auto-archive ticker.
Shared timestamp + bounded description/provenance record of session activity consumed by watchdogs and UIs.
Notes can be pinned to the sidebar for quick access.
Admins can browse a user's chats (ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS).
/rollout prints the current rollout file path; an optional session log records TUI events for debugging.
Before each run, in-memory provider-specific fixes sanitize tool-call ids, repair tool-result pairing, fix turn ordering and clean thinking signatures without rewriting stored history.
Per-agent Talk sessions are persisted in SQLite with transcripts and mutation evidence so voice conversations continue across reconnects and post a summary afterwards.
Pause, resume and stop running conversations from chat and sidebar, with a confirm-stop modal, unified across local and cloud backends.
Each agent turn opens a run row (with parent run for delegations/spawns, optional external task id) and closes it with status and error, never breaking the reply if bookkeeping fails.
Pin messages in a conversation, with a pinned-messages bar and a list of every pin.

Scheduled backups to GitHub, or a checkpoint to GitHub before each update.

f: Signed receipts chain and record check
w: Tool receipts are signed into a chain shown in Inbox › History; "Check the record" reports "Record intact" and says it covers signed receipts, not every displayed step.
Inbox › History lists past runs with "Search what ran" and a read-only Watch view of steps and questions.
Steering shows plain words; stopping a reply leaves a trace; "Done" is never claimed when nothing was done; failure lines stay.
Use a 1-hour cache for person-paced sessions on API keys instead of paid keep-alive pings.
An agent's action menu offers restart, repair, export and delete.

w: Install, update and remove skills from GitHub, registries (ClawHub), URLs or archives, with validation.

Python Functions extend the pipeline: pipes act as models, filters modify inlet/outlet/stream, actions add buttons under messages.

f: Marketplace for plugins, skills, MCP servers and agents
w: Browse, search and install plugins, skills, MCP servers and agents from curated or community catalogues.

Web search through a choice of providers (DuckDuckGo, Brave, SearXNG, Tavily, Exa and more).
Discover SKILL.md skills from user, project, plugin and built-in folders and offer them to the model.

f: Prompt library with versions and variables
w: Prompt groups with versions, production labels, categories, {{variables}} filled at use, auto-send and ACL sharing.

f: Install and remove plugins from npm, git or archives
w: Install, list and remove plugins from npm, git repositories, marketplaces or uploaded archives.
Sign in to protected remote MCP servers with OAuth 2.1 (discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE), with stored tokens and safe refresh.
