w: Plugins bundle skills, MCP servers, apps and hooks described by a manifest (also reading .claude-plugin/plugin.json), loaded from configured roots and toggled in config.
Commands typed in chat apps (with a prefix) run built-in or plugin handlers instead of going to the model.

f: Claude Code and Gemini plugin compatibility
w: Installs extensions from git, npm, archives or marketplaces, converting Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Qoder plugins into Qwen format with consent prompts and settings.

f: Custom slash commands from files and saved prompts
w: Users define slash commands in Markdown/TOML files or saved prompts, with arguments, file and shell injection.

f: Install this app into other agents' MCP configs
w: skyvern setup writes MCP config for Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode, Hermes and mcporter.

f: One command registry shared by every surface
w: One command registry (names, aliases, arguments, surfaces) drives the window, terminal, chat apps and help.
A plugin API and host that loads plugins contributing tools, commands, providers and event handlers.

f: Tool search: load tools when needed
w: Large tool sets stay hidden behind tool search; the model finds and loads tools only when needed.
Manages reasoning effort per model and reasoning display (show, hide, full, clamp), session-scoped or --global.

f: MCP Apps / MCP-UI rendering in a sandboxed frame
w: Renders MCP-UI resources returned by tools as interactive embedded components/carousels.
Restricts which allowed users may run which slash commands per platform and per DM/group scope, with admin lists and user allow-lists.
Filters skills at load time by declared requires.bins, anyBins, env and config paths plus OS, and reports missing requirements in skill status.
Shows the help message listing commands and shortcuts.
Switches model/provider mid-session (session-scoped or --global) through one shared pipeline of alias, provider and credential resolution, with reasoning flags and an expensive-model confirmation.
Shows session, model, provider/auth, token and context info.

f: Background processes the agent can list, read, write to and stop
w: Long-running commands run in the background; the agent can list them, read new output, write input and stop them.
Declarative plugin sets where every entry must pin an exact 40-char commit SHA; tags and branches are rejected.

f: Declared per-server inputs and secrets filled in a form
w: MCP server configs can declare per-user variables (API keys, URLs) users fill in a config dialog.
Learns a reusable skill from anything described: directories, URLs, this chat or notes.
Handles server-initiated elicitation requests by prompting the user for structured input in CLI and desktop.
Plugins register lifecycle hooks, middleware, event-bus listeners and system-prompt sections, dispatched with per-callback timeouts and failure reporting.

f: Plugin hot load, unload and reload
w: Every plugin registration is recorded with its inverse so force reload or targeted unload unwinds registries in reverse order.

f: Plugins walled in their own process
w: Connects LangBot to the separate plugin runtime over stdio (local) or WebSocket (containers), with heartbeat, reconnect loop and desired-state reconciliation of installed plugins per workspace.

f: Progressive skill loading (skill tool, search, resources)
w: Only skill names and descriptions sit in the prompt; the model loads a skill body, its references or a search result on demand.

f: Reload MCP servers without a restart
w: Reloads MCP servers from config without restarting, refreshing cached agents.

f: Try an MCP server or tool by hand
w: Tests each MCP server through the agent-server, stores health per server key, classifies auth failures from 401/403 text and shows status with credential guidance.

f: /commands paged list of commands and skills
w: Lists and reloads custom slash commands without restarting.
Generates or updates AGENTS.md project instructions from a repository scan.
Reviews pending memory writes held by the write-approval gate, approves or rejects them, and toggles the gate.
Exports the conversation to JSON, Markdown or HTML, optionally redacted, and on messaging delivers the file to the chat.
Searches, installs, inspects and manages skills, and reviews skill writes held by the write-approval gate (pending/diff/approve/reject).
record_artifact registers produced files/directories and record_source records citations for the session so clients can list them.
Controls background skill maintenance: status, run, pin, archive and list archived skills.
Browse a catalog of MCP integrations from @openhands/extensions, filter by section, and install with connection-option, transport and OAuth configuration.
An MCP server that serves Mastra documentation, examples and changelogs to coding agents in editors.

f: Export and import a profile without secrets
w: Packs a profile (skills, memory, persona, crons, plugins, settings, theme) into a shareable tar.gz with credentials stripped.
Prompts exposed by MCP servers become slash commands, with arguments parsed from the command line.
Answers server-initiated sampling/createMessage requests, including tool-use results, using the agent's model.

f: Plugin UI surfaces in sandboxed frames
w: Plugins render their own UI in sandboxed iframes connected by a MessagePort bridge and widget kit.
Maps portable mcp.json entries onto MCPServer with single-pass placeholder expansion, command and cwd containment inside the plugin root, remote URL rules and header filtering.
Read-only, bounded client for the public MCP Registry used by the plugin's routes to browse and install servers.

f: Skills from cloud catalogs and remote nodes
w: Skills can come from cloud catalogs or remote executors and are read through a skills.read/skills.list tool using skill:// resource ids.

f: Tools lent by the client (window, IDE, SDK)
w: Frontends register tools as pure JSON specs on conversation start; when the agent calls one, the ActionEvent is streamed to the client which executes it and posts the result back.

f: "/" menu and autocomplete in the composer
w: Typing / in the composer opens a searchable menu of commands, prompts and skills with descriptions.
Lists active subagents, delegations and running tasks (alias /tasks).
Runs a prompt in a separate background session (alias /background) while the main conversation continues.
Sets up an automation from a blueprint template with slot=value arguments (alias /bp).
Forks the session (alias /fork); on Discord, Telegram, Slack and Matrix the fork opens in a new sibling thread, while --here switches in place.
Typing /btw <question> routes the question through an ask_agent side channel without interrupting the main turn and shows answers as separate btw messages.
Chooses what a message sent while Hermes works does: queue, steer or interrupt.
Compresses context on demand (alias /compact), with a focus topic, `here [N]` to keep recent turns verbatim, or --preview to see the effect first.
/config shows readable settings, /config <key> reads one and /config <key> <value> updates a whitelisted key (model, context limits, max steps, knowledge, thinking, self-evolution) atomically.
Shows git changes: unstaged, staged, all, or everything Hermes changed this session, with --stat and path filters.
Exits the chat.
Fast mode (OpenAI Priority Processing / Anthropic Fast Mode) for every request, or only a bounded window per turn (auto) or per session (cold).
Sets a standing goal pursued across turns; an auxiliary judge checks it after each turn and continues with a normal user message until achieved, with gates, pause/resume and wait.
Hands the CLI session to a messaging platform home channel (new thread where supported) and waits until the gateway picks it up.
Sets a recurring prompt (alias /hb) that re-enters the session only when idle, with status/pause/resume/clear.
Prints the conversation history, honoring /timestamps.
Attaches an image from the clipboard to the next prompt.
Shows usage insights and analytics over the last N days (default 30) from session history.
Operates the multi-profile collaboration board (tasks, links, comments) from chat.

f: /loop re-run a prompt on an interval
w: Re-runs a prompt on an interval in the session (alias /proactive) until LOOP_COMPLETE, --times N, an --until judge, or a max-ticks backstop.
Starts a fresh session (new ID and history), optionally pre-titled, behind a confirmation that can be skipped with now/--yes; alias /reset.
Gateway emergency stop: pauses all new work globally until `/pause off`.
Selects a named personality overlay (built-in or user-defined) without touching the user-owned system prompt.
/plan and /code toggle the conversation between planning and code modes like the Plan/Code button, optionally sending a task, while swallowing commands when the relevant agent or socket is busy.
From chat, lists gateway platform adapters with state and pauses or resumes a failing one without unloading it.
In-session list, install, update, enable, disable, link, uninstall, reload and config for extensions.
Queues a prompt for the next turn (alias /q) and lists, edits, removes, reorders or clears queued prompts.
Gracefully restarts the messaging gateway after draining active runs and notifies the chat when back.
Backs up N user turns, rewinds the stored session and re-prompts.
Lists or restores filesystem checkpoints taken before edits, keeping later hand-edits unless --all.
Resumes a previous session by name, number or search, including a one-shot numeric pick after a bare /resume.
Sets the current chat as the platform home channel (alias /set-home) for handoffs and notifications.
Shows or switches the display skin/theme live.
Injects a message after the next tool call without interrupting the running turn (alias /s).
Kills running background processes; on messaging it also interrupts the turn and ends delegations scoped to that chat.
Reviews automations Hermes suggests and accepts or dismisses them (alias /suggest), or browses the catalog.
Sets the session title used by /resume and /sessions.
Shows token usage, cost and provider rate limits; `reset` redeems a banked Codex limit reset.
Shows the Hermes Agent version (alias /v).
Toggles voice mode and spoken replies or shows voice status, in the CLI and on messaging platforms.
Shows the caller’s slash-command access level (admin or user) under per-platform access control.

f: Bounded MCP result and error rendering for the model
w: Renders MCP result blocks for the model with size caps, _meta filtering, image/audio cached as MEDIA tags, resource links and embedded resources.
MCP server exposes browser control (act, click, type, extract, observe, tabs, frames, network, HAR, storage), sessions, profiles, credentials, workflows, schedules and scripts.

f: Code mode: one script calls many tools
w: The model writes one script that calls many tools, so long tool chains cost one turn and little context.

f: Context providers attached from the composer (@ / #)
w: Context providers register with core, and typing @ in the chat input opens a submenu to search and attach items from them.
Cycles tool-progress display off, new, all and verbose (also on gateways when enabled by config).
skyvern doctor checks dependencies, browser and streaming setup.

f: Launch and configure other agent runtimes (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes)
w: Launch coding CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Antigravity, Hermes) in the user's terminal with the chosen Cherry provider written into their config and bundled git on PATH.

f: List, steer and stop live subagents
w: A registry of live subagents lets the model list them, send steering messages mid-run, or stop them.
Shows MCP progress notifications in tool cards.
list_mcp_resources and read_mcp_resource let the model browse and read resources exposed by connected MCP servers; @server:resource references work in prompts.
Answers MCP roots requests with the session working directory so servers know which folder they may act on.

f: MCP tool approval and risk policy
w: MCP tool calls can require approval per tool (with templated prompts) and tools can be omitted from specific surfaces or deferred to tool_search.
The llm-task tool runs a one-off model call that must return JSON, strips code fences and validates the result against a supplied JSON schema.
Extensions can call models only through operator-granted, bounded host invocations with a separate-process schema worker.
Per-server configurable MCP call timeout.

f: Per-server MCP options and auth variants
w: Per-server config supports env/env_vars, cwd, enabled/required, startup and tool timeouts, enabled_tools/disabled_tools filters, per-tool approval mode and output token limits.
Automatically loads selected skills into context at agent start.

Discovers bundled, user and entry-point plugins with an enable/disable gate, imports them by path (siblings pre-registered for relative imports), and warns on missing dependencies or config-schema issues.
Tools are discovered by scanning the tools package and external nanobot.tools entry points, each deciding via enabled(ctx) whether to register for the current scope.
Vendor-specific repo files such as CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md are only injected when the active model belongs to that vendor family, matched via the canonical model name.
Normalises server/tool names into provider-safe unique tool identifiers.
On list_changed notifications the server's tools are re-discovered and the live agent's tool list is rebuilt while preserving the cached tools[] prefix.
Snapshots eligible skills per session and refreshes mid-session when SKILL.md files change, nodes connect or watch capacity recovers.
Runs the memory/skill self-improvement review now in a background fork of the conversation, optionally steered by focus text.
Typing /skill-name at the start of a message loads that skill's SKILL.md as hidden current-turn context while respecting disabled skills and agent whitelists.

f: Scaffold a new plugin or MCP server
w: gemini extensions new creates an extension from templates (MCP server, commands, hooks, skills, policies, themes); validate checks a manifest; link installs a dev copy.
A bundled skill with scripts to initialise, validate and package new skills.
Per-task output_schema validates a child's result with one retry; on a miss the raw text is kept with schema_valid=false and errors instead of discarding work.

Behind the customTools experiment, loads TS/JS tool files from .roo/tools dirs, transpiles them with a bundled esbuild, validates zod parameter schemas, and exposes them to the model as native function tools.

f: Wake on background command completion or matching output
w: With notify_on_complete, a finished background process injects an [IMPORTANT ...] completion message into the conversation on CLI, gateway and TUI.
Toggles YOLO mode, skipping all dangerous-command approvals, persisted across resume.
Copies the last (or Nth) assistant response to the clipboard.
Uploads a debug report (system info and logs) and returns shareable links.
Toggles the runtime-metadata footer (model, cost, timing) on final gateway replies.
Signs in with a Nous account from the CLI or, off-turn in paired DMs only, from a messaging chat, keeping connectors.
Runs one prompt through the default Mixture-of-Agents preset, then restores the session model.
Toggles, lists, scales or adopts a petdex mascot shown in the CLI.
Spawns an independent full-privilege reviewer subagent that reviews the work just discussed in the background and reports back.
Shows the Nous credit balance and links to billing on the portal.
Lets the agent write a new rule file into the workspace rules folder.
A CLI-Anything catalog lets users install command-line apps and the agent run them through run_cli_app with controlled arguments; apps can be @mentioned from the composer.
Before model calls, uses serialized routing metadata and the latest user text to auto-promote relevant deferred MCP tools without holding tool objects.

f: Choose which tools, MCP servers and skills each agent may use
w: Per pipeline, chooses which plugins, MCP servers and skills are available to its runner, with fail-closed validation of stored preferences.
One supervisor per Hermes process kills stdio MCP servers if Hermes dies without cleanup (SIGKILL, OOM, crash).

f: Convert commands and legacy files into skills
w: Imported Claude Code slash commands are rewritten into Codex skills, deriving descriptions and rewriting source-specific terms.
Builds tool policies that disable specific MCP tools per server.
Edit a file by replacing an exact, unique string.
Sample plugins: agents squad, background terminal, custom compaction, env blocker, gitignore read guard, mac notifications, OpenRouter provider, TypeScript LSP, web search, telemetry.
Exports user skills as bounded archives that never activate or execute the skill, with a Web UI export dialog.

f: File read tool with ranges, paging and multimodal content
w: Read files with line ranges and paging, size budgets, and images/PDFs passed to vision models.
Create or overwrite files, with a diff, preserved line endings and size guards.
Log notifications sent by MCP servers are forwarded into Hermes logs.

f: Large tool output spilled to a readable file
w: Tool output over a size limit is cut to a preview and the full text is saved to a file the model can read later.

f: Lifecycle hooks that run user scripts (PreToolUse etc.)
w: Runs user scripts on 12 events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, etc.) and lets PreToolUse hooks block tool calls.

f: Live reload of rules, skills, hooks and agent config
w: Watches rules, skills, workflows, hooks and agent config files and pushes live updates to the runtime.

f: MCP config variable and secret interpolation
w: Server config supports ${VAR} and Cursor-style interpolation, filters hidden-whitespace/suspicious entries, resolves commands and uses a cached npx binary shortcut.

f: MCP conformance tests and test harness
w: Runs the official MCP conformance suite against goose's client with tracked expected failures.
Tool calls recover automatically: 401 triggers OAuth refresh, expired sessions reconnect, and dead stdio children respawn before retrying.
Repeatedly failing servers trip a circuit breaker and per-server connect cooldown so calls fail fast instead of stalling turns.

f: MCP tool catalogue cache and prewarm
w: Per-server tool manifests are cached on disk with a TTL so MCP tools appear in the agent's tool list without spawning stdio servers until first use.

f: MCP trust and state per profile
w: Trust for MCP servers is recorded per profile home and checked at call time against the calling session's profile, so a secondary profile never inherits another's trust.

f: One page to manage MCP, plugins and skills
w: Workspace page to manage MCP plugins, Lark integration and skills with search, detail views, community .skill import and per-skill enable toggles.
PathTrigger skills with gitignore-style globs are injected when the agent touches matching files, giving Cursor-style rules per directory.
Interrupts are scoped to the agent's execution thread so stopping one session never kills tools running for other sessions in the same gateway process.
Reuses MCP sessions across tool calls for stateful stdio servers, isolated per event loop.
TerminalTool runs shell commands in a persistent session that keeps cwd and env between calls, supports background processes, timeouts, interactive input and returns exit code plus output.

f: Personal MCP connections and per-user credentials
w: Owner-only MCP server configs stored per user separate from deployment config, loaded only for the caller and restricted to public networks for non-operators.

Single `terminal` tool runs shell commands in the backend chosen by TERMINAL_ENV (local, docker, ssh, singularity, modal, daytona, vercel_sandbox or a plugin-registered backend) via a builder/spec dispatch table, with a per-task sandbox cache and lazy bring-up.

f: Plugin settings, config forms and storage
w: Extensions declare settings (stored per user or workspace, secrets in keychain) and use ${extensionPath}-style variables in their config.
Return a tree-sitter repo map or a subdirectory listing; defined but excluded from the default tool list.

f: Run commands, MCP and file transfer on paired nodes
w: file_fetch, dir_list, dir_fetch and file_write tools move files to and from paired nodes as base64 over node.invoke (binaries up to 16 MB), bypassing bash stdout truncation under a node-invoke policy.

f: Run independent tool calls in parallel
w: Independent tool calls from one model response run concurrently, with observation ordering preserved for the transcript.

f: Scan MCP tool descriptions for prompt injection
w: Descriptions of discovered MCP tools are scanned for prompt-injection patterns before being shown to the model.

f: Serve or proxy stdio MCP servers over HTTP
w: Serves any MCP server over SSE and streamable HTTP with Express routes.
The agent runs shell commands with timeouts, bounded and streamed output, and an option to keep long commands running.
Lists configured skill bundles, the /<name> aliases that preload several skills at once.
Skills page lists bundled, user and project skills with category facets, filters, detail modal and per-skill enable toggles, using an allow-list for bundled skills and a deny-list for user skills.
TaskTrigger skills declare named inputs that the agent must collect from the user before following the skill's procedure.
Composer tools menu with tabs for agent skills, slash commands and attachments.

f: Turn an OpenAPI description into tools
w: Agents can call any OpenAPI-described API (actions) with auth (API key/OAuth), domain validation and an action editor.

ToolDefinition pairs Pydantic Action and Observation schemas with an executor, annotations (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world) and declared resources, and renders to chat or Responses tool schemas.

f: "!" runs a shell command from the composer
w: Prefixing input with ! runs a shell command directly and streams stdout/stderr into a bordered box in the chat.
Connects browser tools to a live Chromium-family browser over CDP (auto-launching one), disconnects, shows status, or switches to Browser Use mode.
Clears the chat history.
Shows a detailed context-window view (alias /ctx): usage gauge, category breakdown, compression stats and throughput.
/tasks lists scheduled tasks owned by the current chat (receiver and channel type), as plain text on every channel except Feishu's card.
/knowledge on|off toggles the knowledge base and /knowledge list|tree prints its structure.
Loads MCP servers from config, tracks connection state and lets /mcp enable, disable or inspect servers.
Shows the active profile name and home directory.
Opens the next prompt in $EDITOR as Markdown (alias /compose), seeded with optional initial text, then sends it.
Reloads .env variables into the running CLI session.
Creates, lists, restores or prunes snapshots of Hermes config and state databases (alias /snap), restoring through the SQLite backup API.
Shows or hides injected system reminders in the transcript.
Lists, enables or disables tools for the session from the composer.
Enables or inspects Telegram DM topic sessions so each forum topic is its own Hermes session.
Toggles the "Hey Hermes" wake-word listener in the CLI.
Shows, creates, lists or prunes isolated git worktrees, moving the session into a new one; prune never deletes unpushed or in-use work.

f: @-mention a model or agent to answer
w: Typing @ in the composer switches endpoint/model/agent or inserts a prompt.
Composer mention pickers for files (fuzzy search), Agent Manager worktrees and past sessions, inserted as context parts.

f: Add a hub MCP server for one session
w: --mcp owner/package adds an MCP server from the Continue hub for the session; can be repeated.

f: Agent drives interactive TUI programs in a PTY
w: Allocates a real pseudo-terminal so the agent can drive TUI programs, with interactive prompt detection and approval gates.
The message tool's react action adds or removes emoji reactions on any supported channel, resolving the target message id per platform.

f: Agent finds and installs its own tools, skills and plugins
w: MCP server with one deterministic action so agents can install new MCP servers.

f: Agent lists, reads and writes skills
w: Agent tools to list, read and author skills in the project store.

f: Agent opens files and URLs in the side preview pane
w: One desktop_preview tool opens a URL, dev server or file in the preview pane beside the chat, reads its content, or closes it/a tab.
Revisioned in-memory task list (pending/in_progress/completed/cancelled) merged or replaced per call and re-injected after context compression.

f: Agent tools that control the desktop app's own panes
w: Desktop-only tools emit renderer events through an emitter the desktop gateway installs; elsewhere they report 'desktop only' and cost nothing.
The agent creates/switches first-class Projects (per-profile projects.db, the desktop sidebar's named workspaces) only via explicit tool calls, never as a side effect of cd.
Agents can list and use stored credentials (env-style KV, OAuth) which are injected into sandboxes instead of being pasted into chat.

f: Answer questions from the app's own docs
w: /help <question> retrieves the top-20 relevant chunks from bundled aider docs (llama-index + bge-small embeddings, cached per version) and answers in help mode.
The blocker plugin's app-blocker engine dispatches block/unblock to the native Capacitor plugin when reachable and exposes status to providers.

f: Approval for writes to a running process
w: Writes to a running process's stdin can be routed through approval so the agent cannot silently type into privileged prompts.
Lets the model ask the user a question with optional suggested answers, rendered as dialogs in TUI, VS Code and Desktop.
Attach plugins to a new conversation via a picker in the launcher, keyed by plugin spec identity, and view attached plugins in a modal.
Cheap deterministic selectors (BM25, character n-grams, LRU, RRF fusion) rank likely-relevant skills in shadow mode without changing the model catalog.
CLI and TUI start MCP discovery in the background with safe waiting helpers and a startup summary naming failed servers.

Running background processes are checkpointed to JSON and re-adopted after a restart with PID-recycling safety, while completed ones leave bounded per-producer result receipts readable via process_manage.
delegate_task(background=true) dispatches children on a daemon executor and returns a handle immediately; completion re-enters the parent as an async_delegation event, with stop fan-out on interrupt.
read_file refuses or discloses binary types by extension and blocks special files (devices, FIFOs), and handles UTF-8/binary edge cases instead of dumping garbage into context.
Users can bookmark slash commands, which then appear as starter cards in an empty chat.

f: Browser control from the command line
w: skyvern browser subcommands operate a live browser session from the shell for agent use.

f: Browser extension bridge for browser tools
w: Connects to a Jan browser extension for browser MCP tools.

f: Built-in skills that teach the agent to configure itself
w: Ships skills compiled into the CLI binary (e.g. a kilo-config guide) registered before discovery so user skills of the same name override them.
Ships skills for PDF, Word documents, spreadsheets and a skill-creator skill with helper scripts.
Bundled business tool clients served through the stdio MCP lifecycle so provider credentials stay inside MCP processes.
Central registry maps tool names/namespaces to handlers, builds model-visible specs per turn and dispatches calls with tracing.
Changes the session working directory, either by the agent or by the user with /chdir or /cd.
Exposes run-scoped platform/event actions (send message, platform APIs supported by the adapter) as tools that runners can call.

f: Clarifying questions answered with chat-app buttons
w: On messaging platforms a pending clarify blocks the agent thread while the user answers via buttons (Telegram/Discord/Slack) or text, with timeouts and card retirement.
Lets the agent offer clickable follow-up suggestions that appear as a bar above the prompt and auto-dismiss on new input.

f: Clipboard round-trip with web chat UIs
w: --copy-paste copies the chat context to the clipboard before each prompt and watches the clipboard, dropping newly copied text (e.g. a web LLM reply) into the input prompt for submission, with the main model switched to an editor-* edit format.

f: Cloud sandbox backends for code and commands
w: Runs commands in Modal sandboxes via the native SDK (Sandbox.create/exec) with persistent snapshots across sessions.
Foreground command timeouts are capped below the sandbox idle timeout and unsafe values are rejected with a readable message.
Deterministic, bounded compaction of large MCP tool responses (HTML, network payloads) before returning them to the model.

f: Connected MCP server summary in context
w: Injects a compact summary of connected MCP servers, their status, tools and resources into context each turn without dropping any discovered item.
Agents generate DOCX, PDF, PPTX, XLSX and text files and offer them as downloads.
Process-wide registry stops concurrent subagents on the same filesystem from clobbering each other: if agent B writes a file agent A already read, A's next write is refused until it re-reads.
Shared contract to execute plugin JavaScript on Node/Bun via node:vm, on iOS via an embedded JavaScriptCore context and on Android via QuickJS.
Picks the right shell launcher per OS and builds the tool environment, including how the letta binary is invoked from child shells.

f: Current time and time arithmetic tools
w: Returns current time with timezone so the agent can reason about dates.
Shared ThreadPoolExecutor whose workers are daemon threads and not joined at exit, so one wedged tool cannot block process shutdown.

f: Dangerous env var denylist for extensions
w: Refuses 31 dangerous env vars (LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, etc.) when launching extensions.
A default security blacklist audits risky tool calls (e.g. destructive shell commands) and forces intervention.
/diagram first writes an improved diagram description, then generates Mermaid.js code that the web client renders, with cleanup of invalid syntax.
Routes a Docker sandbox through a host-side iron-proxy credential firewall and guards docker_forward_env, docker_env and docker_extra_args so they cannot weaken or bypass it.

f: Drive and annotate the in-app preview
w: drive_preview clicks, types and scrolls in the preview pane using legible element refs that survive re-renders.
Lets users view, customize and reset built-in prompt templates.

f: Edits applied through the client diff/apply UI
w: Edit, find-and-replace and multi-edit tool calls are executed in the GUI so changes stream through the diff/apply UI.

f: Enable or disable plugins per directory
w: Extensions can be enabled or disabled globally or per directory via override rules.

f: Enable, disable and override tools in config
w: Config can override built-in tool descriptions, disable tools or change their default policy.
builtIn_debugRandomNumber tool used to test tool-calling end to end.
The sparkle button rewrites the user's draft prompt with an LLM, optionally using a separate API profile (enhancementApiConfigId) and recent task history as context.
Parses arithmetic expressions with a recursive-descent parser (no eval) and evaluates integers exactly so chat answers never rely on model arithmetic.
Exits the process with status code 1 to signal failure.

f: Extension middleware injected into the agent loop
w: Extensions contribute middlewares placed by semantic anchors translated to stack indices, with failures isolated from the user's run and ordering invariants validated.
Tracks local file changes by mtime+size, detects deletions and syncs them to SSH, Modal and Daytona sandboxes transactionally, with bulk upload and sync-back.

f: Forward MCP server instructions into the prompt
w: Collects instructions from opted-in MCP servers, dedupes and truncates them per server, and adds them to the agent prompt.
Opens the fuzzy command palette (also Ctrl+P) in the classic CLI.

patch's old_string is matched through 9 ordered strategies (exact, line-trimmed, whitespace/indentation/escape/unicode-normalized, trimmed boundary, block anchor, context-aware), with similarity strategies refused under replace_all.
Returns the current git diff of the workspace to the model.
Glob tool finds files by pattern using ripgrep when available with a Python fallback, sorted by modification time and capped.
Greets new group members (group_welcome_msg or per-group fixed text, else an LLM welcome), reacts to pat-pat and replies to 'Hello'.
The agent discovers data-tour targets and highlights/narrates UI elements step by step or hands the user a pageable tour.
Runs commands in a container hardened with cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges and PID limits, with configurable CPU/memory/disk limits, network config and optional bind-mount persistence.
Configurable max_bytes/max_lines/max_line_length caps and one 40% head / 60% tail truncation algorithm with a single notice wording for terminal, execute_code and MCP output.
Tools can provide a human-readable title derived from args for UIs and traces.

f: Import MCP servers from other apps
w: Existing JSON-style MCP configs (Claude-style mcpServers files) are loaded and converted to Continue's YAML format.

f: In-repo skills for coding agents working on the project
w: Ships skills (dev, plugin-dev, deploy, testing, MCP ops, EBA adapter dev) plus an lbs CLI so Claude Code/Codex-style agents can develop and operate LangBot.

f: Inline shell output in skill bodies
w: Skill bodies may contain !`command` placeholders that run at render time and are replaced with output, while fenced and inline code is never executed.

f: Install skills into other coding agents
w: browser-use skill install writes SKILL.md into Claude Code, Codex and other assistant skill directories.

f: Interactive exec sessions with stdin writes
w: Model runs shell commands in a persistent PTY via exec_command, gets a session id for long-running processes, and keeps interacting with them through write_stdin with yield timeouts.

f: Interactive terminal sessions for the user
w: Spawns interactive web-terminal PTY sessions (Bun or Node backends) jailed to an allowed root through symlink-resolved cwd checks, buffers output for late subscribers and bridges keystrokes/resize over WebSocket.
Edits Jupyter notebook cells (replace, insert, delete) by cell id.
Free-tier public endpoints (Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl, Keenable) serve web search/extract with no API key, resolved strictly last after every configured backend and sending no user identifiers.
Keyword plugin replies with fixed text, images or file URLs when a message matches a configured keyword.

Killing a background process snapshots descendants, SIGTERMs the parent first, waits a grace period, then SIGTERM/SIGKILLs survivors and finally stops the systemd scope, avoiding orphans and browser core dumps.
CommandLineExecutor only launches a bare allow-listed application name with no arguments.
Opens the learning journey timeline of learned skills and memories (aliases /learning, /memory-graph), with list/delete/edit.
Built-in /cmd, /commit, /http, /onboard, /review and /share commands generate shell commands, commit messages, call an HTTP endpoint, onboard to a repo, review code or export the session.
Filesystem tools manager wraps directory listing with depth/size limits to avoid prompt overflow.

f: List, grep and view indexed knowledge-base files
w: regex_search_files tool greps the user's indexed documents with an optional path prefix and before/after context lines, capping matches and returning line-numbered results.
tool_call arguments are validated locally against the deferred tool's schema before dispatch, returning precise errors.

f: MCP OAuth for headless and remote setups
w: Moves the browser callback steps of MCP OAuth from a loopback listener into the authenticated dashboard, so remote/headless gateways can complete logins.
CLI subcommands add, remove, list, enable and disable MCP servers in user or project settings.

f: MCP client TLS certificates and identity headers
w: Remote MCP connections can present TLS client certificates and a resolved identity header, with URL validation before connecting.

f: MCP credentials from enterprise or cloud identity
w: mcp_enterprise_managed_auth derives MCP credentials from the signed-in enterprise identity via token exchange, keyring-only storage and staged commits.
Keepalive probes, suspect-marking with lazy verification, in-flight call fail-fast and application-backed liveness parsing with user-facing status text.
Settings to add, edit, enable and inspect MCP servers including OAuth and header config with ownership indicators.
Detects when a model stuffs a Python literal (list or dict) into the command string and returns a corrective error instead of running it.

f: Managed Node runtime for stdio MCP servers
w: Runs every stdio MCP server on Hermes' own managed Node and detects native addons compiled for a different Node ABI.
Uses system rg if present, otherwise downloads the pinned ripgrep release for the platform into the cache.
Plugin kit for mini-games (gamelets) that run in widgets with host-owned lifecycle and request calls.

f: Model runs a slash command as a tool
w: Lets the model itself invoke a defined slash command by name with arguments and receive its expanded content, gated behind the runSlashCommand experiment.
When an edit's search string doesn't match, an LLM is asked to minimally correct the search/replace strings (cached, 40-second timeout) before giving up.
cron_create, cron_list and cron_delete let the model schedule in-session or durable recurring prompts.
stage_widgets tool lets the model spawn, update and close UI widgets with component props on the desktop.

f: Multiple edits to one file in one call
w: Applies several find-and-replace edits to one file atomically in sequence.
Switches between letta, Claude (default), codex and none tool presets per agent or conversation, picking automatically by model provider.
Durable per-agent notes: create, get by id, list/search, patch title/body or exact text, replace and delete by text; all mutations go through one server-owned service with revision checks.

f: Offer tools only when the context fits
w: Actions can declare allowed domains so they are only offered to the model on matching pages.
Desktop runs stdio MCP servers and handles lobehub:// one-click plugin install.

f: Only enabled skills visible in sandboxes
w: Materializes /mnt/skills from enabled skills only so disabling a skill also hides it from shell and file tools across local, Docker, provisioner and E2B sandboxes.
Adds branch path commands that resolve, find, validate and edit a specific value inside Markdown, JSON/JSONC, JSONL or YAML workspace files via an oc:// address.
Per-tool transforms reshape tool inputs/outputs separately for the model, storage and UI (e.g. redact secrets or shrink large outputs).

f: Per-model tool sets (e.g. apply_patch for GPT)
w: Model metadata can include or exclude specific tools; for OpenAI models reached through routers it swaps apply_diff/write_to_file for apply_patch to match each model family's preferred edit format.

Multiplexed surfaces (gateway, dashboard/TUI, cron) resolve TERMINAL_* policy per turn and per profile instead of mirroring it into os.environ, so one profile's backend settings never leak into another's.
Users store key-value variables per session that are kept in shared preferences (e.g. for Dify inputs).
The skill section of config.json is flattened into SKILL_<NAME>_<KEY> environment variables at startup (real env wins).
Optional patched-zsh execve wrapper intercepts each exec inside a shell script so individual subcommands can be approved or escalated out of the sandbox.
One session-persistent child per (owner, mode, interpreter, cwd, tool-set) runs one code cell per call so state survives across execute_code calls, with an LRU cap and per-child kernel disposal.

f: Personal skill library on a shared gateway
w: On a shared Gateway, authenticated operators keep personal skills (create, import SKILL.md/ZIP or add from ClawHub) with revisions, without workspace write rights.
A /launch route opens a modal from a URL naming plugins and parameters, letting users fill inputs and start a conversation with those plugins attached.
The `hermes plugins` composite UI toggles general plugins and picks memory-provider/context-engine plugins.
Checks installed extensions for updates and updates them, with notifications in the TUI.
`hermes plugins validate` runs catalog admission checks (manifest, desktop plugin.js lint, language packs) used by CI.
Plugins can contribute slash commands surfaced in CLI chat.

Before a command runs, pure guard functions validate the workdir, steer foreground long-lived commands to background mode, block lifecycle commands under a supervised gateway, and stop risky git ops on the Windows self-repo.
CLI for quickstart, run/stop server/UI/MCP, workflows, tasks, credentials, schedules, browser sessions, config and status.
Registers built-in, MCP and project-discovered tools; a configured discovery command can emit extra tool declarations that run via a call command.

Merges MCP servers from a project .roo/mcp.json with global settings, hot-reloads and cleans up project servers when that file changes or is deleted, and restarts a server whenever any of its configured watchPaths change.
Runs Google Search grounding through the Gemini API and returns an answer with inline citation markers and a source list.
Publishes generated HTML pages locally, to OSS or a host publisher and opens them in the browser.
Runs Python in a web worker via Pyodide for calculations and data work.

f: Read PDF and Office documents as text
w: Extracts text from PDF attachments locally in a PDFium-based worker and renders low-text pages as images for vision-capable models.
Consecutive identical reads/searches are counted per task and the model is warned or stopped when it loops; any other tool call resets the counter.

f: Read or view an image for vision
w: Model attaches a local image file to its context for visual inspection, with resizing and an original-detail option.

f: Read the file open in the editor
w: Returns the contents of the file currently open in the IDE editor.
Exact string replacement edits that refuse to modify a file the model has not read in this session or that changed on disk since, preserving UTF-8 BOM and encoding.

f: Record tool actions as a reusable workflow
w: Records CLI/MCP browser actions as a trajectory that can be fetched and turned into workflows.
A bounded scan of failed-command output maps known error patterns to one short, actionable recovery hint appended to the result.

f: Refuse to read .env and other secret files
w: Assistant tools to read sources/files with sensitive-file refusal (all .env variants except .env.example).

f: Reject lazy "rest of code unchanged" edits
w: Rejects edits and writes whose new content contains lazy placeholders such as '// rest of code unchanged'.

f: Rename, disable and permission individual commands
w: Every plugin command can be renamed, disabled or given admin permission from the dashboard, with conflict detection between plugins.
Wraps MCP transports to repair non-compliant server responses, e.g. missing structuredContent for tools with output schemas.
Re-reading an unchanged file range returns a short stub instead of the full content, with dedup state that survives compression but serves one full recovery read after compaction.
Experimental TaskOutcome model lets finish actions report a semantic outcome for a task.
The agent can reset a broken terminal session, killing it and starting a fresh shell.
Search file contents by regex with ripgrep, include filters and bounded results.
$role <name> makes the bot play a role from a built-in roles library (fuzzy match) or custom roles/ JSON files; $停止扮演 stops.

f: Run commands on the host from a Flatpak
w: Detects the Flatpak sandbox and wraps shell commands in flatpak-spawn --host so they run on the host.
Connect to Postgres/MySQL/MSSQL and let the agent list tables, read schemas and query.
Terminal sandboxes are created lazily per task, reaped after idle time, torn down on manual/atexit cleanup, and the user is told when an environment was recreated.
Per-agent working directory with write/replace/read actions across md, txt, json, csv, jsonl, pdf, docx, html and images; todo.md for long tasks.
One env builder for every spawned child (terminal, execute_code, background, delegation, MCP stdio) drops Hermes-managed credentials by a data-driven policy and pins the served profile home.
my lets the agent inspect runtime state and change permitted settings (model preset, runtime options, a scratchpad) with audit logging and restricted keys.

f: Semantic search over indexed files and code
w: semantic_search_files runs query extraction and vector search over the user's (and agent's) knowledge base, returning compiled references and skipping queries already run earlier in the research.

f: Send a message or file to the user mid-run
w: Unified messaging/bot-management tool lets agents send messages and manage bots across platforms.
Bundled sequential-thinking server for structured step-by-step reasoning.

f: Shared typed content blocks and actions
w: Shared package defines message content block and computer action types with converters between them.

f: Shell command parsing for permission checks
w: Parses commands with web-tree-sitter and shell-quote to strip wrappers and find every root command for permission checks, across bash, PowerShell and cmd.
Settings for shell-integration timeout, a command delay, a PowerShell counter workaround, a zsh EOL-mark fix, Oh My Zsh and ZDOTDIR handling, to make output capture reliable across shells.
Silently acknowledges platform /start pings (e.g. Telegram bot start) on messaging gateways instead of sending them to the model.
Admins whitelist which skills/commands agents may run without prompting.
Optional agents/openai.yaml gives a skill display name, icons and UI metadata validated against plugin asset rules.

f: Skills scoped per mode or agent
w: Discovers SKILL.md skills in global/project skills/ and skills-{mode}/ directories (symlinks allowed) and limits each skill to modes listed in frontmatter modeSlugs, which Cline's flat skills cannot do.
MCP server exposing skill discovery and install to any agent.

f: Skills that bring their MCP servers
w: When a skill declares MCP servers it needs, Codex proposes installing them through the policy-aware catalog after user consent.

f: Strip terminal escape codes from tool output
w: Strips full ECMA-48 escape sequences (CSI, OSC, DCS/SOS/PM/APC, nF, Fp/Fe/Fs, 8-bit C1) from subprocess output so models never copy them into files.
delegate_task spawns child agents with fresh conversations, their own task_id/terminal session and a focused system prompt, as one goal or a concurrency-capped batch.
Delegation config knobs choose the child's provider/model and credentials (including credential pools), independent of the parent.
Streams child progress lines to the parent's console/TUI with batch tags and builds child system prompts.

f: Subagent result budgeting and cost rollup
w: Child summaries are budgeted (spilled when long), tool traces summarized, lifecycle hooks fired and child costs rolled up into a footer.
Resolves which toolsets a child may use (parent's minus child-blocked tools, optional MCP inheritance) so subagents can't escalate capabilities.
Built-in tool that pauses with a plan file path for host approval; hosts resume with approved or revise-with-feedback.

Rewrites real `sudo` to `sudo -S -p ''` with a quote-aware shell scanner, caches the password per scope, prompts via /dev/tty when needed, probes NOPASSWD, and rewrites compound background commands into brace groups.
Tool output (e.g. long shell output) can be summarised by a model when configured, to save context.
Loads files or directories (respecting .gitignore) and returns an LLM summary focused on a question in one call.
Creates an unexpected experience by discovering and combining other enabled skills.
Assistants with instructions, avatar emoji and parameters, switchable per thread.
Invokes async tools from synchronous agent paths safely.

Foreground results get cwd dual-write, a plugin transform hook, head/tail truncation with disk spill, redaction, exit-code semantics notes and verification-evidence recording before reaching the model.
$开始冒险 starts an AI-driven text adventure with an optional backstory; $停止冒险 ends it.

Manages the user's todo list (write/create/update/complete/cancel/delete/list/clear), addressing items by visible content or paraphrase and returning stable refs when ambiguous; duplicates need confirmation.

f: Tmux pane pool for parallel commands
w: TmuxPanePool keeps a fixed pool of panes in one tmux session so parallel tool calls run terminal commands concurrently.
Repairs string-typed args emitted against a tool's JSON Schema ("42", "true", JSON-encoded arrays/objects, including nested) before dispatch.

f: Tool call approval pause and resume
w: When tool permissions are enabled, tool calls pause for user approval; approved calls are drained and the turn resumes.
Lists registered tools available in the server for clients to build agent specs.
A central alias registry (e.g. write_file to write_to_file, search_and_replace to edit) resolves alternate tool names models emit, while keeping the alias in conversation history.
Records which component (core, MCP, plugin, middleware) contributed each tool for attribution and trust decisions.

Caches tool results in an in-memory LRU and an on-disk store keyed by sha256(tool + canonical args) and tagged with the tool version; side-effect tools opt out and the disk tier runs outputs through a privacy redactor.

f: Tool schema sanitizer for strict providers
w: Rewrites tool JSON schemas so llama.cpp grammar conversion and Anthropic accept them (missing properties, bare strings, type arrays, nullable anyOf).
A tool can call suspend() with a typed payload to pause the agent run and later resume with resumeData supplied by a human or system.
$tool runs chatgpt-tool-hub tools (search, math, messaging and more) in multi-tool or pure single-tool mode.

f: Tools stream progress to the client
w: Tools receive a writer to stream custom progress chunks to the client while executing.

f: Tools to list and read chat attachments and uploads
w: Uploads are staged and published atomically; current-run uploads are injected with heading outlines, while list_uploaded_files pages earlier-turn files with stable cursors.

f: Toolset sampling for batch data generation
w: Maps toolset names to independent enable probabilities so batch runs sample varied tool combinations per prompt.

f: URL gating for web extract (SSRF, secrets)
w: Every extract URL passes secret-URL refusal, SSRF filtering, strict provider resolution and per-URL website policy before the disk cache or vendor is consulted.

f: Verify a write by reading it back
w: After write_file, the written content is read back and compared so the result carries a verified flag (including surrogate/encoding round-trips).
Visual agent flows with typed steps (API call, LLM instruction, web scraping) executed with variable resolution.
get_weather tool that geocodes a place and returns forecast data, shown in a weather widget.
Fetch a URL and return readable markdown or text, with size caps.
Install web mini-apps that run in partitioned webviews with granted capabilities (AI, clipboard, file, network, notification, storage) and quotas.

TTL-bounded caches (default 20 min): an in-memory single-flighted search memo so concurrent identical queries share one paid request, and a cross-process disk cache for extracts that sits after every safety check; only successes are cached.
Wolfram Alpha computation tool.

f: Workspace and toolchain facts in the system prompt
w: Auto-injects workspace environment info (filesystem roots, sandbox, mount states) into the system prompt so the model knows which paths shell and file tools can reach.
Relative file-tool paths resolve against the task's terminal cwd (never the process cwd), with ~ expansion per profile and a warning when the workspace diverges.
Model edits files with a custom *** Begin Patch envelope (Add/Delete/Update/Move hunks with @@ context), parsed by a formal grammar and applied atomically.

f: Customize › Tools page and composer plug menu
w: Branch's own Tools page (Connectors, Skills, Plugins, Command-line tools), the icon-only plug menu in the composer, add/allow buttons, catalogue filter and per-Trunk access chips.

f: WASM and script tools with memory/CPU limits
w: Owner-written JavaScript and WebAssembly tools run in a capability-limited sandbox with declared host capabilities and resource caps.

f: Assistant drafts an add-on for review
w: The assistant drafts a plugin, skill or filter that the owner reviews and switches on.

f: Add-skill dialog with draft and suggestions
w: Branch's add-skill dialog: describe a skill, draft it, choose a source, add it, and add suggested skills (off for every Trunk until chosen).
Show what a tool call or exposed MCP tool would do without running it.
Branch-specific commands that open its own screens and owner settings from the window or terminal.
Bring Branch's terminal-only commands to the window's command table.
Owner idea: copy a capability (tool, skill or setup) from one place and paste it into another Trunk or computer.

f: Branch HTTP API, OpenAPI description and SDKs
w: Branch's own HTTP API with an OpenAPI description and TypeScript, Python, Go and React SDKs.
Call Branch from C through a foreign-function interface.

f: Browser side panel and embeddable chat widget
w: Chat in a browser extension side panel or an embeddable widget.
Download videos, read captions and make short videos.

f: Agent-to-agent protocols and external agent platforms
w: A2A both ways, Agent Protocol task API, fleet and handoff to another device; call hosted agent platforms.
Run a plugin against a test suite and compare results with a baseline before enabling it.
Subscribe to MCP server events (events/list, subscribe, unsubscribe) with Standard Webhooks signature checks so events start automations.

f: Never run a slash command from an edited message
w: Editing a message that contains a command must not start the command again.
The mail source saves UIDVALIDITY with its cursor and restarts the sync when it changes.

f: Check scripts keep state between runs
w: A watcher script keeps a small capped state and wakes the assistant only when something changed (condition watchers).
A signed list of known-bad plugins, skills and MCP servers blocks installs and switches off installed ones with the reason shown.

f: Portals: preview servers on another computer
w: See a preview server that runs on another of the owner's computers.
Two non-conflicting saves to the same Markdown file are merged instead of refusing the older one.
Upload a managed file and expose it to a task through a read-only mount.
An embedded code editor inside Branch.
Watch files for AI comments and act on them.
Configurable chat engines over knowledge.
A local studio to try agents and workflows.
Use LiteLLM as a model provider.
Two-way live audio/text streaming.
Operate an Android device over ADB.
A Gradio web interface.
A troubleshooting agent that runs, reads failures and fixes in a loop.
Search X (Twitter) with the owner's connected account.
API keys and sign-ins for model providers and connectors, with account order.
Branch's own slash picker rows and selection behaviour in the composer.
From a chat, /improve files a change to Branch itself for the owner's review.
/screen and /screen stop show the live computer in the owner's DM.
A dialectic peer model of the person.
Each action has one route, with no duplicate hidden identities (for example MCP GitHub vs gh).

f: Desktop app shell with bundled backend
w: A native desktop window (Electron or Tauri) that starts or attaches to the agent engine and renders the chat app, with menus and IPC.
One engine process serves every window and terminal; new clients attach to it and it shuts down when nobody uses it.

f: Startup splash with boot progress and failure recovery
w: While the engine starts, a splash shows progress; if it fails, a diagnosed cause with retry and sign-in actions replaces the blank window.
If the window's UI crashes, a recovery screen appears instead of a blank window.

f: Typed UI-to-engine RPC with reconnect and event replay
w: The window talks to the engine over one typed channel that reconnects with backoff and replays missed events, so the UI never loses state on a blip.
Main process and window talk through typed procedures so both sides agree on inputs and outputs.
Register several machines or engines (this computer, NAS, cloud, other PCs), name them, and switch between them from one window.
Connect the window to an engine on another machine through the system OpenSSH client, so ~/.ssh/config, agents and ProxyJump just work.

f: Remote engine first-run setup with native OAuth
w: On first launch, point the app at an existing remote engine (URL, auth, connection test, browser OAuth with PKCE) instead of installing locally.
On Windows, the desktop app can run and connect to engines inside WSL distributions.

f: Login-shell PATH and Windows platform shims
w: The app finds CLI tools the way the user's shell does and ships Windows shims so bundled helpers start on Windows.
The window reopens where and how it was left, kept on a visible display.
Open extra windows (pop-out chats, sub-windows) that share the same session state.

f: Frameless title bar with themed native controls
w: No OS title bar: the app's own row is the top of the window, and the native min/max/close buttons follow the app's theme.
A see-through slider and OS materials (mica, acrylic, vibrancy) for the window.
A tray/menu-bar icon with open, new session, settings, update and quit, plus a running-session badge.

f: Close or minimise to tray and keep running
w: Closing the window hides it to the tray so agents and the gateway keep working; reopen from the tray.
The tray or menu-bar icon animates and changes to show working, idle, needs-you and recovery, with a stop control during runs.
A tray menu section shows provider usage and daily cost history.
A Tauri tray app on Linux with quick chat, gateway discovery and keep-awake.

f: Status bar plugin for tiling desktops
w: An optional panel plugin shows agents, active sessions, attention dots and a quick prompt.

f: Keep the computer awake while working
w: Prevents sleep while any task is running, via OS inhibitors, as a toggle.

f: OS notifications when work finishes or needs you
w: Native notifications for finished turns and approvals, with click-through actions that open the right conversation.
In the terminal, OSC 9/99/777 escape codes or the bell raise OS notifications when a turn needs attention.
Selectable sounds (and haptics) when a turn finishes or something needs you, with per-event settings.

f: Agent state in the window/tab title
w: The window or tab title shows the conversation title and an emoji/marker for the agent's state.

f: Inbox of pending asks and finished work
w: One durable inbox collects what needs the owner (approvals, questions, installs) and what finished, collapsing duplicates, with per-row actions.
The agent can push a structured notice (job finished, approval needed, reminder) to the in-app rail, desktop and phone.
Short in-window toasts and notification cards (who needs you, who is done) that dismiss themselves, with undo.
app:// links open sessions, add a gateway or send a prompt.

f: Confirm before installing from a link
w: Installing an extension from a link shows the exact command and source in a confirmation first.
Checks for and installs updates with a clear prompt and progress, per install type and channel.
Ship UI fixes without a full reinstall by updating the renderer bundle in place.
After an update, a What's new dialog and release notes one tap away.
Dismissible info/warning banners (admin, usage, plan, lockdown) with action buttons.

f: Error cards that explain the fix
w: Failures show typed cards (context full, limit, model, provider, key) with likely causes and a fix link.
Detects local-model out-of-memory and missing runtime dependencies and explains what to do.
Runs environment, provider and network checks and shows results with fixes.
View the app and engine logs from the window.
A debug view of the raw agent event stream.
See the conversation's system message, injected context and available tools with schemas.
Captures main-process errors to a log and watches for event-loop lag.
Locks down navigation, window-open, data-URL limits and webviews in the desktop renderer.
File reads over IPC are allowed only from registered windows' main frames.
Configure HTTP(S) proxy for the desktop app with error diagnostics.
Move the app's data directory to another location.
Reset the app to defaults, listing exactly what will be deleted.
When the OS launches the app as the whole GUI, it runs one fullscreen window hosting agent views.
The main chat thread: user and assistant messages, steps, cards and command output, with progressive loading.

f: Fast long conversations (windowed or virtualized transcript)
w: Long threads open fast: only the latest turns are drawn, with 'Show earlier', or rows are virtualized.
Streamed words appear smoothly, like typing, without re-rendering every token.
When several sessions stream at once, updates are coalesced and the focused one gets priority so the window stays responsive.
While a reply streams, only the unfinished tail block is re-parsed and unfinished Markdown is closed, so settled blocks are reused.
Replies render Markdown correctly: lists, tables, code with highlighting, links, safely sanitized and cached per message.

f: Code blocks with copy, label and lazy highlighting
w: Code blocks get a Copy button and a language label; colour highlighting loads lazily; long blocks can start collapsed.
Inline and block LaTeX renders as math in the window.
Mermaid code blocks render as diagrams with pan, zoom and export.

f: Markdown extensions: footnotes, alerts, fenced blocks
w: Footnotes, GitHub-style NOTE/WARNING alerts and ::: custom blocks render in replies.
@mentions of people, models or agents render as tokens inside messages.
Agent output can render as charts, with an 'Open larger' view.

f: Clickable file paths and links in replies
w: File paths and links in replies become clickable and open the file or page.
Switch a reply between rendered and raw Markdown, for example to copy it.

f: Detail level toggles (reasoning, tool details, collapsed blocks)
w: Choose how much to show: tool calls concise or expanded, reasoning shown or hidden, details blocks open or closed, or a focus view with just prompt and answer.
The model's reasoning shows as a collapsed section you can open.
Each tool call shows as a card with arguments, status, icon and expandable output, with tailored bodies per tool.

f: Folded step line for consecutive tool calls
w: Runs of tool calls fold into one line that says in plain words what was done and how it ended.
Running commands show a live, ANSI-aware output tail and exit status.
Edits and commands appear while the tool arguments are still streaming.
A side panel renders tool results by type: screenshots, terminal, diffs, files, search results, reports.
Hover a message for copy, edit, retry, delete, feedback, flag, remember and read aloud.

f: Edit an earlier message and resend (rewind)
w: Edit a previous message and resend it, choosing to rewind the conversation, the files or both.

f: Quote a reply or ask about a selection
w: Select text in a reply to quote it into the next message or ask/explain it.

f: Save a message as an image or print
w: Capture a message as an image or print a conversation.
Under each reply: tokens, time, cost and which model answered.
A sent message shows at once as sending, then flips to error with Retry if the engine doesn't confirm.
Your question stays pinned at the top while its long answer scrolls under it, with task actions in the header.
The thread follows new content unless you scrolled up; a 'Jump to latest' button says how much is below.
Scrollbars show only while scrolling, or always if the user prefers.
Move between messages in a long conversation.
When switching message branches, scroll to the switched message.
Switch messages between chat bubbles and full-width document layout.
Comfortable, Wide or Full conversation width on wide screens.
Choose chat text size and zoom the whole interface.
Pick the app font, including installed easy-reading faces, with the theme font as fallback.
Right-to-left languages lay out correctly, per message or per chat.

f: Rich composer with inline reference chips
w: The message box turns @files, @urls and /commands into chips, keeps its own undo, and has a + menu for inserts.
Enter never sends a half-composed Japanese/Chinese/Korean word, in every Enter-to-send box.
The message box grows with the text and can be resized by a grip.
Unsent text is kept per conversation across crashes, restarts and closed windows.

f: Large paste collapses into an attachment
w: Big pastes become a placeholder or file attachment instead of flooding the message box.
Up in an empty box recalls earlier messages; a stash keeps a half-written draft for later.
Typing / opens a filtered, frequency-ordered list of commands and skills with descriptions.

f: Saved prompts as custom slash commands
w: Create, edit and reuse saved prompts that appear as / commands.

f: @ mentions for files, agents and material
w: Typing @ searches files, skills, agents and people in one filtered list that works where the caret is.
As you type, a model suggests the rest of the prompt inline.

f: Vim keys in the message box
w: Optional Vim normal/insert modes with motions and operators in the composer.
Open the current draft in $EDITOR and load the result back.
Choose whether Enter sends or adds a line.
Turn spellcheck in the message box on or off.
Typing : opens an emoji picker.
The message box is usable at once while the engine starts; the first send waits until ready.
Typing words like stop or wait interrupts the running agent.

f: Prompt queue while the agent works
w: Messages typed while the agent works queue up; you can edit, reorder or remove them.

f: Side question without derailing the task

f: State-machine agents: the model only picks a legal event
w: Agent control flow is a statechart; at each decision the model is shown only the events allowed in the current state and proposes one, the machine validates and transitions, and ready-made machines cover tool loops, routers, supervisors, handoffs and parallel steps, with an event log for replay and resume.

A small flow language and state-machine runtime that pins conversations to designed paths (e.g. authenticate before support), chaining input, dialogue, retrieval, execution and output rails around the model.

When a session goes idle with unfinished todos, a countdown injects a continuation prompt so the agent keeps going, skipping when the user aborted, a question is pending, compaction is running, tokens ran out, or progress has stagnated.

f: Rubric outcome supervisor with revision loop
w: A session can carry an outcome with a rubric or rule verifier; after each run a grader decides satisfied, needs_revision (its reason is fed back as the next user message), max_iterations_reached or interrupted, and every verdict is stored with token usage on the session.

f: Automatic mentor intervention and reflector-guided wind-down
w: An execution monitor counts identical and total tool calls; past a threshold it automatically asks an adviser agent (optionally a stronger model) to analyse progress and appends its advice to the tool result, and near the hard tool-call limit a reflector steers the agent to finish cleanly. The authors measured about 2x better results for a 27B local model.

Failures are retried at the lowest layer that can fix them (tool call, backend, agent runtime, gateway daemon), each with bounded attempts and a cleanup deadline, and only escalate upward when a unit stops making progress; overload is handled separately by lowering caps.

f: Render old history as images to cut tokens
w: Moves long text (older history, tool schemas) into rendered PNG image blocks for Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini requests when a density gate says it saves tokens; the original text stays recoverable and any error falls back to plain text.

Context is selected under a token budget (knapsack over fragments) and every omitted piece gets a receipt and a content-addressed handle so the agent or user can recover the exact original bytes later and see what was kept or dropped and why.

f: Content-aware tool-output compression with retrievable originals
w: Detects whether a tool result is a log, JSON, diff, HTML, code listing, search results or a table and shrinks it with a matching compressor; every original is stored in a local SQLite store so the agent can pull the full bytes back by query.

f: ObservationPack: stable handles for repeated large tool results
w: Large tool outputs that would be replayed in later requests are replaced by stable handles kept in a local ledger, with exact paged recall when the model needs the text again.

f: Deterministic layered token-compression codec for tool observations
w: A no-model-call compression pipeline shrinks prompts and tool observations through stacked lossless-style layers (deduplication, a static and a dynamic codebook/dictionary, JSON compaction, path and whitespace folding), cutting tokens before the request goes out.
A cheap helper model condenses long diagnostic logs into a compact receipt, accepted only if every quoted line exactly matches the archived original; otherwise the full result is kept.

f: Agent-directed context reduction by message tags
w: Every message and tool result gets a short tag; the agent calls ctx_reduce to drop or shrink tagged items it no longer needs and ctx_expand to bring a compressed item back, so the context is trimmed surgically instead of by a compaction pause.

f: Cost-aware compaction decision (cache invalidation vs savings)
w: Before compacting, the engine estimates whether the token savings outweigh the cost of invalidating and rewriting the prompt cache, and adjusts the target from measured context growth, so compaction runs only when it pays.

f: Typed AI functions (cast, classify, extract, generate, @fn)
w: One-call helpers that turn free text into a given type: cast to a schema, classify into an enum or label list, extract all values of a type, generate N typed items, summarize, and @fn to give a plain function signature an LLM body. Useful as building blocks for automations and skills.

f: AI-slop detector and writing quality gate
w: Scores text for tells of bland AI writing (hedging openers, stock vocabulary, negative parallelism, em-dash overuse) per 1,000 words and returns pass/warn/fail with relaxed, balanced and strict presets calibrated on a blog corpus.

f: Non-LLM goal planner that replans after every action
w: Typed actions declare preconditions and effects; an A* GOAP planner (or a utility planner) finds an action sequence to the goal, replans after each action from the new world state, prunes irrelevant actions and detects unreachable goals, so flows can combine known steps in new orders without asking the model to plan.

Rules constrain the loop: a tool may only run after another, must run at a given step, has a call limit or consecutive-call limit, or needs the user's permission first; the runner enforces them each step so the agent follows a reliable procedure without a hard-coded workflow.

f: Overnight autonomous runs with a morning report
w: A background 'overnight' run manager (start/status/log/review/cancel) with a manifest that tracks wake time, a coordinator session and a morning report posted when the owner wakes, so the agent works unattended overnight and reports back.

f: Endless continuation: auto next steps, ideas and goals
w: Opt-in modes where, after each reply, the agent automatically continues with the next logical steps (including tests), dreams up and implements improvement ideas for the codebase, or, when a /goal is met, writes and starts the next goal.

f: Batched command run with output bindings
w: The model sends one command_run containing several shell, patch and planning steps where later steps reference earlier outputs through placeholders; the runtime executes the whole chain (streaming, with file locks) without another model round trip, cutting tokens sharply on coding tasks.

Before any work starts the agent interviews the user, scores remaining ambiguity with evidence after each answer, tracks answer provenance and 'decide later' items, and only crystallizes a testable spec (seed with acceptance criteria) once ambiguity falls below a threshold.

f: Read the room: friction signals change agent behaviour
w: A deterministic lexical reader scores each owner message for friction (caps, 'still broken', repeated corrections, interrupts, denials, urgency) and a reducer turns it into a policy: act on corrections at once and narrowly, explore when curious, get terse when urgent, and weigh forceful instructions more in memory.

f: Desires that drive autonomous heartbeat time
w: The agent keeps a store of its own desires; the heartbeat picks an actionable one to focus on, pursues it, records activity, and desires evolve or are reviewed over time, so scheduled autonomous time has its own motivation besides standing chores.

f: One protocol over many agent harnesses, with a conformance suite
w: Codex, Claude Code, OpenHands, Aider, Hermes, Gemini CLI and others run behind one Responses-style API with sessions, streaming, files, cancellation and structured failure reasons, and a published protocol with a conformance test kit checks each harness adapter.

f: Per-step persona switch with relevance-filtered history
w: Each loop iteration predicts the best next step, picks the best-fit persona (researcher, developer, CSV analyst, synthesizer) for it, and rebuilds the chat history from only the chunks most relevant to that prediction before deciding which function to run.

Keeps the model's full reasoning only for the most recent turns and asks it to carry forward short notes in normal content, so long multi-turn coding runs keep deep thinking without the context exploding.

At a chosen decision point the agent generates K candidates in parallel, scores each with a check (for example running the tests) and keeps the highest-scoring one instead of committing to a single answer.

A /harness command swaps the whole agent harness (system prompt, tool set and schemas, compaction prompt, guidance) to emulate Claude Code, Kimi Code, Kimi CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode, Pi, SWE-agent, mini-SWE-agent, Terminus and others, with routing that picks the harness a given model performs best in.

f: Process-as-code orchestration with journal replay, forking and breakpoints
w: A workflow is a JS process file whose task, parallel, sleep, subprocess and breakpoint calls are recorded in an append-only run journal; each iteration replays the journal to a deterministic point, so runs resume, fork from any step and stop at human approval breakpoints while the coding agent just executes the next pending effect.

f: Sentinel autopilot: nudge, escalate to a person, or stop when a long run parks
w: When the lead agent pauses before its goal is done, a classifier decides whether to nudge it onward, escalate a genuine blocker to the owner over Telegram or Slack with a resume token, or treat the goal as done; off by default and enabled per team.

f: Hook sandbox: dry-run a hook with simulated input
w: Pick any configured hook, feed it a simulated event payload and see its stdout, stderr, exit code and transformed result, run in an isolated environment with only PATH/HOME/TMPDIR and no API tokens or credentials, plus validation of the hook definition.

f: Backfill a schedule over past dates
w: A scheduled trigger can be backfilled for a chosen past date range, creating the runs that would have happened, with pause/resume and a banner showing backfill progress.

For a big coding task the agent first interviews the owner in batches of questions with a follow-up budget, compiles a PRD, splits it into atomic 'beads' with a dependency graph and coverage revision, executes each bead in an isolated worktree loop with a completion checker, then generates and runs a final test pass with a file-effects audit.

f: Focus items with agent-managed bound triggers
w: The agent keeps a list of focus items it is tracking and must bind every task trigger it creates (cron, once, interval, HTTP poll, on-message from a given agent or person, webhook) to a focus item; it adjusts its own triggers as work evolves and cancels them when the focus is completed.

f: Discover automatable workflows from recorded activity
w: A scheduled discovery agent reviews the captured screen and audio history, finds repeated work the user does, and proposes workflows with step evidence that the user can accept, run and share; an eval script scores discovery quality.

f: Application tracker with follow-up cadence and funnel stats
w: A tracker of every evaluated and applied job with dedup and repost detection, follow-up reminders on a cadence after the applied date, and funnel velocity and discard analytics in a TUI dashboard.

f: Proactive sentinel that learns routines and predicts tasks
w: Attention producers (active threads, project rhythm, recently abandoned work, daily plan, rejected-offer cooldown) feed a routine learner and task discoverer; a planner tick decides whether to nudge or act, derives do-not-disturb windows, defers, and tracks feedback on each offer.

f: Agent-owned outcomes over weeks with reviews, metrics and owner action items
w: Hand one lead agent an outcome with a definition of done and optional metrics; it turns it into roadmap tasks and schedules, reviews progress on a cadence recording evidence and next steps, files access requests for missing capabilities and action items for things only the owner can do, and can only propose completion; the owner marks it done.

f: Public form and chat page that starts an automation and returns its answer
w: A form trigger or chat trigger gives an automation its own web page; whoever fills the form or chats starts the run, and a 'return response' step sends the result back to that page.

A Markdown playbook is co-written with the agent and run from the same document: regions are marked, verbs such as interview, simplify, challenge-assumptions and crystallize act on them, and runs report back into the document.

f: Typed runbooks compiled into skills with resumable checkpoints
