w: A YAML runbook declares steps (agent, script, loop, parallel, branch) whose inputs and outputs are JSON-schema files; a compiler checks the contracts close and the graph has no cycles, then emits a SKILL.md plus checkpoint scripts so a broken run resumes at the last finished step.

f: Scheduled-job pipeline graph and weekly heatmap
w: Declares pipelines as edges between scheduled jobs (job A's artifact feeds job B), draws them as a DAG with health per job, and shows a weekly heatmap of when jobs fire.

f: Track published posts and run a daily retro
w: Every published post is recorded in a local database; a scheduled job fetches views, likes and comments per platform, flags pending or failed publishes, and feeds a daily review of what worked.

f: Nestable reusable blocks usable in any text field
w: A library of named blocks (plain text, prompt, code, module call or whole workflow) that can be referenced from any prompt or text field and nest inside each other, so shared instructions and computed values are reused consistently.

f: Scheduled social engagement in the owner's voice with per-platform limits
w: A scheduler runs one agent per social platform (LinkedIn, X, Reddit, Bluesky, Threads, Medium, Dev.to and more) in its own signed-in browser profile, following the owner's identity, voice and content strategy, with daily per-platform action limits, a run lock and a quality audit of what was posted.

f: Auto Run playbooks over markdown checklists
w: Point the agent at a folder of markdown task documents; each unchecked item runs in a fresh session with clean context, gets ticked off with a synopsis, documents can loop, human-only steps pause with a banner, and saved playbooks run headless from the CLI or cron.

f: Recorded phone macros with guarded replay and agent hand-off
w: Record a task as a macro, then replay it step by step only while the screen matches the recorded state; on a mismatch the run hands off to the agent to recover instead of tapping blindly.

f: Meeting prep briefs before calendar meetings
w: A scheduler watches the calendar and, before each meeting, writes a prep brief from what the knowledge graph knows about the attendees and topics, and notifies the user; a popup also detects a meeting starting.

Polls a watchlist of social accounts within set hours and a spend budget, scores fresh posts for relevance, retrieves the owner's context and drafts suggested replies that are delivered for review and never posted automatically.

f: Cost estimate for a recurring agent routine before enabling it
w: Estimates a routine's monthly token spend from its cadence, how often runs are no-op, report or action at its autonomy level, and the share of stable cacheable context, so the owner sees the cost before switching it on.

f: Real-time co-editing of a workflow with cursors and comment threads
w: Several people edit the same workflow at once through a CRDT over WebSocket, see each other's cursors in their own colours, and leave threaded comments with @mentions pinned to places on the canvas.

A daily notes page (also a desktop HUD/pill) where writing a task item or mentioning the assistant gets picked up within minutes; a proactive observer agent also reads the page and leaves inline comments or drafts a plan, without the user opening a chat.
Each scheduled job keeps up to 20 deduplicated lessons its runs saved (oldest dropped first), which are given to the next run so recurring jobs stop repeating mistakes.
A workflow step that collects events for a subscriber over a time window (regular or with backoff, or on a schedule) and sends one combined notification instead of many.

f: Split a failing multi-part task into child tasks (mitosis)
w: When a task holding several deliverables fails the first time, it is split into focused child tasks linked as dependencies, deduplicated against existing children under a workspace lock.

f: Deep-work projects that assign steps to the human
w: A goal is parsed into a project plan whose tasks are split between agents and the human; dependent tasks are scheduled, and human-required tasks are pushed to the owner's chat apps and wait for him before downstream agent work continues.

f: Feed subscriptions that post new items into chats
w: Owners subscribe a chat channel to RSS, Reddit or YouTube feeds; a poller fetches with rate limits and posts each new item as a message, tracked per subscription so nothing repeats.

f: Inbox work loops with ship gates and a health governor
w: Long-running loops pull items from Gmail or Slack into a ledger, triage them and prepare outputs (labels, reply drafts); each outgoing action is held for the owner unless a declared policy or a revocable grant allows it, and a governor quarantines, throttles or pings when a loop's queue or outputs look unhealthy.

f: Two-way sync between visual agent builder and TypeScript code
w: Agents built on the visual canvas can be pulled as TypeScript files and edited in code, then pushed back; pulling again merges into existing files, preserving comments, key order and variable names, and reports conflicts.

f: Brain dump triage into an Eisenhower matrix
w: The owner dumps raw ideas; an agent triages them into tasks placed on an urgent/important matrix (Do, Schedule, Delegate, Eliminate) that can be dragged between quadrants and delegated to agents.

f: Weekly work report from git and calendar
w: Collects the owner's week from GitHub or local git activity and Google Calendar events, and writes a progress report with achievements, ongoing work and plans.

f: Call tools a web page exposes through WebMCP
w: When a page registers WebMCP tools, the browser agent discovers them (including in frames and late registrations), validates input against their schemas, invokes and cancels them with size and count limits, and notices when the page context changes under it, so it can use the site's own actions instead of clicking.

f: WebMCP bridge: expose tools to browser-native agents
w: Bridges an agent's MCP tools (plus in-page tools) to Chrome's navigator.modelContext so agents built into the browser can discover and call them directly from the page.

f: Browser action receipts with failure kind and next command
w: Every click, fill, press or navigate returns a one-line receipt (URL, outcome, dialogs, downloads); a failed action names a typed kind such as covered, disabled or stale-ref plus a runnable next command, and clicks wait for actionability and refuse to land on a covering element.

f: Point at page elements and leave comments as instructions
w: In the agent's browser panel the person switches to annotate mode, clicks or drags over page elements and attaches comments (up to 24); the annotated elements and notes are sent to the agent as inspect, change or review instructions.

f: In-page agent via one script tag (text DOM, no screenshots)
w: Drop one script into any web page and it gets its own agent that reads a compact text DOM tree and clicks, types and scrolls in place with a visible simulated cursor, plus React/antd input patches; no extension, headless browser or vision model needed.

f: Simulate candidate web actions before acting
w: For each candidate click or type on a page, a model imagines the resulting page state a few steps ahead and scores progress toward the goal; the agent executes only the best-scoring action, avoiding irreversible mistakes.

f: Bounded table extraction from live pages
w: Pulls whole tables and virtualized grids out of a page into row artifacts, with row identity from aria-rowindex or a key column, sampling, and an explicit stop reason (row, byte, time or no-progress limit) so partial results are honest.

The agent can tie each browser action to the requests, response bodies, console messages and page changes it caused, find slow or duplicate API calls, apply explicit HTTP rules or replay a request to test a hypothesis, and export the redacted evidence as JSON.

f: Agent web-security workbench (capture, edit-and-replay, diff HTTP traffic)
w: An agent can browse a target with capture on, list captured requests, resend one with edited fields, diff two responses and run request sequences/matrices to hunt for vulnerabilities, with findings recorded.

f: Agent Window and borrow-a-tab in the owner's browser
w: Agent tasks in the owner's real browser run in their own visible window so the owner keeps working; an existing tab can be borrowed only after an on-page confirmation and is handed back when the task ends, with cleanup on disconnect.

f: Declutter pages and flag dark patterns for the agent
w: Hides cookie banners, ads (EasyList), chat widgets, newsletter modals and footers to save tokens (~11% measured), and annotates manipulative patterns such as confirm-shaming, fake scarcity, countdown timers, hidden fees, pre-ticked checkout boxes, spoofed links and hard-to-cancel flows so the agent is not steered by them.

f: Layout-preserving text rendering of a page for text-only models
w: Interactable (or all text) elements are tagged in the page with bracketed ids, and an OCR pass turns the tagged screenshot into whitespace-structured text that keeps the visual layout, so a model without vision can act on ids like CLICK [23]; works with Playwright and Selenium.

f: Chrome performance-trace insight extraction for agents
w: Records a Chrome performance trace, chunk-parses it and distills actionable performance insights (slow phases, bottlenecks) into a compact form an agent can read, alongside network and console tools whose output is formatted with source-mapped stack traces.

f: Passkeys (WebAuthn) for websites in the embedded browser
w: Sites opened in the built-in browser can register and sign in with platform passkeys through a native bridge, with a policy on which origins may use them.

Turns any Telegram file into an HTTP link that streams with range requests straight from Telegram over MTProto, using several worker bots, so files above the Bot API's download limit work without first downloading them.

f: Steer terminal agent sessions from a chat app
w: Telegram, Feishu or WeChat get a card when a session waits (which session, what for, Allow/Deny buttons); replying 'N: text' types into session N, 'shot N' returns a picture of the pane, and in advanced mode a plain request is routed to the right session and typed only after the user says ok.
The assistant joins a live stream's chat, reads viewer comments and gifts (Bilibili danmaku over websocket, YouTube and Twitch live chat) and answers them as the on-screen character.

f: Chat-to-chat forwarding and live sync with transform plugins
w: Rules forward messages from source chats to destination chats, either all past messages or live from now, passing each through plugins: whitelist/blacklist filter, regex replace, formatting, header/footer captions, image/video watermark and OCR.

f: One Slack app per agent, provisioned automatically
w: Setup creates a separate Slack app for each agent (manifest, avatar, workspace install) so every agent has its own bot identity with no tokens to paste, and agents can open shared rooms and write room canvases.

f: Cloud stand-in keeps the bot answering while the PC is off
w: A free Cloudflare Worker takes over the same Telegram bot when the home PC stops checking in, answers and queues work, then hands the bot back when the PC starts, with phone approvals relayed through it.

f: Owner-written custom chat commands in a sandboxed template language
w: Server owners write custom commands triggered by text, reactions, slash commands, components or intervals in a Go-template language with a per-command key-value database and execution limits, edited in a web panel.

f: Evidence-based stuck detector for delegated coding agents
w: Watches an external coding agent process and decides whether it is working, waiting or truly stuck from tiered evidence (output activity, workspace changes, live sub-agents, repetition), so it never kills an agent doing real sub-agent work, plus a post-exit verdict.

f: Executable architecture and behavior contracts as the done gate
w: Project rules live in the repo as contracts: static structure rules checked over the code with tree-sitter (Python, TS, Go, Java, Rust, C), and runtime behavior rules checked with generated inputs and minimized counterexamples; `status` says GREEN or BLOCKED and the agent cannot finish while red.

A task the agent marks closed is only accepted if a commit touching real files (not notes) was made since dispatch and pushed upstream, or the agent wrote a note explaining why no change was needed; repeated fake closures quarantine the task instead of looping.

f: Acceptance bound to a verification fingerprint
w: Verification runs separately from the task and is fingerprinted with the exact diff; a review gate and the human acceptance step are tied to that fingerprint, so accepting stale or changed work is refused and an attestation is recorded.

f: Decision memory keyed by code entity, injected before edits
w: Agents record why an approach was chosen, what was rejected and what would change their mind, keyed to a function, route or dependency; a pre-tool hook surfaces those records when the agent is about to edit that code.

f: Failover between coding agents with failure budgets
w: Classifies each delegated-agent failure (connectivity, unavailability, same-shape repeated failure), spends per-agent failure budgets with cycle caps, and fails over to another configured coding CLI with a retry prompt.

f: PR babysitting: watch CI and rerun only proven-flaky jobs
w: Opt a PR into /baby-sit and the agent watches its CI through webhooks, diagnoses each failure, fixes real breakages and reruns only jobs whose failure evidence shows they are flaky.

f: Proactive coding buddy with codebase-health observers
w: A background companion runs observers (diagnostic clusters, git pressure, worktree hygiene, provider health, MCP auth, customization drift, trajectory clutter) and scheduled jobs (daily digest, Friday retro, idle suggestions, refactor hunter, test-coverage watcher, PR-issue matchmaker, error triage, self-critic), and a speech policy decides when it may speak up.

Watches a work tracker (Linear, Jira, GitHub, GitLab or Asana), gives each eligible issue its own isolated workspace (locally or over SSH) and a Codex app-server run governed by a repo WORKFLOW.md, retries with backoff, and returns proof of work (CI status, PR review feedback) on the issue, with a status dashboard; a language-neutral SPEC.md lets you re-implement it.

File reads tag each line with a short content hash and edits address lines by number plus hash, so edits against stale content are detected and recovered instead of silently mis-applied; sloppy and apply_patch modes share one engine.

f: Phased feature pipeline from goal to PR with review gates
w: A big feature runs as fixed stages: build a repo knowledge base, inquiry questions, research by specialist researcher agents, design, a roadmap, per-phase plans (tracer bullet first, then TDD fill-ins), plan validators, implementation with review axes, final fix and PR description; optional owner gates pause at each review and 'need user input' points.

f: Blast-radius query on a static code graph
w: Builds a static import/symbol graph with layers and health checks and answers 'what is affected if I change this file' before an agent edits.

f: Affected tests and dead code from the code graph
w: Given changed files, the graph lists the tests that exercise them (with per-language test conventions), and it reports unreferenced code, so the agent runs only relevant tests and can prune dead code.
Finds unreferenced functions, classes and exports using the symbol index, aware of dynamic imports, intra-file calls and JS re-exports, evaluated against a labeled corpus.
Runs passing and failing tests with coverage to rank the statements most likely to hold the bug (Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, Rust backends) and fuses that with other signals before the agent edits.

f: Co-change coupling and change-impact prediction from git history
w: Answers 'what always changes together' and 'what breaks if I touch this' by mining git history for co-change with per-type half-life decay plus counterfactual removal over the code graph.

f: Find the same bug shape elsewhere (antibodies)
w: After a fix, the bug's structural pattern is stored as an 'antibody' and the graph is scanned for other places with the same shape.

f: Speculative edit sessions with diagnostic delta
w: The agent previews an edit in memory, gets the before/after diagnostics difference from the real language server, and only then applies or discards it, so broken edits never touch disk.
Installs and supervises a worker inside IDA so the agent can query and annotate disassembly of binaries through tools.

The agent edits code by symbol instead of line numbers: replace a function or class body, insert before/after a symbol, rename a symbol across the whole project and safely delete a symbol only when nothing references it, with diagnostics returned after each edit and atomic file writes.

f: Action fusion: edit plus validation in one call
w: An edit or write tool call can carry its follow-up validation command (tests, lint, build), which runs right after the write in the same call, removing a model round-trip per edit.

While the agent is fixing failing checks, writes to test files are refused by default (or flagged), so it must fix the code or say the test is wrong; a test changed after a failure is reported next to any 'verified' result so green never hides a rewritten test.

f: Check bonds: prove each passing check can fail
w: Before trusting a pass, the verifier briefly adds fixtures that must make each check fail; a check that still passes, or whose test configuration the change itself edited, is reported as untrusted instead of green.

Common TypeScript errors in generated code (cannot find name, missing module, missing exported member, default/named import mismatches) are repaired by AST rules that add imports, fix paths or create stubs, without a model call.

f: Stage mode: agent writes held in an overlay until applied
w: The coding agent's file writes go into a staged queue that its own later reads see as an overlay; nothing touches disk until the user applies, CRLF is preserved and the queue survives restart.

f: Guided tour of an agent's changes
w: A button turns a task's diff (or a file) into a step-by-step tour with explanations, suggested questions, threads and an ask bar, so the user can understand and question what the agent changed before merging.
After the first review, the tool generates check questions per finding, answers them against the code, scores each issue and drops likely false positives before reporting.

f: SAST scan fed into AI review
w: Downloads OpenGrep on demand, scans the changed code, trims its JSON to the fields the model needs and gives it to the reviewer with guidance.

f: Vulnerability research scans with ranked, validated findings
w: Breaks a repository security review into small prompt steps run in parallel by coding-agent CLIs, merges output into one finding schema with candidate dedupe, ranks severity with editable rankers, runs post-scripts that try to prove each issue (PoC, report), and exports a share-safe ZIP.

f: Coverage-verified security review with a checked ledger and SARIF
w: A parser cuts C/C++ code into units that each review agent must answer fixed questions about; a checker re-derives the spots from source and marks the run unverified if an agent skipped any, then findings are assembled into a report and SARIF.

f: Token-budgeted compression of large PR diffs
w: Large pull requests are fitted into the model's budget by extending hunks with context, dropping deletion-only hunks, sorting files by language and token weight, and clipping or splitting into several calls, so reviews still work on huge diffs.

f: PR command toolkit across git hosts
w: Comment commands on a PR: /describe writes title, summary and labels; /improve posts committable code suggestions with inline-comment dedup; /ask and line questions; /update_changelog; ticket compliance checks against the linked issue; all through one provider interface for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gerrit, Gitea and CodeCommit.

f: Cross-model adversarial review of a diff
w: After the main model writes a change, a model from a different family (Codex, GPT or Gemini via OpenRouter) red-teams the same diff against the spec, reporting only correctness, requirement and invariant gaps with file:line; disagreements are shown to the user, and a skipped review gets its own exit code so it is never mistaken for a pass.

f: Whole-repo semantic drift audit with parallel rubric reviewers
w: Scans a whole repository, dispatches focused reviewers (stale docs, spec vs code, duplicate/orphan files, conventions, i18n sync, icons) in parallel, consolidates and dedupes findings with evidence and severity, and produces a self-contained HTML report; never edits files.

f: Upserted GitHub tracking issue for recurring audit findings
w: Scheduled CI audits find their previous tracking issue by a stable hash marker and update it in place instead of opening duplicates, so recurring findings live in one issue.

f: Architecture decision records retrieved and enforced
w: Imports and compiles the project's ADRs into a decision index; relevant decisions are retrieved into the coding agent's context, governed rules are enforced deterministically on proposed changes by path selectors, and conflicts, staleness and decision authority are checked.

f: Deterministic UI quality detector for generated frontends
w: A rule engine scans generated UI code for AI-slop tells (purple gradients by hue, generic patterns, accessibility misses) with severities, one-line fixes, auto-fix for some rules and a 0-100 score that can gate CI or a review hook.

f: PR reviewer that learns the repository's review style
w: An automatic or on-demand PR reviewer publishes findings to GitHub, then collects how maintainers reacted to past findings and review comments to build per-repository style guidance that shapes later reviews; outcomes are reconciled and evaluated.

f: Compiler-verified backend builder (requirements to DB, API, tests and code)
w: From a chat description the agent runs a waterfall of phases (analyze requirements, design database schema, design API, write e2e tests, implement) where each phase emits an AST that a compiler validates and the agent corrects until it builds.

f: Dependency upgrade agent that fixes breaking changes
w: Bumps a package to a target version, builds the project to collect errors, uses the TypeScript AST and the new package's type signatures to build a dependency/plan graph, then edits affected code in order until the build passes; can run on Dependabot/Renovate PRs.

f: Issue to failing test to execution-selected fix
w: From an issue URL it writes a regression test that fails, samples several candidate patches, keeps the one that passes the real test suite (after a static blast-radius check), and opens a PR from a fork; every phase is checkpointed so a crash resumes.

f: Backprop runtime failures into the spec
w: A post-tool hook spots failing test runs and queues a backprop step; the gap becomes a new numbered acceptance criterion plus a regression test before the loop resumes, so a bug found late tightens the spec instead of just being patched.

f: Staged evaluation pipeline with reward-hacking veto
w: Finished work is judged in stages: mechanical checks run real commands, a semantic judge checks acceptance criteria, then multi-model consensus with reviewer independence; an adversarial pass and a reward-hacking veto reject work that games the checks, and the grading command is never shown to the worker.

f: Risk-tiered pipeline with automatic security review
w: A deterministic (no LLM) classifier rates each task low/normal/high/security from keywords and paths; low risk takes a fast path while anything touching auth, crypto or network adds a dedicated security audit stage before the branch is cut.

f: Test-first enforcement hook for coding agents
w: A pre-edit hook sends each proposed write/edit plus the latest test results (from reporters for Vitest, Jest, pytest, Go, Rust, PHPUnit and more) to a validator model, and blocks implementation that has no failing test or goes beyond it; a post-edit hook enforces lint during refactor; can be toggled per session.

f: Executor/supervisor task runner with focused retries
w: Pick a cheap executor model and a separate supervisor model per task; the supervisor checks acceptance criteria then repo quality policy, keeps already-verified passes and points the next attempt only at unresolved items, with every attempt's plan, output, checks and diff kept for inspection.

f: Which session made a commit (multi-session commit provenance)
w: In a checkout shared by several agent sessions, records which session ran each git commit and which sessions' file writes are inside it, separating authored commits from fast-forwards, without writing trailers or notes.

f: Verified handover passport for AI-built projects
w: Scans the repo and Claude Code/Codex/Cursor history for facts, claims and decisions, runs install/build/test in a Docker sandbox, and writes a digest-stamped passport where every statement has a truth status and evidence; the recipient re-runs the checks with one command and any divergence is named.
Narrows an issue to the files, then the classes/functions, then the exact edit locations using a compressed repo skeleton plus embedding retrieval, before any code is written.

f: Magic commands: resolve merge conflicts and investigate security alerts
w: One-click commands hand the agent a prepared task: resolve the current branch's merge conflicts, investigate a GitHub security alert, Dependabot advisory or Sentry issue, address review comments or update a PR, each with its own configurable prompt, model and effort.

f: Pre-trust new worktrees for Claude Code and Codex
w: Before spawning a worker in a fresh worktree, writes the trust entry into ~/.claude.json or passes a Codex -c trust override, so dispatched agents don't stall on the workspace-trust dialog; a PTY auto-answer stays as fallback.

f: Auto-merge of parallel worker worktrees with conflict mailbox
w: When several helper agents work in separate worktrees, a merge coordinator merges finished work back in order, and any conflict is posted to the responsible worker's mailbox to resolve instead of stalling the team; survives restarts.

f: Isolated full dev-environment stack per worktree with port checkout
w: From a small Coastfile, each git worktree gets its own containerized copy of the app's services and volumes on dynamic ports, so parallel agents never collide; one instance at a time is 'checked out' onto the canonical host ports, and shared service groups can be reused across instances.

f: Red/green review of agent edits inside a rendered document
w: Agent edits to a markdown file show as red/green changes inside the WYSIWYG (Lexical) editor, matched by tree diff, and you accept or reject each change in place instead of reading a text diff.

f: Deterministic AI-slop detector for generated code
w: Regex and AST analyzers flag typical AI-generated leftovers (placeholder comments, debug prints, over-defensive code, stale TODOs, excessive docs) before review, with suppression and auto-fix, so cleanup costs no tokens.

f: Prompt-to-app builder with instant previews and runtime-error repair
w: The agent asks clarifying questions, writes a full-stack app, bundles it into an instantly served preview (no dev server), captures the browser console of the preview, repairs runtime errors and redeploys, with a pre-deploy safety gate and restore points.

f: Agent overlay on the owner's own shell
w: The owner's normal shell runs inside a PTY wrapper; a hotkey opens the agent CLI as an overlay that can read the visible screen and scrollback after pattern-based privacy filtering, get cwd/shell context updates, and queue exact input that is typed only after the owner approves.

f: AI readiness score for a project
w: Scores how ready a repository is for coding agents (instruction files for Claude, Codex and Gemini, context size, custom extensions) and offers one-click fixes.

f: Guard plugin forcing headless Claude Code to end with final JSON
w: An embedded Claude Code plugin with hooks that blocks commit/push 'finalizer' commands inside the executor and refuses to stop until the run emits the required final JSON, so the runtime (not the model) owns commit and handoff.

f: Rendered UI evidence gate (render, score, revise)
w: After an agent builds a screen, the UI is rendered and checked by deterministic, code, visual and temporal reports against JSON schemas; an evidence gate blocks acceptance until the reports pass, and the agent revises.

f: Project design-rule compiler and semantic palette generator
w: Compiles chosen design decisions into project-local rules, generates semantic palettes and spacing contracts, and keeps the project's existing choices across updates.

f: Repository docs kept in sync with code changes
w: Builds a tree of every class and function with its callers and callees, writes documentation for each in dependency order, and on each commit detects changed objects through git and regenerates only their docs (usable as a pre-commit hook).

f: Repository wiki with evidence-grounded claims and targeted updates
w: The agent writes a linked Markdown wiki of a repository where each fact is stored as a claim pointing at versioned source evidence; on later runs only claims whose evidence changed are revisited, links are validated, finished pages survive interruption, and related repos' wikis can be searched together over MCP.

f: Expedited human review cards with diff image and voting
w: When a change is ready, a review card with a rendered diff image is posted to Slack or the author's DM; eligible people vote, readiness and eligibility are checked, and the change merges once approved.

f: Fetch a dependency's source at the installed version
w: The agent asks for a package (npm, PyPI, crates.io or a GitHub repo); the tool resolves the version actually in the lockfile, fetches that version's source into a cache and returns its path so the agent can grep and read the real code.

f: Compile, deploy and verify smart contracts from chat
w: The agent writes Solidity, compiles it with solc, deploys to a chosen EVM chain (server key or the user's wallet), records only after a successful creation receipt, and verifies source on Etherscan or Blockscout.

f: Hardware project designer (OpenSCAD and parts inventory)
w: From a plain description, extracts requirements, picks components (checking a stored parts inventory first), designs the circuit and writes an OpenSCAD enclosure, validating it and exporting STL plus a preview image.

f: Design handoff reader for coding agents
w: Pulls requirement pages (Axure text, annotations, focused crops by text, block id or coordinates) and design drafts from a design-handoff service, downloads semantically named slices and extracts sizes, spacing, colours and fonts with an HTML+CSS reference for the agent to adapt.

f: Team lessons turned into deterministic commit-blocking checks
w: Repo-specific team knowledge is stored as reviewable memory and briefed to the agent before it acts; each hard-won lesson becomes a deterministic anti-pattern/precommit check that refuses the commit (not another model opinion) when the code repeats a known mistake, with a verdict and precision gate.

The agent resolves a library name to an id and pulls current, version-specific documentation and code examples for it into context, as an MCP server, AI SDK tools or a CLI plus skill, so it stops inventing outdated APIs.

f: Pinned coding-agent runtimes installed into agent workspaces
w: A release catalog with cache installs pinned builds of Claude Code, Codex and Node into each agent's workspace so hosted coding agents run inside the agent's own computer.

f: Evolutionary code optimization (MAP-Elites islands + evaluator cascade)
w: Give it a program and a scoring script; it repeatedly asks models for diffs or rewrites, runs a staged evaluator with timeouts, keeps a MAP-Elites archive across migrating islands, and checkpoints/resumes, so the user gets a measurably better version of a function, prompt or kernel; includes a web visualizer of the program lineage.

f: Coding agents in remote sandboxes over one HTTP API
w: A static binary inside any sandbox (E2B, Daytona, Modal, Docker, Cloudflare, Vercel and more) runs the chosen coding agent and exposes sessions, permissions and streamed events over HTTP/SSE in one universal event schema, with transcript persistence adapters (SQLite, Postgres, IndexedDB) for later replay.

f: Working / blocked / idle detection for any terminal coding agent
w: Per-agent detection manifests (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Hermes and 20 more) read each terminal pane and mark it working, blocked or idle, so the owner sees which agent needs an answer and agents can wait until another agent is truly blocked.

f: Mixed coding-agent task plans landed in plan order
w: A read-only planner researches the repo, asks about vague points and returns a task graph where each task names its coding agent, model, effort and mode; the owner edits it before anything runs, independent tasks run in parallel worktrees, completion is decided by a marker in the runner's output, and passing work lands on one integration branch in plan order.

f: Bridge from the running app into the coding agent
w: A local bridge streams errors, console output and screenshots from the app being developed into the agent session and lets the agent send control back, Sentry-style, with an MCP server.

Each change gets a folder with proposal, delta specs (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED requirements with WHEN/THEN scenarios), design and tasks; an artifact graph says what comes next, a validator checks scenarios and task lists, and archive merges the deltas into the living specs.

f: Co-edit guard for blocks that must change together
w: Tag a code block and the doc or config it affects; on a diff the check reports any block edited without its partner, compares values across files, and runs keep-sorted/unique/pattern and AI-written checks, so an agent's edits do not leave docs stale.

f: Dependency API changes since the model's training cutoff
w: Reads the project's lockfiles, finds which pinned Python packages changed after the coding model's cutoff, statically diffs their APIs, shows where the code uses changed APIs, and writes short AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md notes so the agent avoids the old form, with no model calls.

Builds a whole app from a description: a spec writer clarifies requirements, an architect picks stack and templates, a tech lead splits epics into tasks, and developer/code-monkey agents implement each task with the user reviewing between steps.
Lists every localhost port that each agent's process tree is listening on (dev servers it started), with the owning pane, and can terminate the process holding a port.

f: Use a GitHub repository as a tool for a task
w: Describe a task; the agent searches and filters GitHub for a suitable repo, ranks its important files, summarizes how to use it, then installs and runs it in Docker (repairing pip errors) to produce the result.

f: Open a project in its dev container
w: Parses devcontainer.json, resolves Dev Container features from OCI registries and builds/starts the container with Docker so the project can be opened inside its declared environment.

f: Diff coverage gate and patch ratchet
w: CI gates that fail a change when lines it touched are not covered by tests, and a ratchet baseline that only lets quality numbers improve, so agent-written patches cannot lower coverage.

f: Block secrets from entering git in agent commits
w: Before an agent's git commit or push runs, staged added lines are scanned with gitleaks and the command is blocked on a secret; --no-verify and --no-gpg-sign are refused, reads of protected paths are denied, and a native pre-commit hook plus CI action act as backstops.

f: One approval inbox for external coding-agent CLIs
w: Installs hook scripts into Claude Code, Codex, Grok, pi and others so their permission prompts and questions arrive as notification-style banners in one panel, answered with a primary action or options, with remembered per-agent approvals.

f: Performance investigation workflow with baselines and profilers
w: A structured perf investigation keeps state across sessions: it records baselines, runs benchmarks, finds the breaking point under load, profiles Node, Python, Go, Java and Rust code, tracks hypotheses as experiments, and compares results to the stored baseline before accepting an optimisation.

Work items move through Ideation, Refinement, Spec, Sprint and Tasks only along allowed transitions; moving forward requires recorded evidence (linked tests, coverage, smoke and delivery evidence) or an explicit, visible skip, and ambiguity checks gate ideas and refinements.

f: Terminal sessions that survive app quit and SSH drops (zmx)
w: Every terminal runs inside a small session daemon rather than as a child of the app, so quitting, relaunching or losing an SSH link reattaches each session with its scrollback instead of restarting it.

f: Compact build and test output wrappers
w: Wrappers run Maven, npm/Node and Go test commands and print only failures, counts and the lines needed to fix them, cutting output by up to 99% so agents keep context for the actual work.
The agent can offload a build/compile to another host, syncing sources and returning results, so heavy compilation runs off the local machine.

f: Design agent with side-by-side mockup variants on a canvas
w: From one prompt the agent writes several HTML/CSS mockup variants and a theme (palette, fonts) into a design folder; a canvas view shows them side by side to compare, fork and iterate, then the chosen design can be handed to a coding agent.

f: Compare two review runs: new, persisting, resolved, not re-checked
w: After fixing code, re-run the review and see which findings are new, which persist (with updated line numbers), which are resolved, and which were never re-checked, following renamed files; shown in a local web viewer.

f: Drive Electron desktop apps (Slack and others) over CDP
w: Electron apps such as Slack are relaunched with a debugging port, show an overlay inviting them to join the agent's session, and are then controlled through the same DevTools protocol as browser tabs, so the agent reads and acts in desktop apps by DOM instead of pixels.

f: Learn an app by exploring, then use the learned guide
w: Before doing real tasks the agent explores an app on its own (or watches a human demo) and writes a short document per UI element describing what it does; at task time those per-app docs are fed to the model so it taps the right controls.

f: Critic-checked desktop steps (planner critic, step check, actor critic)
w: Before each planned step a step-check model looks at the live screen and decides whether the step is already done, needs changing or should run; after acting an actor critic verifies the result and corrects it, and a planner critic revises the plan, so tasks work from any starting state.

f: Global kill-switch hotkey with heartbeat that must be live before any input
w: A registered global hotkey chord latches a stop of all agent desktop input; the listener heartbeats to a supervisor and input is refused when no stop path is live or its heartbeat is stale, until the user explicitly resets.

f: Self-evolving phone agent with learned tips and shortcuts
w: A manager/operator/reflector/notetaker team runs phone tasks over ADB; after each task experience reflectors write general tips and reusable multi-step shortcuts to a long-term store that later tasks load, so the agent gets faster and more reliable with use.

f: iOS Simulator streamed into the app window
w: The iOS Simulator's framebuffer is streamed into a pane next to the chat, so the agent and owner can see and interact with the app being built without switching windows; simulator targets are enumerated and picked per chat.

f: Persistent agent VM with incremental snapshot and state reconcile
w: Each agent gets its own lightweight VM that boots fast and, unlike a disposable sandbox, keeps its filesystem and memory between sessions via incremental QEMU snapshots and a state-reconcile step, so an agent's computer can be paused and resumed with everything intact.

f: Self-hosted microVM sandboxes with snapshot, clone and rollback
w: Run agent sandboxes as hardware-isolated KVM microVMs on your own machines (sub-60ms start, E2B SDK compatible), with copy-on-write snapshots to clone a sandbox, roll back to any saved state, and pause on one node and resume on another.

f: Wake a sleeping computer before connecting
w: Sends a Wake-on-LAN magic packet to the owner's computer so a remote session can start even when the machine is asleep.

f: Attach to existing tmux, zellij and screen sessions from the browser
w: Lists the user's running tmux/zellij/screen sessions, windows and panes and attaches to them in a web terminal, so an agent started in a terminal earlier can be picked up and steered from the phone; a 'vt' wrapper forwards any new terminal command too.

f: WSL-to-Windows screen capture with region masking
w: A pi extension lets a WSL-hosted agent capture the Windows desktop (full, region, monitor, active or a specific window) using only built-in powershell.exe + .NET; window mode uses PrintWindow PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT to grab even occluded windows, and regions can be cropped, resized and masked to hide sensitive pixels before sharing.

f: Privacy screen masks the physical display during remote control
w: While someone controls the computer remotely, the local monitors are covered by masks excluded from capture; touching local input asks to disconnect and locks the session (macOS, Windows, Hyprland gate).

f: Shared PTY where the AI co-types in the human's live terminal
w: The agent and the person share one live PTY (local, SSH or Docker): the AI types its commands straight into the same interactive terminal the human is watching and can type in, rather than running commands in a hidden shell, with a PTY manager and agent-event stream keeping both sides in sync.

f: Drive desktop apps through their scripting runtimes
w: The agent sends a script through one shell command; a COM, AppleScript or local-HTTP bridge runs it inside Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, After Effects, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Blender, Houdini, 3ds Max or Unity and returns JSON, with per-app API indexes and guides, no screenshots or MCP server.

When switched on, the app captures the screen every N minutes, asks the model for the single best next step grounded in what is visible, and shows it as a suggestion card that only prefills the message box when clicked; screenshots are deleted and never persisted.

f: Disposable real VMs with operator-approved egress
w: An agent creates, uses and recreates full Linux VMs from digest-pinned golden images through one constrained socket API; guests reach only a package cache and configured mock ports, and any other destination becomes an egress request the operator approves.

f: Synology NAS file, sharing and transfer tools
w: The agent can discover a Synology NAS, keep per-NAS profiles, list/upload/download/move files, create share links and run transfers through DSM APIs, also exposed as a `co syno` CLI and skill.

f: Agent-native email over JMAP with proof-of-work auth
w: A JMAP email client built for agents (send, reply with context, blob upload with limits, charset handling) authenticated by client-computed proof-of-work, exposed as MCP tools and an n8n node, so an agent operates its own inbox autonomously.

Checks every open PR the owner has on GitHub, sorts them into needs-you versus waiting-on-others, analyses CI failures and maintainer comments, drafts replies and rebases for approval, grades new issues to pick up, and checks a repo's policy on AI contributions first.

f: Natural-language robot control skills over MCP
w: An agent commands physical robots (Unitree Go2/G1, arms, MAVLink drones) through skills such as navigate to a semantic place, follow a person, observe, GPS travel points and stop, exposed over an MCP server so outside agents can drive them.

f: MCP aggregating proxy with per-user access and downstream token refresh
w: One MCP endpoint fronts many downstream MCP servers, pooling their connections and refreshing each server's own OAuth tokens, and exposes to each caller only the slice of tools/skills their identity is allowed, so the agent never holds the downstream credentials.

Ready tool servers for ServiceNow, Zendesk, Gong, Salesloft, Ashby, Vanta, Freshservice, Statuspage, Productboard, Monday, HubSpot and Salesforce so an agent can read and act in common sales, support, HR and compliance systems.

Agent channels and tickets are mirrored to a GitHub Projects v2 board: channels become epics, tickets become draft items, and Type/Status/Priority custom fields stay in sync while the app stays the source of truth.

A single provider interface lists and imports tickets from GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Asana, Trello, Notion, Plane, Monday, Featurebase, Forgejo, Plain and YouTrack so any ticket can be sent to an agent task.

f: Support-inbox autopilot with sentiment x urgency routing
w: Each incoming email is classified (intent, sentiment level, urgency 1-5) and a decision matrix routes it to auto-send, a human-review draft queue, or escalation with SLA timers and IM notifications.

f: Email triage that learns importance, with ready reply drafts
w: The built-in mail client classifies threads into important and everything else (and labels), learns from the user's importance and category corrections, and pre-drafts replies to important mail using the knowledge graph.

f: Desktop Outlook through COM (no cloud sign-in)
w: On Windows, the agent reads, searches, drafts and sends mail and reads the calendar through the locally installed Outlook client over COM, returning structured JSON, so no Microsoft Graph app registration or OAuth is needed.
Read and write Microsoft OneNote notebooks, sections and pages through Microsoft Graph with the owner's signed-in account.

f: Agent Bitcoin wallet with local spend policy and L402
w: An agent holds an encrypted-seed Bitcoin L2 wallet to send, receive and pay Lightning invoices and L402 API paywalls, bounded by a local spend ledger, recipient allowlist, fee guards and a policy bound to the seed; secrets are never printed.
Signs in to Tesla Fleet API with OAuth and lets the agent read vehicle data and location and send commands such as charging, climate and locks.
Agent tools for Hikvision, Axis and Vivotek IP cameras/DVRs plus Ring and Blink: device info, snapshots, live stream, motion detection settings, events and recordings.

f: Ask a connected SQL or graph database in plain language
w: Agents connect to a SQL database, Neo4j or ArangoDB, pull the schema and descriptions into context, write SQL/Cypher/AQL from a question, validate the query before running it (including read-only safety checks), retry on errors and answer from the results.

f: Database tools: prebuilt per-database toolsets and declarative SQL tools
w: Connect a database and get ready toolsets (list tables, run SQL, query plans, active queries, locks) or define your own parameterized SQL tools in YAML with auth-bound parameters, served to the agent over MCP.

f: Home media requests (Sonarr, Radarr, Overseerr, Ombi)
w: From a chat, search for a movie or show (TheMovieDb), request it from the owner's Sonarr/Radarr/Overseerr/Ombi server with per-user quotas, report issues, and get notified when the download is available.

f: MQTT edge devices: sensors and actuators as tools
w: Register IoT/edge devices with a wizard, then the agent lists devices, reads sensor values with history, sends MQTT commands and controls actuators, with device cards and a detail drawer in the UI.

f: Publish to Chinese social platforms (Xiaohongshu, Douyin, WeChat Channels)
w: Skills that publish notes and videos to Xiaohongshu, Douyin and WeChat Channels through the user's signed-in creator session (login check and verify first), plus fetching comments and engagement.

f: Contacts sync across Google, Microsoft, iCloud and CardDAV
w: One contacts registry with providers for Google, Microsoft, iCloud and any CardDAV server (including IMAP-hosted), so the agent can search and edit the owner's real address books.

f: Personal life ledger: habits, time logs, plans vs reality, finance
w: A local database and agent-usable CLI/API for areas, visions, tasks, habits and habit actions, planned events, time logs with templates and daily stats per area, finance snapshots, body measurements and sleep, so the assistant can log what happened and compare it with what was planned.

f: Provision and rotate scoped service tokens
w: Creates and rotates narrowly scoped tokens on services such as Vercel and Supabase through their APIs, or by driving the dashboard with Playwright when no API exists.

f: Charge other agents for work (x402 paywall)
w: An agent's A2A endpoint can require an x402 payment: middleware issues payment requirements, tracks payment sessions with a nonce store against replay, and runs the task only after a facilitator confirms payment.

f: Hire a real person for a task
w: The agent searches people by skill, location or equipment, posts job offers or job-board listings, and manages the hiring lifecycle for things it cannot do itself (QA testing, store beta testing, local errands).

f: SEO and Search Console analysis skills with CMS write-back
w: Skills plus scripts that pull Google Search Console and PageSpeed data, detect the site's CMS (WordPress, Ghost, Strapi, Contentful), audit pages, keywords, links and schema, and push approved SEO fixes back to the CMS; companion skills cover Google/Meta/X/LinkedIn/Reddit/TikTok ads with approval boundaries.

The agent asks citation-backed questions of NotebookLM notebooks, adds and reads sources, and generates Studio outputs (audio overview, video, infographic, report, slides, data table) in a chosen language, using the fast internal batchexecute RPC with a browser fallback and rotating across several Google accounts with auto re-auth.

f: Publish artifacts to the user's own cloud drive
w: Artifacts are published to one private bucket and one shared CDN distribution in the user's own AWS account, so each later publish is an upload plus invalidation, kept separate from deploy tooling so a site delete can never wipe the drive.

f: OAuth proxy so MCP clients can sign in through ordinary identity providers
w: Lets an MCP server accept MCP clients that expect dynamic client registration while authenticating against providers that lack it (GitHub, Google, Azure, Auth0, WorkOS and more), with a consent screen, redirect validation and token handling.

f: Overleaf sync, compile and marked-up diff
w: The agent can list, pull, push and two-way sync Overleaf LaTeX projects with conflict detection, compile to PDF, download the .bbl, produce a latexdiff marked-up PDF, and expose all of it as MCP tools or a git remote.

f: Design systems the agent designs against
w: Import a design system (from GitHub, shadcn or a brand) into a token contract with evidence and a showcase preview, then have the agent build prototypes, landing pages and slides that follow it.

Checks agent-made slide decks for layout problems (overflow, overlap, off-canvas, crowding) from both the OOXML and rendered images, applies a design policy and writes a review manifest and report before delivery.

f: Book-length translation projects with EPUB export
w: Ingest a long work, translate it as a resumable project with consistency across chapters, revise passages, and export to EPUB.

f: Pixel-verified annotated screenshots and flow recordings
w: Give a URL and CSS selectors; it captures annotated screenshots, before/after composites, terminal captures and step-by-step flow recordings (GIF/MP4 with cursor, camera and spotlight), placing marks from measured DOM boxes and refusing to save any output that fails pixel validation.

f: Screenshot library with local AI organizing and search
w: Captured screenshots are categorized and described by a local Ollama model in the background, embedded for semantic search by description, OCR-transcribed, and can be segmented or upscaled by add-on workers.
From one topic it generates a script, collage keyframes, motion/Ken Burns animation, voice-over, beat-synced music, captions and a thumbnail, then assembles a finished explainer/ad video with ffmpeg.

f: Animated film from a repo's git history
w: A skill directs a two-minute animated film from a repository: picks real commits, releases and reverts, builds outline, cast sheet and storyboard in an HTML review studio, then renders a 4K/60fps MP4 after approval.

f: Agentic footage editing through an edit decision list
w: The agent analyzes input footage (vision and audio), decides the cuts, writes an edit decision list, and assembles the result with silence trimming, audio mix and loudness normalization, then runs QA and review before delivery.

f: Dub a video into other languages
w: Transcribes a video, translates the script, synthesizes a new voiceover per language and re-renders the video with the dubbed audio and captions.

The agent edits a local CapCut/JianYing draft directly (tracks, subtitles, timing, speed, volume, keyframes, effects, templates, TTS, SFX), with lint, dry-run, diff and backup/restore, so the human opens a fully editable project instead of a flattened export.

Plans, drafts, checks quality and revises long documents through a writer IR with numbering and anchors, then exports via Pandoc/LaTeX or publishes to Notion, Feishu, WeChat articles, Obsidian, GitHub or Google Drive.

f: Long-form fiction pipeline with story state and continuity
w: Write a novel chapter by chapter with planner, architect, writer, continuity checker, state settler, reviewer and reviser agents; characters, foreshadowing and world facts live in a validated state store and each chapter is drafted in a workspace then committed atomically with its state.

f: Tailored CV and cover letter PDF generation with page budget
w: Builds a CV tailored to each posting from a structured career profile into HTML/LaTeX and PDF, keeping experience order, fonts and a page budget, plus generated cover letters and saved application answers.

f: Editorial SVG diagram skill with geometry verification and diagram import
w: The agent produces self-contained HTML+SVG diagrams across 42 layout types in light, dark and editorial variants, verified by scripts for label geometry, overlaps and accessibility, and can convert existing draw.io, Excalidraw and Mermaid diagrams into this style.
An infinite whiteboard (shapes, freehand, mind maps, frames, minimap, templates, export) where the agent proposes changes as a patch the owner previews and applies, scoped to a selection.
Train a character LoRA on the user's own images locally (musubi-tuner in a dedicated venv), with presets, install-path checks, progress status and conversion into the image tool's LoRA folder.

f: Background-refreshed context files about the owner's machine and habits
w: A context manager keeps a set of Markdown context files up to date in a background worker: host system and resources, GPU compute, storage, devices discovered on the home network, local inventory, recent activity and habits, media profile and browser history, which the assistant reads to ground answers in the real setup.

f: Import WhatsApp history from exports and phone backups
w: Parses WhatsApp chat exports and Android/iOS phone backups, extracts per-contact profiles and the best past replies, and bulk-embeds them into the assistant's memory so it starts with years of conversation history.

f: Memory served as a virtual folder that ordinary file and grep tools read
w: Hooks intercept the agent's normal Read/Grep/Bash calls on the memory folder and answer them from a SQL-backed store with hybrid lexical and semantic search, so any harness uses memory with its built-in file tools and no extra tool.

f: Memory-injecting model proxy for outside agents
w: Point Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or other agents' base URL at a local proxy; it classifies each request, injects recalled memory into Anthropic or OpenAI-format prompts, and captures turns for extraction, so every agent shares one memory with no plugin.

f: Structured queries over a markdown note graph
w: A folder of markdown notes becomes a graph through nesting and inclusion links; agents run database-style queries (frontmatter filters, subtree, graph matches, projections) and retrieve a note with its parent context, and can extract, inline or restructure notes, all on plain files.

f: Searchable local history of everything on screen and heard
w: Event-driven capture of screens and audio is turned into OCR and accessibility text, transcripts with speakers, and frames in a local SQLite full-text store with retention and disk-pressure handling; agents search it, get activity summaries and export clips through an MCP server and SDK.

f: Repo-local agent worklog and handoff kept with the code
w: A numbered set of reviewable Markdown memory files (overview, architecture, workflow, security, known issues) plus an append-only JSONL agent worklog and a handoff note, regenerated from git changes and validated, so any coding tool can resume where another left off.

f: Portable single-file memory capsule with WAL, time index and encryption
w: All memory (text, embeddings, lexical index, time index, metadata) lives in one append-only file with a write-ahead log, crash recovery, as-of-time queries and optional encrypted capsules, so a memory can be copied, shared or backed up as one file.

f: Per-type reserved budgets for memory recall
w: Memory recall gives each type of entry (facts, preferences, episodes...) its own token pool retrieved independently, so low-priority types still surface, while behavioral corrections load every time outside the budget competition.

f: Per-agent private database with self-scheduled next run
w: Each agent can opt into its own SQLite database that it designs and queries through db_* tools (schema, bulk CSV import/export, soft delete, changelog, storage quota), plus a single schedule_next_run slot so it wakes itself to act on that data; detail tabs show Schema, Data, Views and Activity.

After each exchange the memories that were injected are scored on whether the advice actually worked, either by the main model through a score tool or by an independent sidecar model to avoid self-grading; helpful memories are promoted and bad ones demoted or archived, shaping future recall.

Memory is tiered: an index always in context, a hot set of pinned files plus files ranked by decayed usage frequency preloaded under byte/token/item budgets and recomputed only at model change or compaction, and cold files read by tool.

f: Keystone memories and trust tiers for shared fleet memory
w: Owners pin 'keystone' memories that act as policy and always surface, and each agent's writes carry a trust tier that decides how its memories rank and propagate to other agents, with outcome signals (reuse, repeat recall) feeding back into retrieval.

f: Tree-index reasoning retrieval for long documents
w: Long PDFs and Markdown files are turned into a table-of-contents style tree (headings detected even without an embedded TOC, with page ranges and summaries); the agent reads the tree and picks the sections to open, giving cited page-level answers with no vector database or chunking.
Scores the agent's memory files out of 100 with critical/warning/info checks (stale daily logs over 30 days, size, config), and builds a prompt asking the agent to clean them up.

Discovers the types and fields already used in a markdown/Obsidian vault, writes a schema, then enforces it on every card, deduplicates entities, fixes wikilinks and orphans, regenerates index (MOC) pages and runs decay cycles that demote untouched cards.

f: Narrative memory with a routing gate
w: Each incoming message is routed by a gate to the ongoing narrative (storyline/topic) it continues, or starts a new one; the agent then loads that narrative's continuity summary and events instead of a flat recent history.

f: Typed schema-driven domain context graph with connectors
w: You define doc types and their schemas, store entities per schema and link them with free-text edge semantics, extract entities from connectors (e.g. MCP sources), and query/maintain this 'brain' deterministically so agents operate on structured, kept-correct domain data rather than fuzzy recall.

f: Linked memory notes that update their neighbours on write
w: Each new memory becomes a note with keywords, tags and a context description; the system finds related past notes, decides which to link, and rewrites the linked notes' context and tags so the memory network evolves as new facts arrive.

f: Interview agent that builds the owner's profile
w: An interviewer agent asks the owner questions about themselves, and the answers are transformed and indexed into the memory a personal agent later retrieves to answer as them.
Camera frames and poses are embedded into a spatial vector store so the agent can answer where it saw something and navigate back to a remembered place, with replayable observation streams.

f: Tiered short/mid/long-term memory with heat-based promotion
w: An OS-inspired memory manager that keeps short-term, mid-term and long-term stores and promotes/consolidates entries between tiers by access heat and recency, with retrieval and dynamic updating, reaching SOTA on the LoCoMo long-term-memory benchmark.

f: Hand-editable Markdown memory with cascade re-index
w: Every memory kind (facts, episodes, profile, agent cases and skills, knowledge pages) lives as Markdown; a watcher and reconciler pick up direct file edits and cascade them into the SQLite and LanceDB indexes, with backfill and per-kind handlers.

f: Code-grounded memory withheld when its cited paths move
w: Each memory packet cites repo paths; when those paths move or change, the memory is flagged stale and withheld from recall, a triage command lists what moved and prints the exact reverify or supersede command for a human, and nothing is bulk-cleared automatically.

f: Encrypted signed knowledge store with expiring agent grants and device sync
w: Personal records are encrypted and signed in an append-only log that syncs between the owner's devices (hybrid logical clocks, relay) and can be recovered; each agent gets a scoped grant that expires and can be revoked, so it only reads what it was allowed to for as long as allowed.

f: Session memory shared as a published dataset
w: Past sessions from several coding agents are scrubbed, indexed and pushed as a dataset; another machine, a teammate or anyone (if public) can recall from it with one flag, and 'ask' answers a question grounded in recalled sessions, naming the sessions used.

Teammates' agents record decisions in parallel into content-addressed event segments synced through the team's own S3 bucket (git experimental); textual merge conflicts cannot happen, and genuine semantic conflicts appear as branches resolved by one new decision.

f: Proactive recall from every coding agent's history on disk
w: Indexes sessions already written by 35 agents (including Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) with files opened, commands and exit codes and exact edits, then surfaces relevant past work at session start, before an edit and after a failed command; hits note decisions marked rejected or accepted and warn when files touched since have changed. No model or embeddings; 97.2% R@5 on LongMemEval-S.

Probes a configured model and compares its behaviour/fingerprint against a sealed baseline to catch a provider silently swapping or updating the model behind a stable name, so a run can flag that the model is no longer the one that was tested.

f: Image blob broker: send images to models as stable URLs
w: Outgoing images get content-hash-keyed, stable, multi-use URLs (local server behind a tunnel or uploads to object storage, drives or image hosts) or provider file uploads, so resent turns stay byte-identical for caching and image tokens are not re-uploaded each turn.

f: Run your own model on a rented GPU pod
w: Point it at an SSH-reachable GPU pod (Prime Intellect, Vast.ai, DataCrunch, AWS); it installs vLLM, starts one or more models with GPU memory split across them, tracks them, streams logs and gives an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the agent.

Saves several Claude Code OAuth logins as credential-only snapshots and, when one hits its limit, activates the next eligible login so the conversation resumes without a hand-over; exhausted logins wait for reset or back-off.

f: Sign in with many coding-product subscriptions as model sources
w: Sign-in flows, token refresh and protocol translators that let the owner use accounts from Kiro, Windsurf, Cursor, Qoder, Trae, Zed, CodeBuddy, iFlow, Kimi, Grok CLI, Antigravity, Cline and others as model backends, normalizing streaming, tool calls, thinking and usage.

f: Free-tier model router with rest periods
w: Keeps a ranked, refreshed list of free models across OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq, Cerebras and Mistral; each request goes to the smartest one the user has a key for that is awake; rate-limited models rest a minute, daily-capped ones rest until reset, mid-answer failures retry on the next; /free shows awake, resting and no-key models, and paid keys in the shell are ignored.

f: Prompt-cache expiry countdown and rebuild cost
w: Shows how long until the provider prompt cache expires for the main agent and each subagent (60 min / 5 min TTLs), detects when a turn rewrote the whole cache and prices that rebuild, so idle-time waste is visible.

f: VRAM hand-off between chat model and image/video generation
w: When the local chat model and an image/video pipeline do not both fit in GPU memory, the chat model is unloaded (confirmed gone) before generation and reloaded afterwards in a finally step, with an honest card explaining the wait; chat history is never touched.

Agents and nodes authenticate with decentralized identifiers (DID); middleware verifies DID auth across HTTP, gRPC and connector calls and the SDK signs requests, giving cross-service agent identity without a central token issuer.

f: Persistent interactive Claude Code session in tmux (subscription-safe)
w: The project states that headless 'claude -p' runs bill against separate paid Agent SDK credit since 2026-06-15, so it keeps one long-lived interactive claude in a tmux pane, types prompts into it under a cross-process lock, parses replies from the pane, detects stalls by the spinner (not silence) and a watchdog force-recovers a wedged session; a test forbids any 'claude -p' use.

f: One-click provider switching for installed coding CLIs
w: Keeps a catalogue of provider presets and writes the chosen one live into each installed CLI's own config (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Hermes, Pi, Grok Build) with backups and project-level patches, plus syncing MCP servers, skills and prompts across them and WebDAV/S3 config sync.

f: Open-loop follow-ups routed to the best-matching character
w: Unresolved topics in direct and group chats are tracked as open loops; a scheduler scores candidate characters (domain match, relationship, recent-recommendation penalties, relevance threshold) and sends a follow-up recommendation introducing the right one.

f: Need discovery proposes new specialist characters
w: On a short interval and daily, recent conversation signals are scanned for needs no existing character covers; above a confidence threshold a new specialist role is generated and offered to the owner as a friend request, with daily limits, suppression windows, expiry and opt-outs for medical, legal and finance.

f: Trust policies for incoming agent calls
w: Markdown trust policies (open, careful, strict) with YAML front matter decide who may call your agent: zero-token allow/deny lists for admins, contacts and blocked keys, onboarding strangers by invite code or payment, and an LLM trust agent only for the 'ask' case; every request must still be signed.

f: Send each errand to the best-value installed harness, with skills and a cost receipt
w: Detects which coding CLIs, subscriptions and model credits are installed (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Copilot, Cline, OpenRouter, local), picks the cheapest capable lane per job, stages the needed skill bundles for the delegate, can ask a panel of stronger models for a second opinion, and reports what each job cost.

f: Repo Mesh: pull-based task queue across your machines
w: Tasks with dependencies go into a queue bound to one repository; idle machines on a peer mesh claim them into fresh worktrees by capability tags and free slots, with spawn budgets, duplicate-dispatch guards, dependency-failure notices and idle-session reaping.

f: Cross-person agent hotline with three-state delivery
w: Two people's agents on different machines talk directly over the owner's own network with a shared secret; send reports sent, delivered-to-process and answered as separate states, and a check tool shows a message nobody picked up.

f: HTTP chat API over any terminal coding agent by screen parsing
w: Runs a TUI agent in a virtual terminal, diffs screen snapshots to extract the agent's messages, strips each agent's input box and chrome, detects readiness, and serves send/messages/events (SSE) plus a web chat.

f: Live messaging and file claims between coding harnesses
w: One local MCP server lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI sessions see who is present, claim files and get overlap warnings before editing, message each other live through a relay, and hand off tasks with a written handoff and review packet.

f: Staff a task team from a large library of specialist agents
w: A router matches the task against hundreds of local and hub specialist agent cards (A2A cards, linted and migrated), shows the model a compressed candidate shortlist to cut routing tokens, and spins up a temporary orchestrator that calls the chosen specialists, with approvals, receipts and a run journal.

Bots, humans and webhooks are all actors with persistent inboxes in shared threads; unaddressed messages go to the thread default bot, only the first @mention in a reply wakes the next bot, a hop limit stops loops, and a hand-off is held until the target bot has caught up on newer thread messages.

f: Magentic manager orchestration with plan review and stall intervention
w: A manager-led orchestration where a lead keeps a task/plan ledger, reviews progress each round, can pause for human plan-review, and detects and intervenes when the team stalls or loops - a distinct pattern beyond simple handoffs or chains.

One agent session can read the text on any other terminal tab, type into it, open new tabs and start agents, keep a group chat and task list with reports that survive restarts, and be told how long each tab has been idle.

f: Auction swarm: agents bid for tasks
w: Tasks are put up for auction; agents submit bids (custom scoring) and the winning agent does the work, also in batches.

f: Hook-based message bus between different coding CLIs
w: Launching any of 11 coding CLIs through hcom installs per-tool hooks that log activity to SQLite and deliver messages mid-turn or wake idle agents, so agents can message each other, read each other's transcripts, file edits and terminal screens, subscribe to status/edit-collision events, and spawn, fork, resume or kill each other in real terminals.

f: Supervisor team of mixed-vendor coding CLIs with durable handoff and inbox
w: A supervisor CLI (e.g. Claude Code) gets MCP tools to assign work to, hand off to (and wait on), or message worker CLIs from other vendors (Codex, Kiro, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kimi, Hermes...), each running with its own login in its own terminal; worker status is read from its terminal, messages queue in an inbox until the recipient is idle, and handoff results survive restarts.

f: tmux-compatible remote daemon for agent teammates
w: A Go daemon speaks enough tmux (split, list, wait-for) over a WebSocket PTY that agents expecting tmux (Claude Code teammates, Codex teams) spawn as native panes; Claude hooks are routed back for notifications.

f: Tower: lead agent running file-scoped missions for worker sessions
w: A lead plans missions with task checklists and reserved file scopes, spawns worker sessions on their own branches, and receives findings and inbox messages; a mission cannot be marked completed with open tasks, no diff, or unread messages, a non-clean review sends it back, and only the lead merges or abandons, all kept in a git-backed store.

f: Always-on goal-driven operator agent with server-paced wake loop
w: One long-running agent plans from a goal, posts jobs, reviews results and merges PRs, keeping its charter, plan and memory in a git repo; the server wakes it every 3-30 minutes only when it is idle and the owner is not typing to it.

f: Which agent needs you: attention ranking and narration
w: Ranks all running agent sessions by how urgently they need the user (waiting for approval, finished, stuck) and can speak a short summary of what needs attention.

f: Single-active lease per task across agent runtimes
w: A task (Work) holds one active lease naming which agent runtime and attempt owns it, with a recovery-pending state and deadline, so two agents (e.g. Codex and Claude) never work the same task at once and a crashed owner is recovered rather than duplicated.

f: Manager agent answers workers' permission dialogs
w: Workers' PermissionRequest hook posts each permission ask to the server, which types it into the manager agent's terminal; the manager allows or denies, and any silence, timeout or error falls back to the normal dialog for a person.
Agents that are not reachable directly register a mailbox; messages to them are held by a relay and delivered when the agent comes back online, with endpoint resolution by address.

f: Cross-repo ticket DAG with per-repo routing
w: A request is decomposed into tickets with a dependency graph and an assigned repo alias; a scheduler runs them in order across repositories, routes each to that repo's admin agent and tracks cost per ticket.

f: Independent review gate on agent-claimed tasks
w: An agent claims a task with its bound runtime session recorded as provenance; submitted work can only be accepted or rejected by an authorized actor other than the assignee, and a rejected review continues the same task.

f: Deferred tasks that wake on other tasks or a deadline
w: A task can be parked to wake when all or any of a set of watched tasks reach an outcome, or when a deadline passes, so a lead can wait for helpers without polling; waits survive restarts and stale ones are reaped.

f: Wave planner with critical path and runway warning
w: A planned task DAG is validated and split into parallel waves, the critical path is computed and shown, dispatch auto-advances as waves finish under a concurrency cap, and a runway indicator warns before the ready queue empties at current fleet speed.

f: Racing experiment forks with a safe fallback
w: When an assistant faces a choice, candidate answers run as isolated forked sessions or worktrees in parallel; the first to complete wins and its answer is replayed onto the original session, and if all fail the most rollback-safe candidate is used.

f: Branches and selective synthesis into a decision brief
w: A question branches to several specialists in parallel; a human selects or excludes each output, and the room publishes an immutable decision brief whose evidence and provenance (which model, which output) stay linked.

f: Hire outside agents over Nostr with paid jobs
w: Agents publish capability cards to Nostr relays; other agents discover them, send jobs, get results and pay in SOL with on-chain verification, spend ceilings, delegation proofs, a job ledger with recovery and reputation, exposed as MCP tools.

f: LLM council: draft, vote, pick winner, refine (TypeScript)
w: Several council member models each draft a plan or document, members vote on the drafts with quorum rules, a winner is selected and a refiner merges the best parts; sessions can be stopped cleanly per owner.

f: Collaborative build DAG with a single-writer lease
w: Several models propose, a coordinator delegates a dependency graph of work, and only the agent holding the writer lease may edit the shared folder at a time, with a gate script and validator between rounds.

f: Capability search over a registry of outside agents with nested teams
w: Agents on different machines register their capabilities with a hub; an agent facing a task searches the registry semantically for teammates, invites them into a group chat, and sub-groups can form for subtasks with async task tracking.

Two people's assistants negotiate a meeting over A2A: one proposes slots, the other counter-proposes against its owner's calendar and working hours until a slot free for both is found, with a shared thread id, a hard hop cap, a daily outbound-call budget and a booking audit.

f: Characters post to a social feed (moments)
w: Each AI character posts moments with images and music themes; an editorial planner rotates content angles so characters differ day to day, an image budget caps generation spend, and the owner can like and comment.
The full orchestrator - classifier routing, agents, MCP tools, realtime voice and tracing - runs entirely on iPhone/iPad/Mac with no server.

f: Wasted-context report and learned read shield
w: Tracks every file read and whether it was later used, prices sessions per model segment, shows heatmaps and an efficiency score, learns which files are usually useless per project and can warn on or block those reads via a .contextignore.

f: Trust stamps carried inside agent-made files
w: Agents stamp files they produce or verify with compact claims (trust score, source, evidence, AI-made, verified), embedded in the file itself (Markdown, DOCX, PDF, images, spreadsheets and more) or a sidecar, optionally signed; the next agent runs a check and builds on verified claims instead of re-verifying.

f: Which session is burning your plan quota (session runway)
w: Attributes live Codex and Claude token use to individual sessions against the 5-hour and weekly windows, with API-equivalent price per session and a pace estimate for the week.

f: Pause, edit and forward model requests (request interception)
w: Turn on interception for a session and each outgoing model request is held in the dashboard, where the owner can inspect and edit the payload and then approve it (or let it time out) before it reaches the provider; edits are summarised and reflected in the log.

f: System prompt history and diff across versions
w: Captures the system prompt each agent version actually sends, keeps its history and shows what changed between versions in the dashboard, next to a workflow timeline of calls.

f: Tape trace inspector and model-view replay
w: Every session is an append-only tape of facts (messages, provider attempts, tool surfaces, view manifests); a trace inspector shows each request and can rebuild exactly what the model saw for any past call, with lineage across compaction.

f: Spend burn-rate forecast to month end
