w: Fits the last 7 days of spend with linear regression and smoothing to project month-end cost and days until the budget limit is reached.
Costs page that prices scheduled-job runs, flags token anomalies, shows week-over-week change and cache savings, and produces an optimization score with concrete suggestions.

f: Unified usage history across other coding CLIs, kept after they delete it
w: Parses the session logs of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode, Pi, Antigravity and Grok into one normalized, priced history with daily/weekly/monthly, per-model and per-project views, cached so the history survives after those tools delete their own files, with shareable text/SVG reports.

f: Verify a run record and check whether it reproduces
w: Each run leaves a hash-chained trace with receipts and evidence; trace verify checks the record was not altered, and trace reproduce compares the recorded journal with a fresh run of the same workflow and classifies every task by why it did or did not reproduce, with lineage and an OpenTelemetry export.

f: Live reasoning map the agent maintains
w: Through MCP tools the agent keeps a revisioned graph of goals, hypotheses with confidence, options scored per criterion, experiments, evidence and supports/challenges links, with sources; the user can edit it and their edits are protected from the agent.

f: Agent process and resource usage window
w: Scans and samples CPU/memory of every agent child process (Codex, Claude Code) across the process tree and shows it in a resource window.

f: Config layer map and skill/hook/MCP dependency graph
w: Shows every skill, command, agent and hook from user, project and plugin sources with which one overrides which, maps how hooks, skills, commands and MCP servers depend on each other as numbered chains, and extracts each skill's trigger keywords with example prompts that would fire it.

f: Scoped spend budgets with incidents and auto-pause
w: Monthly spend budgets per company, agent or project with soft-warning and hard-stop thresholds; crossing one opens a budget incident, pauses the scope and cancels its running work until the owner resolves it, with a costs page and provider quota windows.

Writes a complete runtime (portable Node, built daemon and start scripts for macOS, Linux and Windows) onto a USB stick with AES and HMAC keys in its config, and detects and verifies the stick when plugged in.

f: Run the assistant's scheduled skills on GitHub Actions with no machine on
w: A scheduler workflow on GitHub Actions cron dispatches skills and chained skill runs on free CI runners using a chosen coding CLI, keeps memory and outputs committed in the repo, sends results by Telegram, and audits network egress of each run.

f: Encrypted file transfer between your machines (direct peer, server fallback)
w: Files and workspace folders move between registered machines in encrypted chunks, trying a direct peer connection first and falling back to a server-routed path with size limits and route caching.

f: Detached dispatch of jobs to another host
w: Send a durable job (workspace, session, model, permission policy) to another machine running the app; the target provisions its runtime and syncs model config, keeps running if the controller disconnects, keeps a reconnectable transcript, and permission requests can be answered remotely.

f: Detect, install and update other agent CLIs from a catalog
w: An embedded, refreshable catalog of 109 agent CLIs with detection strategies (binary, npm, pip, brew) and installers per package manager, checking versions in parallel and offering updates, exposed over CLI, TUI, tray, REST and gRPC.

The agent never mutates infrastructure itself: it submits a JSON intent that a deterministic controller validates against a five-action allowlist and a generation guard before applying; known problems (e.g. OOM) are fixed by rules, novel ones escalate to a companion agent whose proposal needs human approval in Slack.

f: Deploy apps to the owner's own servers from a typed intent
w: A typed config says which servers the owner has and which apps they want; the tool resolves it into a desired-state graph and plans, applies and prunes real infrastructure (hosts over SSH, Cloudflare, Forgejo, Komodo, GitHub) with locks, migrations and backups.

f: Distributed runner fleet with heartbeat liveness and restart
w: Agent runners run across the owner's own machines as pods that send batched heartbeats; the control plane tracks liveness, detects stalled/dead runners and restarts execution, with isolated per-agent block-store workspaces, all steered from one console.
Each agent workspace can join its own Tailscale or NetBird overlay network through a managed sidecar, so an agent's computer reaches private hosts without exposing the main app.

After a config change (for example a new model id), the agent's health endpoint is probed; K failures in M minutes restore the last config that was seen healthy, restart the service and alert by Telegram/Slack/Discord/webhook.

f: TLA+ models of agent runtime protocols checked in CI
w: Compaction, delegated turns, file locks, message queue, task and workspace lifecycles, workspace leases, history crash recovery and async primitives are specified in TLA+ and model-checked by a CI workflow, catching races before they ship.

f: Config releases: run the approved config, not the session's copy
w: Agent sessions load agents, skills and runtime config from a read-only, built release of the base branch rather than their own working checkout; a release can be quarantined, and runtimes swap or reload it in place, so an agent editing its own config cannot change what is running until it is merged.

f: Plugin facets across processes with replicated state
w: Plugins declare services they provide and need; each plugin splits into facets that load in the right place (agent worker, terminal UI, web UI), services keep stable facades across reconnects, and authoritative state replicates to local and remote consumers as atomic delta transactions.

Answer questions over very long documents by splitting them into chunks, letting member agents answer from each chunk in parallel, then retrieving and summarizing the useful partial answers into one reply.

The owner defines named prompt transformations (summary, key insights, questions and custom ones), tries them in a playground, and applies them to any added source so each document gets stored, searchable insight notes.

f: Autonomous data discovery with refuter-verified insights
w: Pointed at a warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, Postgres and others), the agent learns the schema, picks what to investigate within a query budget, writes and fixes SQL, then a separate verifier and refuter re-query every claimed number before an insight and ranked recommendation is shown.
Crawls a site and writes an llms.txt (and full variant) summarising its pages so an agent can load a compact map of the site.

f: Social-media crawler cluster for opinion data
w: A crawler subsystem (MindSpider) scrapes posts and user comments across Weibo, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou and other platforms, with broad-topic extraction and deep sentiment crawling, feeding an analysis pipeline.

The agent supplies a JSON schema and the tool extracts every matching data point from a large set of documents in chunks, returning structured rows as a file instead of reading everything into context.

f: Numbers traced back to the code output that produced them
w: Every numeric value in the written text must reference a value in the analysis code's outputs; values are checked against those outputs and rendered as links back to their source, so a reader can verify each number.

f: Adaptive tutor that plans lessons from your feedback
w: Builds a syllabus for any topic, delivers one lesson at a time, reads the learner's annotations and feedback to shape the next lesson, then evaluates and summarizes, with learning-method skills (Feynman, deep, graph).

f: Citation and quote-fidelity verification against source documents
w: Every finding's quote is matched against the extracted source text; on top of fuzzy matching, a deterministic guard checks salient tokens (amounts, durations, percentages, negation) so a quote that changes '90 days' to '30 days' or drops a 'not' is rejected as fabricated.

From a scenario or document, generates demographically grounded persona agents, runs them on a simulated social feed and an AMM prediction market over rounds, then reports the outcome distribution, counterfactuals and a written report.

f: Multi-analyst stock research with bull/bear and risk debates
w: For one stock, market, sector, fundamentals and news analyst agents write reports, bull and bear researchers debate them, a research manager decides, a trader proposes a position and aggressive/neutral/conservative risk agents debate it before a final view, at selectable depth.
Runs the crawler locally: sitemap discovery, crawl scope and regex rules, depth limits, robots handling, canonical URLs, relevance-ranked site maps and HTML-to-Markdown, without a hosted API key.
Given a URL, extracts the site's logo, color roles, fonts and brand marks into a structured brand profile, with an LLM pass that falls back safely when the model fails.

f: Graph-based web exploration with adversarial answer synthesis
w: Research runs crawl pages as nodes of a growing knowledge graph, choose the next link by reasoning over the graph, then write several drafts that are attacked and revised before the final answer; the web UI streams the live graph.

Researches a topic over the last 30 days by fanning out to Reddit, X, YouTube transcripts, TikTok, HN, Polymarket odds, GitHub, Bluesky and more in parallel, then dedupes, clusters, reranks by real engagement and writes a grounded brief (optionally an HTML page).

f: Scholarly and filings source providers (PubMed, ClinicalTrials, EDGAR, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar)
w: Typed research providers query PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, SEC EDGAR filings, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, arXiv and Wikipedia directly, normalizing results into citable source documents, with robots.txt checks and an SSRF-safe fetcher.

Typed tools fetch income statements, balance sheets, cash flows, key ratios, segments, earnings, SEC filings (and read them), insider trades, institutional holdings, news and stock screens for a ticker, so the agent can research a company from primary data (informational only, not advice).

f: Citation DOI cross-verification across scholarly databases
w: Every printed citation is looked up in CrossRef, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar and kept only when its DOI appears in at least two of them, so drafts carry no invented references.

f: Claim labels in research reports: verified with source, inferred, missing
w: Every claim in a research report carries [VERIFIED:url], [INFERRED] or [MISSING]; verified labels must point at a collected source, synthesis may not upgrade inferred or missing claims, and the report shows counts of each so the reader sees what is actually known.

f: Per-platform backend routing with a health doctor
w: Each platform has a preferred and fallback access route (CLI tool, API, MCP or scraper); a doctor probes every route, reports what works and how to fix the rest, and the project swaps a route when a site blocks it without the owner changing anything.

f: Job portal scanners across ~100 ATS providers with liveness checks
w: Scans job boards directly through ATS APIs and pages (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday and ~100 more) with SSRF/IP guards, then checks each posting is still open through API, page and browser fallbacks before it is evaluated.

f: Prediction-market odds and public data feeds
w: Ask 'what are the odds of X' and the agent searches a unified market index across Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, Metaculus, PredictIt, Betfair and Smarkets, plus FRED economic series and ACLED conflict events, with freshness tracking.

f: Autoresearch: agent population improves a graded task
w: Give a codebase and a grader; several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) work in isolated workspaces, every commit is scored by a sealed grader the agents cannot read, and they share attempts, notes and skills through a hub, optionally split into islands with migration, until an auto-stop rule fires.
While answering, the search agent decides whether a quick card applies and shows it next to the answer: stock quote with chart, calculation result or weather, each fetched by its own widget executor.

A runtime proxy and watcher that intercepts a deployed agent's model/tool traffic, evaluates the live trajectory with a trained safety model, and intervenes (blocks or flags) unsafe steps, exposed as a server, CLI and websocket proxy.

f: Context trust scores with provenance filtering and decay
w: Every piece of prompt context carries its provenance and a trust score (CLI 0.95, chat apps 0.70-0.75, web fetch 0.50, memory 0.70...); summaries and old history decay in trust, and a filter drops parts below a minimum trust or from blocked provenances before the model call, logging each exclusion.

f: Backup before approved destructive file changes
w: Before the agent deletes or overwrites files, the approval names the exact change and a recoverable copy goes to a bounded backup vault with a receipt; if backups are off or space runs out the prompt says plainly that the change may be unrecoverable.

f: Edit gate that catches an AI change removing an auth guard
w: Compiles the backend's routes, guards, queries and side effects into a deterministic behavior graph, arms a baseline, then after each agent edit diffs the graph and blocks the edit (via a PostToolUse hook) if a route lost its guard, became newly exposed or broke an invariant; offline, no model calls.

f: Per-project agent VM with host-held keys
w: Each project gets its own pre-provisioned VM where agents can run with full autonomy; git signing and push go through a forwarded SSH agent so private keys never enter the VM, and secrets are rendered into tmpfs that disappears on reboot.

f: Agent writes as reviewable change requests with field-level diffs
w: Every agent write to shared data or docs is packaged as a change request carrying a message, author and per-operation field-level diff; a person reviews, revises individual operations, and merges or rejects, with workspace rules deciding what auto-merges.

f: Agent BOM and cryptographic seal with verify
w: Takes a cryptographic snapshot (seal) of an agent's whole definition and emits an AI-BOM (CycloneDX) listing its models, tools, prompts and MCP servers, then can verify later that the running agent matches the sealed one.

When an agent runs npm/pip (and other) installs, the requested packages are identified and evaluated for malicious or risky signs before the install runs, blocking or asking, with a repair step for already-installed bad packages.

f: Task scope contract enforced on every tool call
w: Each task gets a confirmed contract (review-only or edit, allowed paths, a budget for spawning helper agents); a guard on tool calls denies writes outside it, extra delegation or repeated re-checks, and explains why with a suggested next step, in watch or enforce levels.

A periodic job compares each agent's last hour against its 7-day baseline and raises deduplicated alerts for risk spikes, never-seen actions, call-frequency spikes and cost spikes, using plain counts over the audit log.

f: Agent profiles that hide paths and gate commands, with a scriptable policy
w: A profile sets allow, ask or deny per command and CLI, and hide or show per file or folder so hidden paths are absent from what the agent sees; a policy script and built-ins (mount-root guard, output cap) gate every filesystem op and session write before it runs.

f: Runtime threat monitor that pauses or kills the agent's sandbox
w: A daemon watches the agent container's processes, network connections, files, logs and cgroup usage, matches them against Sigma rules and GTFOBins patterns, records evidence, and automatically pauses or kills the container when it sees something dangerous.

f: Formal prover for sandbox policy changes
w: Before a policy change is applied, a prover compares the candidate against the current boundary and lists any new reach it grants (a new host with credentials, a new API method, process or write access), so only widening changes wait for human review.

f: Sandbox learning mode writes least-privilege profiles
w: Run an agent once in learning mode; its file access is traced (strace on Linux, eslogger on macOS) and collapsed into a least-privilege filesystem profile that auto-loads next time, with drift detection that prompts before widening a profile later.

f: Kernel-enforced agent policies that follow process lineage
w: A YAML/DSL policy compiles to eBPF rules that kill forbidden actions anywhere under the agent's process tree (e.g. no git push, no writes outside /src, even via scripts), enforce causal order such as tests before commit, and only notify when outputs go stale; the kill reason is fed back to the agent through hooks or MCP.

f: API-method-level egress rules (HTTP, GraphQL, JSON-RPC, MCP)
w: The sandbox egress proxy enforces rules at the request level, not only by domain: allow or deny by HTTP method and path, GraphQL operation, JSON-RPC/MCP method or websocket, with live policy updates and token-grant injection per endpoint.

f: Per-service egress policy presets with provenance
w: Ready-made network policy presets per service (GitHub, Gmail, Outlook, Jira, npm, PyPI, Hugging Face, Brave, Tavily, local inference...) that are added or removed as a unit, with recorded provenance and ownership, fail-closed removal and a readable scope summary.

When a sandboxed command is denied, the failure is attributed to a file path or network host and the user gets a card proposing the narrowest sensible grant (nearest directory, never the home or workspace root); accepted grants are stored and reused.

f: Page sanitizer against hidden prompt injection and data leaks
w: Before a page reaches the model, rules strip hidden text, HTML comments, invisible Unicode, meta/attribute/JSON-LD injection, encoded payloads and known injection phrases, redact cross-origin frames and user comments, and mask PII and secrets.

In strict mode the agent may only send pre-approved response templates (with fields filled from context); generation picks and fills a template instead of writing free text, so wording stays compliant.
Flags retrieved chunks or user input that are padded, oversized or repetitively structured to make the model forget its system prompt or exhaust the token budget, on input and retrieval paths.

f: Automated red-teaming of your own agent
w: Generates attacks against the owner's agent with plugins (indirect prompt injection, excessive agency, tool discovery, SSRF, data leaks and many more) and multi-turn strategies (iterative, Crescendo, GOAT), grades the responses and reports which attacks succeeded.

f: Injection scanning of images, QR codes, PDFs, audio and video
w: Before untrusted files reach the agent, text is extracted from PDFs, images (OCR), QR codes, audio and video and run through the injection pattern set, and the report says what could not be read so a clean result is not mistaken for a full scan.

f: Exfiltration detection in inline code plus project taint
w: Shell commands and inline interpreter code in 15+ languages (python -c, node -e, PowerShell and more) are parsed for reads of secrets flowing to the network, including obfuscation; once untrusted content is read the project is marked tainted with its source so later risky calls are blocked.

An input rail checks each user message against the configured allowed and disallowed topics and blocks or redirects off-topic requests before the main model answers, composable in order with jailbreak and content-safety rails.
Before a resource is fetched, a gateway plugin checks its URL, domain and IP against VirusTotal (with a small cache and optional submission of unknown URLs) and blocks known-malicious ones.

f: Secrets lent from the owner's phone, in memory only
w: API keys live on the paired phone; the computer's daemon mounts them into an in-memory file system over a Noise-encrypted WebRTC link, a command can use a key without reading it (exec with the file), and when the phone app closes a grace timer unmounts and wipes everything.

f: Read-only cloud action gate before credentials attach
w: Every cloud or forge API call the agent's sandboxed code makes is resolved to the IAM actions it needs (from AWS and GCP permission datasets, plus GitHub, GitLab and Kubernetes policies) and checked against a read-only policy before any credential is attached, so the agent can safely be pointed at production.

f: Keyring: leased, scoped credentials for agents via MCP broker
w: Instead of handing an agent raw keys, grants give scoped, revocable access leased for at most 15 minutes, sealed to the agent's identity key, approved with WebAuthn, and every access is a signed event; an MCP broker serves them.

f: Cedar policy for agent actions with observe-then-enforce
w: Agent tool calls are evaluated against Cedar policies locally; a policy can run in observe mode (record what it would have blocked) before being switched to enforce, and every decision and outcome is written to an attributable ledger.

f: Post-hoc audit rules over agent commits
w: A git hook audits each agent change against codified rules: secret leaks, sensitive files, unauthorized or bulk changes, deleted config, broken build, network exfiltration, persistence, privilege escalation, path traversal, junk files, read-before-write and honest reporting, with fix suggestions and a report.

f: Triggered policy kinds: intent guards, playbooks, tool guides, tool guards, output formatters
w: Policies are authored files whose triggers (natural-language similarity, keyword, app, agent state, tool, always) select what applies: intent guards answer or block certain requests, playbooks inject step lists, tool guides enrich tool descriptions, tool guards and approvals check calls, and output formatters reshape the final answer, each decision recorded.

f: Detection rules over every agent's activity on this computer
w: Installs hooks into dozens of agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, Hermes, Goose...) and normalises their actions into one event model; CEL rules and multi-step chain rules (secret read then egress, permission denied then runtime bypass, guardrails off then egress) raise findings, optionally block via pre-action hooks, and build SHA-256-manifested case bundles.

f: MCP tool poisoning and rug-pull detection
w: Flags MCP tool descriptions that hide instructions for the model, tools requesting more privilege than their purpose needs, and servers whose tool definitions change after approval (rug pull).

f: Tiered hook chain where installed add-ons cannot loosen policy
w: Plugins sit in ordered tiers (policy prepend, user, append, built-in); an outermost security module lets policy hooks, managed instructions and tool lists skip past user-installed plugins, refuses user-tier tool registration under an MCP allowlist, and re-runs any tool check a user plugin loosened so a rule-based deny always holds; unreadable policy fails closed.

A command scores this machine 0-100 on what a compromised agent could read, reach and run (secrets on disk, egress, privilege, containment, supply chain, enforcement coverage) and renders a report with what to fix.

f: Agent spending policy: one-time payment approvals and new-recipient confirmation
w: Money the agent holds passes through code limits (per-transaction and daily caps); instead of raising a cap, the owner authorises one payment bound to recipient, amount and expiry, and the first payment to any never-paid address always needs confirming; an optional allowlist is absolute.

f: LM-emulated tools for agent risk testing
w: Tools are described by specs and their outputs are simulated by a model (standard or adversarial simulator), so risky scenarios such as deleting data or leaking private info can be tested without real side effects; generated red-team cases are scored by separate safety and helpfulness evaluators.

f: Threat assessment of an agent workflow graph
w: Parses an agent setup (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents, ADK, n8n and more) into a graph of agents, tools and data flows, draws it, and generates a threat report against the MAESTRO framework.

f: Main agent isolated from the outside world via disposable workers
w: The main reasoning agent keeps no web, file or API reach of its own; any outside-world task goes to a short-lived worker launched from a template in a container with allowed paths and a typed result contract, so injected instructions or hostile code stay inside the worker and only structured results come back.

f: Safe outputs: agent proposes writes, a separate step applies them
w: The unattended agent runs read-only and can only emit typed write requests (comment, label, PR, issue) through a safe-outputs MCP server; requests are sanitized, capped per type, redacted, optionally checked by a threat-detection pass, then applied by a separate privileged step.

f: Information-flow labels and egress allowlist as testable policy
w: Tool outputs carry sensitivity labels on a lattice (public to secret); policy denies a tool call whose sink clearance is below the data it would carry, and an egress library denies destinations outside a per-tool domain allowlist; benchmarked against AgentDojo prompt-injection tasks.

f: Agents push only their own branch; work lands by change request
w: A git proxy enforces that each agent session can push only to its own branch, and the only way to move commits elsewhere is a change request: a session's request always targets the branch it started from (only a person may retarget), and a human approves the merge, which happens server-side.

An agent's allowed autonomy grows from its track record rather than a fixed permission set, and a self-model module (SOMA) lets it propose actions and learning on its own initiative, with dedup so it does not nag.

f: Share a skill as a remote API without revealing it, with trust tiers and auto-revoke
w: The owner exposes a skill so peers get only its name, schema and results, never the prompt; four trust tiers gate each skill, hidden skills answer 'unknown skill', and granted access is downgraded automatically when the shared goal (OKR) completes.

f: Air-gapped session relayed over SSH with pinned TLS
w: Run the agent on a machine with no internet; the laptop relays the raw bytes to the model over an SSH tunnel with TLS pinned end to end, so the air-gapped box never talks to the network directly.

An agent plans and runs a penetration test against an authorized target inside a Docker toolbox, tracking a task tree, executing commands with an audit trace, and scoring itself on local CTF-style benchmarks.

f: Approvals rendered in the calling agent via MCP elicitation
w: When a tool served over MCP reaches a risky step, the approve/deny prompt is sent as an MCP elicitation so it appears in whichever agent called the tool (Claude Code, Cursor), and the decision is stored as an event.

A deterministic verification service exercises an agent's changes - builds, tests and browser/API behavior - stores the captured evidence, runs before/after differential verification and synthetic-user QA, and returns an evidence-based verdict, all local and exposed over MCP, instead of an LLM reading the diff.

f: Memory retrieval that tunes its own policy, gated by replay
w: Recall telemetry is diagnosed for failure patterns, candidate retrieval policies (weights, retrievers, consolidation settings) are proposed, replayed against past queries, and promoted only if they score better, with a policy store to keep or roll back versions.

Run, evaluate, reflect and evolve the spec across generations with convergence detection, material-progress checks, drift recording, a frugality budget, a watchdog and rewind to an earlier generation.

f: Compile a skill into a deterministic pipeline
w: An agent reads a working SKILL.md and splits it into plain code for fixed steps plus typed model calls only where judgment is needed, emitting a durable workflow (DBOS, Temporal, Inngest, Cloudflare) with human approval gates and a scorecard comparing cost and accuracy against running the skill as an agent.

f: Git-backed propose/approve for skills with per-file ownership
w: Skills, tool manuals and knowledge are git files; anyone (including an agent that hits a broken skill mid-task) can propose a change, and on protected branches it routes to the owners of exactly the files it touches and ships only once they approve, with the git history as the audit trail.
A scenario harness that replays poisoning attacks against a memory store adapter and scores block rate and false positives, so memory defences can be measured and compared.

f: Skill compliance check from generated scenarios
w: From a skill, a spec of required steps is generated, test scenarios are generated from the spec, the agent is run on them, and its tool-call trace is classified and graded as compliant or not, producing a report of where the agent ignores the skill.
Each test describes a user persona, goal and expected outcome; a model plays that user in a multi-turn chat with the agent and a judge decides whether the expected outcome was reached.

f: Auto-authored test scenarios proved before they are kept
w: Point the harness at an agent's source; it works out what the agent does, builds a real world its tools act on (SQLite/Postgres state), writes scenarios with setup and checks, and keeps only scenarios it can prove run, all driven as a chat.

f: Agent test suites with mocked tools and LLM-authored cases
w: Record real conversations into test cases or have an LLM author and segment them, then run suites against an agent with tool calls mocked by matcher, model overrides, assertions on replies and tool chains, and an LLM judge, with queued runs and stored results.

f: Screenshot-based success judge for GUI and web runs
w: A vision-model evaluator reads the task, the action history and the screenshots of a browser or phone run and decides whether the task actually succeeded; the verdict feeds a Reflexion retry with a written lesson.

f: Eval stability report, judge audit and KB-mined deterministic checks
w: Runs an eval suite N times and lists which cases flipped verdicts, blaming each flip on agent variance or judge flakiness; audits the LLM judge against known ground truth; and mines deterministic fact checks from the knowledge base to replace judge calls.

f: Train a crew from human feedback over several runs
w: A train command runs the crew N times, asks the human for feedback on each task's output, has a model turn feedback plus outputs into concrete suggestions, stores them per agent, and injects them into the agents' prompts on later runs.

f: Approved-run flywheel export (eval cases and training JSONL)
w: Runs the owner has approved are redacted and turned locally into trace records, context cards, eval cases and training-ready JSONL with readiness metrics, each against a JSON schema, without training a model or sending telemetry.

f: Train the local model from everyday chat feedback
w: An OpenAI-compatible server sits in front of a self-hosted model; each conversation turn becomes a training sample, the person's next message is judged into a reward or a hindsight hint, and asynchronous RL or on-policy distillation (optionally LoRA) updates the model while it keeps serving.

Operators and pipelines that turn documents into fine-tuning data: QA and multi-hop QA, chain-of-thought, code, text-to-SQL, tool-use samples, and embedding/reranker pairs with hard-negative mining, plus cleaning and filters.

Fingerprints past worker sessions (task labels, tools, files, keywords), clusters similar ones and flags whether the agent's approach to the same kind of task has evolved or is inconsistent, as a standardisation hint.

f: Turn repeated owner instructions into standing rules, and measure if they worked
w: Scans the owner's own past messages, clusters rewordings and typos of the same instruction ('keep it simple', 'dont complex this'), offers each repeat as a rule (yes/no/reword) for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, and on later runs counts how often it was said before vs since.

f: Versioned prompts with weighted A/B variants
w: Prompt templates get auto-incremented versions; an A/B test assigns weighted variants so a named prompt resolves to one variant per call, letting prompt changes be compared live.

f: Self-made curriculum to learn an application
w: Given an app or domain (e.g. spreadsheets), the agent writes itself a course of progressively harder practice tasks, attempts each, and keeps the working code as reusable tools in its tool repository.

f: Strategy genes and capsules (GEP) distilled from skills and runs
w: Experience is stored as compact strategy Genes (signals to match, strategy, constraints) and Capsules (a validated application with execution trace); skill docs and conversations are distilled into genes, a selector picks genes by run signals, and candidates are mutated, evaluated in a sandbox and recalled with verification.

f: Team skill mining with gates, scope promotion and auto-pull
w: A background worker mines captured sessions from every teammate's agents for repeated procedures, writes SKILL.md files, checks them with a gate runner, promotes them from personal to project or org scope, publishes them and auto-pulls them into every agent on the team.

f: Find and prune unused skills, MCP servers and subagents by transcript evidence
w: Reads past sessions to count which installed skills, MCP servers and subagents actually fired, estimates the context tokens each idle item costs every session, marks unused ones (holding back items with incomplete evidence) and prunes them interactively with a full restore.

f: Coaching rules over the owner's agent sessions (any harness)
w: Parses session logs from Claude Code, Codex, opencode and VS Code Copilot and runs 45 declarative rules (written in a small safe DSL) for prompt quality, session hygiene, tool mastery and context use, giving the owner scores, trends and specific advice.

Runs groups of rollouts per task, verifies them, has the model compare winners and losers to extract semantic lessons, and updates an experience library injected into the prompt, improving the agent without weight updates.

f: Hookify: turn an unwanted behaviour into an enforced rule
w: The user says what the agent did wrong (or lets a conversation analyzer find it) and gets a plain markdown rule that warns or blocks matching tool calls, prompts or stop attempts (e.g. dangerous rm, editing secrets, stopping without tests), enforced by hooks from then on.

f: Learn from other coding agents' failed sessions
w: Scans the local session logs of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Grok and OpenCode, finds repeated failures and writes corrections into the matching instruction file (CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md).

f: Skillbook of learned strategies (reflector + skill manager)
w: After each task or piece of feedback, a reflector analyses the trace and a skill manager applies small add/update/remove operations to a persistent Skillbook of strategies (with helpful/harmful tallies and deduplication), which is injected into later runs without fine-tuning.

An agent's change to its own schemas, workflows, effects or config goes through propose, shadow (run the change against a copy of the world and summarize its effects), approve, apply and receipt phases, with a review UI for drafts; every external effect returns a signed receipt for replay.

f: Continual harness: ranked supplemental state refined by evidence
w: Supplemental prompts, memories, skill descriptions and reusable sub-agent specs are durable harness entries ranked by relevance to the current goal; /refine (and an auto-refine arm) plans small evidence-backed edits to them, never the base system prompt, with recorded snapshots for rollback.

f: Handoff brief when a session nears its token budget
w: A listener watches token use; past a threshold it synthesizes a validated handoff brief (decisions, open tickets, files touched) and renders it as Markdown so a fresh session can resume the work.

f: Fork a session into a different agent harness
w: Fork a conversation, from any message, into another harness (for example a Claude Code session continued in Codex or OpenCode), recreating its worktree if needed.
Export a conversation with its media into an encrypted share file that another user imports as a native session, with media URLs rewritten.

f: External session stores (Postgres, Redis, S3) with a conformance suite
w: Agent session transcripts are mirrored to and resumed from a pluggable store (Postgres, Redis or S3 examples), and a shared conformance test checks any new store behaves the same, so sessions can live off-machine and resume elsewhere.

f: One searchable archive of sessions from every agent client
w: Adapters ingest sessions losslessly from Claude Code, Claude desktop and claude.ai exports, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Letta Code, Devin, pi and more into a local or S3 store with full-text and vector search, synced on a schedule and exposed to any agent over MCP ('check how we solved this before').

f: Conversation as an editable tree with structural undo
w: The session is a document tree: the user can fold selected history into a thread, move or copy items between branches, and undo or redo any structural change, so context is something you edit rather than only append to.

f: Lossless token-compact encoding for structured tool results with session deltas
w: Tool results that are JSON/YAML/CSV are sent to the model in a compact, model-readable text format that round-trips losslessly and, across turns, sends only deltas of repeated structure, cutting tool-result tokens by roughly half or more.

f: Capability gateway MCP for any agent
w: One remote MCP server gives any agent (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor) a person's assigned skills, plugins, MCP connections and Google/Microsoft capabilities through search_capabilities, execute_capability, list_skills and get_skill, with org/team assignment and per-tool policy.

A catalog of ~330 site and app adapters as YAML pipelines; when one breaks, a failure classifier picks a remedy, patches the adapter, verifies the fix and quarantines adapters that keep failing, and each task routes to the strongest operator (API, local, browser, accessibility, then pixels).

f: Single-file SQLite agent filesystem with copy-on-write overlay
w: An agent's files, key-value state and tool-call timeline live in one SQLite file that can be mounted (FUSE on Linux, NFS on macOS), layered copy-on-write over a host folder so the real files stay untouched, run a program sandboxed against it, and snapshot or restore it by copying the file.

f: Virtual filesystem and shell over SaaS and data sources
w: Gmail, Slack, Google Drive/Docs/Sheets, Notion, GitHub, Linear, S3, Postgres, Redis, vector stores and more mount side by side under one root, and a built-in bash-compatible shell (pipes, jobs, redirection) lets the agent use ls, grep, find, jq and awk across all of them, plus virtual CLIs like slack and git that need nothing installed.

f: Embedded POSIX shell with built-in coreutils and jq for every OS
w: The agent's shell commands run in an in-process POSIX shell interpreter with built-in coreutils and jq, keeping env and working directory between calls, so the same commands work on Windows without bash or WSL; background jobs and output truncation are handled.

f: MCP server inspector (tools, resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation, app views)
w: A browser inspector connects to any MCP server (with OAuth and custom headers) and lets the owner list and call tools, read resources, run prompts, answer sampling/elicitation requests, watch notifications and preview MCP App views with an iframe console.

f: Fusion: add vision and tools to any model via the gateway
w: The gateway injects MCP-backed capabilities (a vision tool that describes images, a tool-fallback MCP and a ToolHub of shared tools) plus hosted web search into requests for models that lack them, so a text-only model behind a third-party agent can still see images and search.

Typed record tables (formulas, filters, views, attachments, CSV import) where a column can be an AI field that classifies, extracts, summarizes, translates or generates text or images from other fields per row, with dependency tracking.

f: Double-entry accounting books the assistant keeps
w: A bookkeeping plugin with chart of accounts, journal entries, opening balances, fiscal years and multiple currencies; the assistant posts entries from conversation and the owner sees balance sheets, reports and time series with server-side validation.

f: Download manager from chat with cloud upload
w: From a chat command the user queues a direct link, torrent/magnet, NZB, cloud folder or video page; it downloads via aria2/qBittorrent/yt-dlp/rclone with per-file selection, shows a live progress message with cancel, then uploads or mirrors to Google Drive, any rclone remote or back to the chat.

f: Security testing tool pack (pentest and forensics)
w: The agent can run web vulnerability tests (SQLi, XSS, SSRF, command injection, traversal, CORS, GraphQL, race conditions), recon (DNS, vhosts, TLS SANs, S3 buckets, git secrets) and forensics (PCAP credential/DNS/TLS analysis, Volatility memory analysis, malicious Office macros) as MCP tools.

f: Shared MCP server pool across sessions
w: Instead of each agent session spawning its own copy of every MCP server, one process per server is shared through a Unix-socket or HTTP proxy, scoped per project when needed, with respawn de-duplication and zombie/fd-leak protection, cutting memory when many sessions run.

f: JSONPath edit tool for structured files
w: The agent views, sets, adds and removes values in JSON files by JSONPath expression instead of text find-and-replace, so config edits stay valid JSON.

f: Context kits auto-equipped by detected stack
w: The owner keeps named kits of conventions, tools and voice; on launch the tool detects languages, git state, machine and commands, picks the matching kit and writes its fragments into a local gitignored overlay the agent reads, never touching committed instruction files, with an explain command.

f: Declarative skills and MCP sync to other agents with a lock file
w: One YAML file (composable with extends for org/team/project) lists skills, commands, MCP servers and instructions from Git sources; a sync converts them into each agent's native format (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI...), diffs a content-hashed lock file so only changes are touched, and resolves secret placeholders from env or a password manager.

f: Private team skill registry with review and scanning
w: A team runs its own skill registry: members publish versioned skill packages to namespaces, each submission is security-scanned and reviewed before it is listed, and others search and install through a CLI, with roles and an audit log.

f: Drive and test terminal UIs with a shared human attach
w: Any command runs in a named background PTY session; the agent reads logs, waits for given text, takes a screen snapshot and types keys, while a human can attach to the very same session, interact, and detach. A dev script wrapped this way never blocks the agent.

f: Installable apps: UI, agents, skills, schedules and a backend
w: An app is a manifest bundling a purpose-built dashboard, its own agents and skills, schedules and an optional backend service that the host provisions, supervises, restarts and reaps; apps install from git-backed registries with caches and recovery.

f: Guardrail skills that block the first matching edit
w: Skills declared as guardrails in a rules file (path globs, content regexes, block/suggest/warn) stop the first Edit/Write to a matching file until the agent has read the skill, with skip markers and an env override.

f: MCP gateway with virtual servers and REST/gRPC translation
w: One endpoint federates many upstream MCP servers, REST APIs and gRPC services; tools from different sources are composed into virtual servers, with health checks, auth reactivation and translation of stdio, REST and gRPC services into MCP.

f: Semantic skill auto-activation that abstains on near-ties
w: An embedding model scores each message against skill-authored trigger phrases; a skill activates only with a clear lead over the runner-up (deterministic file/phrase rules still fire), loads its required MCP servers, survives compaction, and is released when forgotten.

Shell output sent to the model is classified and compressed by per-tool patterns (git, cargo, npm, docker, kubectl, test runners and ~80 more) that keep errors and salient lines while dropping noise, with verbatim passthrough for output that must not change and a footer saying what was cut.

f: REPL working memory survives session resume
w: Variables, imports and results in the agent's Python REPL are pickled after each response and restored when the session is resumed, so large state kept outside the context window comes back with the conversation; unpicklable values are reported as lost.

f: SQL query layer over live APIs, MCP servers and files
w: Agents query GitHub, Slack, Datadog and hundreds of other sources with one SQL statement (joins across sources, only the needed columns) instead of many paginated tool calls; sources are declarative YAML manifests mapping HTTP endpoints, pagination, auth and rate limits to tables.

f: Agent-authored mini apps with drafts and rollback
w: The agent creates, validates and (only when asked) publishes mini apps through dedicated tools; apps run in JS workers with model and agent bridges, path grants with a permission diff before changes, customization drafts with live preview, and version rollback.

f: Agent-created meta tools with dedupe and danger checks
w: Mid-task the agent can define a new reusable tool (name, description, schema, shell-template handler); the service refuses near-duplicates of existing tools by name/description overlap, rejects dangerous handlers (rm -rf /, curl | sh, reverse shells, sudo), fingerprints it and registers it for later turns.

f: LLM tool emulator (run without executing tools)
w: Agent middleware that, for chosen tools, asks a model to produce a plausible tool result instead of executing the tool, so a run can be rehearsed or tested without side effects.

f: Embeddable notification inbox with snooze and actions
w: A drop-in inbox component with tabs, read/archived status, per-notification primary/secondary action buttons, snooze to a chosen time and per-channel preferences.
Keeps a history of text copied inside the app (terminals, transcripts), memory-only unless persistence is turned on, with pinned entries and a drop-up to paste them back.

The agent renders a Mermaid diagram or opens an image in a review window; the human approves it or draws on it (circles, arrows, notes, blur, crop), and the blocking call returns structured JSON with the annotations so the agent iterates. The same tools are offered as an MCP server.

f: Installable app panes beside the agent
w: Apps from an in-workspace marketplace (or any URL plus MCP server the owner points at) open as live panes next to the chat; the agent drives the app while the owner watches or takes over, and what the owner does in the app becomes agent context.

f: Pixel office view of working agents
w: A pixel-art office where each agent sits at a desk facing its screen while working and turns toward you when it needs you, giving an at-a-glance live overview of many agents.

f: Screen cover while agents keep working
w: One hotkey covers all displays and blocks local input without sleeping or disconnecting, so agents, builds and SSH keep running while the owner is away; the cover glows when a coding agent pings that it needs attention, and Touch ID or password uncovers it.

f: Mind-map canvas with AI nodes fed by connected notes
w: Notes, web links, images, file trees and AI chat nodes sit on a zoomable canvas; an AI node uses the nodes connected to it by edges as its context, and AI nodes can be linked to each other so several agents converse on the map.

f: AG-UI generative UI with bidirectional shared agent/app state
w: A frontend framework and protocol where the running agent streams renderable UI components (generative UI), shares a typed state object two-way with the app (co-agent state), and pauses for human-in-the-loop on an action, with renderers for React, Angular and Vue - so the agent drives real app UI, not just chat.

f: Workspace rows with branch, PR status and listening ports
w: Each agent workspace row shows git branch, linked PR number/status, working folder, listening ports and the latest notification, with a blue ring when the agent needs attention.

f: Ask about whatever is on screen
w: A hotkey brings up the assistant beside the current app; it snapshots the focused or pointed-at UI element and its surroundings through the accessibility tree (length-limited) and uses that as the question's context, e.g. explain this error, summarize this page, rewrite this email draft.

f: Infinite zoomable canvas workspace with worktree territories
w: Terminals, editors, browsers and viewers are panels on a pannable/zoomable canvas with minimap, snap guides, panel links and a coloured territory per git worktree, so parallel agents stay visually separate.
Connects to VTube Studio's API to trigger the avatar's hotkeys, expressions and motions from the assistant's replies, so an existing Live2D streaming avatar acts out the conversation.

f: Gamepad and macro-pad control of agents
w: Drive the agent app with an Xbox/Switch controller or a Work Louder keypad: bindable buttons for agent actions, with keypad lighting that reflects agent state.

f: Living companion animated by real agent activity
w: A persistent particle creature whose motion is computed from the agent's actual event stream (reasoning, code edits, files, browsing, network, errors, tokens, cost), stays still when idle, shows missing telemetry as unknown, has a reduced-motion mode, and runs in the terminal, browser, desktop and phone from one engine.

f: Visual layout editor for the app shell
w: The owner opens 'Customize layout' and drags regions (rails, chat, composer, panels) around a live depiction of the window, with an inspector for position, order, style and presets, and a list of the session's changes.

f: Agent island (notch-style live activity on the desktop)
w: A macOS notch/dynamic-island overlay shows each running agent's current tool and streamed activity text, with sounds and a notification policy for when to expand.

f: Reply copilot over other chat apps (fill, never send)
w: On the phone, reads the conversation currently on screen in QQ, X or Feishu through the accessibility tree (OCR fallback), judges the other person's intent and risk, ranks three reply drafts and writes the chosen one into the input box; sending stays with the user.

f: Agent-published pages with pinned comments the agent answers
w: An agent publishes a report or HTML directory as a Page at a stable link; teammates pin comments on it (desktop or phone), and a watching agent session receives the comments, replies or resolves them and republishes at the same link.

f: Run the agent host inside a browser web worker
w: The Node-based harness and its plugins are bundled to run in a web worker: a virtual filesystem, a POSIX shell parser and interpreter, Node builtin shims and stand-ins for native packages (node-pty, ripgrep, ws, sharp) let a full session run in the browser with no server.

f: App-scoped WireGuard tunnel inside the phone app (expo-tailcat)
w: An Expo native module embeds a userspace WireGuard client so the phone app alone can reach one port on the owner's computer, with no system VPN or Tailscale app; a loopback proxy with a random capability path feeds normal fetch/WebSocket.

f: Deterministic intent router ahead of fallbacks
w: Spoken commands are matched first by a keyword intent parser (Adapt) then an example-trained matcher (Padatious) with confidence tiers, and only unmatched utterances fall through to ordered fallback handlers, so common commands answer instantly without a model call.

f: Real phone-number voice agent (PSTN calls, SMS, IVR)
w: Gives the agent a real phone number to place and receive PSTN calls and SMS, runs a telephony voice pipeline (speech-to-text, LLM, text-to-speech), navigates phone menus via DTMF/IVR, and stores call transcripts, exposed over REST and MCP.

f: Bot-free meeting capture from system audio and mic
w: Records the computer's own output audio plus the microphone during any call (no bot joins), streams it to a choice of local Whisper, Apple Speech or cloud STT with reconnect policy, silence handling and a health classifier, and serializes the meeting lifecycle into notes.
Run a voice agent against scripted callers with a fake or scripted model, assert on what it said and did, and grade with an LLM judge, without placing real calls.
After each call an LLM extracts variables and a disposition code and runs a QA analysis with per-node summaries and metrics, masking sensitive data, so call outcomes are reviewable.

f: Photoreal streaming video avatars for voice replies
w: The agent's spoken replies drive a realtime streaming video avatar (HeyGen, Anam) in a live session, so the user talks to a lifelike face instead of an audio-only voice.

Pairs Even Realities G1 glasses over BLE and uses them as a surface: stream reply text to the lenses, push notifications, notes and bitmaps, read battery, set brightness and head-up angle, and capture the glasses' microphone (LC3 audio) for voice input.

f: Live voice call that delegates slow work to background agents and keeps talking
w: A realtime speech model holds the call; anything slower than a few seconds is handed to a background bot so the voice never goes silent, and the person can interrupt, change topic or ask how a running job is going, with results announced when they land.

f: Act on each spoken clause before the user finishes
w: Speech is split into clauses as it streams and each clause is queued and executed in the frontmost app immediately ('open chrome and go to youtube and play lofi'), with a floating pill showing what was heard.

f: Dictate into any app with cleanup (hold Fn, speak, text appears)
w: Holding the Fn key anywhere on the Mac records speech, transcribes it locally or in the cloud, removes fillers and fixes grammar with a context-aware prompt (email, chat, code), and streams the cleaned text into whatever text field has focus.

f: Live auto-answer from what is heard
w: While a conversation is transcribed, a judge decides when the other person asked a question worth answering and a policy and clock pace drafts of a suggested answer shown on screen in real time.

f: Microphone noise suppression before speech recognition
w: Optional DeepFilterNet noise filtering cleans incoming audio (fans, traffic, keyboard) before VAD and speech-to-text, improving recognition in noisy rooms.

f: Spoken task progress and completion announcements
w: While the voice conversation continues, background tasks report progress and completion through an announcement manager that waits for a free window (not over the user), queues notifications and says e.g. 'It's ready', with recovery after reconnect.

f: Realtime voice providers: Qwen Omni, Doubao SeeDuplex, StepFun, MiniCPM-o
w: Speech-to-speech realtime sessions with Qwen-Omni (DashScope), Doubao SeeDuplex, StepFun and local MiniCPM-o through one provider registry, alongside Google Live and GPT live.

f: Duck other apps' audio while the assistant listens or speaks
w: When voice interaction starts, the volume of other applications is lowered (Windows audio sessions, macOS) and restored afterwards, with a null fallback where unsupported.

f: Adaptive interruption detection and false-interruption resume
w: A model watches overlapping speech to tell a real barge-in from a cough or 'uh-huh'; brief false interruptions pause rather than cancel the reply and speech resumes, protected speech can be marked uninterruptible, and tool results survive an interruption.

Run a voice agent against a contact list (CSV or synced source) with capacity limits, retries, traffic split between agent versions, a circuit breaker and recovery of stale dispatches, with live campaign stats.
The agent detects that it is talking to an automated phone menu, listens to the options and presses keypad tones (DTMF) to navigate it, and can also collect keypad input from callers.

f: Background and thinking sounds during voice turns
w: Plays ambient audio and optional 'thinking' sounds (typing, hum) while the agent is processing or running tools, so a voice call never goes dead silent.

f: Speech metrics on recorded voice calls
w: Recorded agent calls are diarized and scored for interruptions and pauses (who talked over whom, gap lengths), giving measurable turn-taking quality for a voice agent.

f: Builds its own missing tool, then loads it into itself
w: When a Trunk needs a capability it does not have, it writes the extension (tool, command or guard) as TypeScript, runs that extension's tests, shows the owner what it does and asks once, then hot-loads it without restarting and keeps it for next time; risky extensions run inside the safety layer like any other tool.

f: Drive every installed agent CLI on the owner's own subscription (Grok Build, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity)
w: Branch detects agent CLIs the owner has installed and signed into (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity) and runs Trunks through them, so each paid subscription becomes a worker through its own official login; one adapter registry, per-adapter status, usage and failure handling.

f: Show it once: record a workflow by demonstration and replay it as a routine
w: The owner says 'watch me' and does a task on the computer; Branch records the steps (apps, clicks, typed fields, pages), turns them into a named routine with plain-language steps, asks about anything ambiguous, takes corrections, and can run it on a schedule or on request; any step that sends, buys, deletes or signs in still asks.
